   439	def _rewrite_command(args: argparse.Namespace, root: Path) -> int:
   440	    index = build_label_index(root)
   441	    files = collect_input_files(root, args.paths, args.files_from)
   442	    changes: list[tuple[Path, str, str]] = []
   443	    unresolved: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []
   444	    for path in files:
   445	        old = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
   446	        new, missing = rewrite_text(old, index)
   447	        if old != new:
   448	            changes.append((path, old, new))
   449	        unresolved.extend((path, locator) for locator in missing)

   451	    for path, locator in unresolved:
   452	        rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
   453	        print(f"unresolved: {rel_path}: {locator}", file=sys.stderr)
   454	    if unresolved and not args.allow_unresolved:
   455	        print("refusing partial rewrite; pass --allow-unresolved to rewrite safe matches",
   456	              file=sys.stderr)
   457	        return 1
   458	
   459	    if args.write:
   460	        for path, _old, new in changes:
   461	            path.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8")
   462	    else:
   463	        for path, old, new in changes:
   464	            rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()

   466	                old.splitlines(keepends=True),
   467	                new.splitlines(keepends=True),

   469	                tofile=rel_path,

   477	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   478	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
   479	    parser.add_argument(
   480	        "--root",
   481	        type=Path,
   482	        default=Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent,
   483	        help="repository root (default: parent of scripts/)",
   484	    )
   485	    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
   486	
   487	    resolve = subparsers.add_parser("resolve", help="resolve labels to current spans")
   488	    resolve.add_argument("labels", nargs="*", help="blueprint labels to resolve")
   489	    resolve.add_argument("--path", dest="paths", action="append", default=[],
   490	                         help="scan a repository file or directory for label tokens")
   491	    resolve.add_argument("--files-from", type=Path,
   492	                         help="scan repository paths listed one per line")
   493	    resolve.add_argument("--format", choices=("markdown", "plain", "json"),
   494	                         default="plain")
   495	
   496	    rewrite = subparsers.add_parser("rewrite", help="replace unambiguous legacy locators")
   497	    rewrite.add_argument("paths", nargs="*", help="repository files or directories to rewrite")
   498	    rewrite.add_argument("--files-from", type=Path,
   499	                         help="rewrite repository paths listed one per line")
   500	    rewrite.add_argument("--write", action="store_true",
   501	                         help="write changes in place (default: print a diff)")
   502	    rewrite.add_argument("--allow-unresolved", action="store_true",
   503	                         help="rewrite safe matches while reporting unresolved locators")
   504	
   505	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
   506	    root = args.root.resolve()
   507	    try:
   508	        if args.command == "resolve":
   509	            return _resolve_command(args, root)
   510	        return _rewrite_command(args, root)
   511	    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:

1	# Protocol — model-backed PR review
     2	
     3	Normative for `local/bin/review.sh`.  Read `local/protocols/meta.md` first: it
     4	governs how this document changes and what must be recorded when it does.
     5	
     6	Replaces `.github/workflows/pr-review.yml` — the `gate`, `code-review` and
     7	`prose-review` jobs — together with the review half of the `@claude` /
     8	`@codex` mention system documented in `docs/pr_review_management.md`.  The
     9	substantive review criteria are unchanged: `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` §5 and the
    10	prompt pair under `.github/prompts/` are the same texts the GitHub jobs used.
    11	What changed is only who runs them and where the verdict lands.
    12	
    13	    local/bin/review.sh <pr-id> [--force-review] [--dry-run]
    14	
    15	---
    16	
    17	## 1. Why the reviewer is chained to CI
    18	
    19	The parent workflow's own header records the reason (`pr-review.yml:3-8`):
    20	the predecessors `claude-code-review.yml` and `blueprint-prose-review.yml`
    21	fired on every push, so a pull request whose build was about to fail still
    22	drew two full reviews per push — and the auto-fix loop then rewrote the very
    23	code under review.  Chaining the review to CI completion spends review effort
    24	only on code that at least compiles.
    25	
    26	Locally the chain is: `ci.sh` publishes the `local-ci/*` statuses on the head
    27	SHA; `review.sh` refuses to do anything until the `local-ci/summary` roll-up is
    28	`success` for the **current** head.  There is no event bus, so the chain is an
    29	ordering discipline rather than a trigger, and the discipline is enforced by the
    30	gate below rather than by trust.
    31	
    32	Marking a draft ready is not a trigger there and is not one here.  A review
    33	follows a CI run, and only a CI run.
    34	
    35	## 2. The gate
    36	
    37	The gate is a ladder.  Each rung either passes, skips (exit 0, no verdict), or
    38	**blocks** (exit 3, publishing nothing at all — the *absence* of a green
    39	`local-review/summary` is the block).  The distinction between skip and
    40	block is the whole point of the rung: `pr-review.yml:59-61` fails the job with
    41	"PR CI concluded X; PR Review must not report success without a review", a
    42	fail-instead-of-skip semantics that exists because a skipped review once read
    43	as a green one.
    44	
    45	| # | Rung | Outcome when it fires |
    46	|---|---|---|
    47	| 1 | `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` is the literal string `false` | skip, exit 0 |
    48	| 2 | no open GitHub PR for the number, or no head SHA | error, exit 1 |
    49	| 3 | branch name contains `] ~ ^ : ? *`, space or backslash | error, exit 1 |
    50	| 4 | branch under review equals `MIPSTARRE_TRUSTED_REF` | error, exit 1 |
    51	| 5 | `local-ci/summary` is missing on the head SHA, or is not `success` | **block**, exit 3 |
    52	| 6 | the local branch tip ≠ the remote PR head | error, exit 1 |
    53	| 7 | head commit subject matches `^\[(claude\|codex)-(auto\|review)-fix\]` | skip, exit 0, unless `--force-review` |
    54	| 8 | a fix lock is held for this branch | skip, exit 0 |
    55	| 9 | the head moved while this run queued for the review lock | skip, exit 0 |
    56	| 10 | the diff against the merge base is empty | skip, exit 0 |
    57	
    58	Rung 1 is `vars.CLAUDE_REVIEW_ENABLED` (`pr-review.yml:44-48`).  **Only the
    59	literal string `false` disables it**; unset, empty, `"0"`, `"no"` and `"False"`
    60	all leave the reviewer enabled.  This is DESIGN.md invariant 4, and it is not a
    61	stylistic preference: a port that treats unset as false silently stops
    62	reviewing and reports nothing.
    63	
    64	Rung 7 is the ping-pong guard, and §5 explains it.
    65	
    66	Rung 5 reads exactly one status, the `local-ci/summary` roll-up `ci.sh` posts
    67	last; it never iterates the per-step contexts.  Per-step completeness is the
    68	merge gate's job (`pr_merge.py` gate 3 blocks on any missing `local-ci/<step>`),
    69	and it costs this gate nothing: a partial `--only` / `--skip-build` run posts
    70	nothing to GitHub at all, so a subset can never green-light a review either.
    71	
    72	## 3. Trusted prompts
    73	
    74	The reviewer persona and task prompt are read with
    75	
    76	    git show "$MIPSTARRE_TRUSTED_REF:.github/prompts/<file>"
    77	
    78	never from the checkout under review.  On GitHub this was a second
    79	`actions/checkout` of the default branch into `.trusted-actions/`
    80	(`pr-review.yml:140-146`), with every prompt path prefixed by that directory
    81	(`pr-review.yml:173-182`, `:248-252`).  The property being preserved is that a
    82	pull request cannot edit the instructions given to its own reviewer.  A branch
    83	that *is* the trusted ref is refused outright (rung 4), because for such a
    84	branch the property is unsatisfiable.
    85	
    86	`MIPSTARRE_TRUSTED_REF` defaults to `main`.  Repointing it at anything a
    87	contributor can push to defeats the guard; if you must, record why in
    88	`results/telemetry/events.md`.
    89	
    90	Two prompt pairs are used, verbatim:
    91	
    92	| Review | Persona | Task |
    93	|---|---|---|
    94	| code | `claude-code-review-system-prompt.md` | `claude-code-review-prompt.md` |
    95	| prose | `blueprint-prose-review-system-prompt.md` | `blueprint-prose-review-prompt.md` |
    96	
    97	To each, `review.sh` appends a **local execution contract** — the only text it
    98	adds — which states that `gh`, `git push` and `mcp__github__*` do not exist,
    99	that the working tree is read-only, where the diff and the checkout are, and
   100	what the output must look like (§6).  The contract is authoritative where it
   101	conflicts with the trusted prompt, because the trusted prompt still describes
   102	GitHub surfaces that are absent here.
   103	
   104	## 4. Untrusted data
   105	
   106	The diff is the material under review, which makes it the most likely carrier
   107	of an injection attempt.  It is passed as an attachment, not as instructions:
   108	
   109	* control characters are stripped, ` ``` ` and `~~~` are broken, and the patch
   110	  is truncated to `MIPSTARRE_DIFF_MAX_LINES` (default 4000);
   111	* it is fenced in an explicit untrusted block with a do-not-obey frame;
   112	* the head commit subject, which also comes from the branch, is stripped of
   113	  control characters and of `<<<` / `>>>` before it is quoted into context.
   114	
   115	When `dispatch.sh` is present it applies its own framing and truncation on top
   220	"not reviewed" rather than as a pass.
   221	
   222	## 8. Concurrency
   223	
   224	| Lock | Key | Cancellation |
   225	|---|---|---|
   226	| review | PR id | none — a queued run waits, then re-checks the head |
   227	| fix (`autofix.md`) | branch | supersession sentinel |
   228	
   229	The split of keys is inherited (`pr-review.yml:18-20` groups by PR number with
   230	`cancel-in-progress: false`; `auto-fix.yml:259-261` groups by head branch with
   231	`cancel-in-progress: true`) and it matters: cancelling a review wastes the
   232	tokens already spent and produces nothing, whereas cancelling a superseded fix
   233	saves a write to a branch that has already moved.
   234	
   235	Locks are directories under `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/` holding the
   236	holder's pid — `flock(1)` does not exist on macOS.  A lock whose holder is gone
   237	is reclaimed.  After acquiring the review lock, `review.sh` re-reads the local
   238	tip and the remote PR head: a fix commit that landed while this run queued
   239	invalidates the review, and the run exits without a verdict rather than
   240	describing a commit that is no longer head.  The same check runs again after
   241	the agent returns; a head that moved during the review makes the result stale
   242	and forbids publication, leaving the raw output in the runtime cache.
   243	
   244	`review.sh` also refuses to start while a fix lock is held for the branch.
   245	The two tools share one worktree here, where GitHub gave each job a fresh
   246	checkout; without this cross-check the reviewer would read a tree being
   247	rewritten under it.
   248	
   249	## 9. The findings ledger
   250	
   251	`docs/pr_review_management.md` records the audit failure this replaces:
   252	review feedback lived on three separate GitHub surfaces — inline
   253	`pulls/N/comments`, issue-level `issues/N/comments`, and review summaries
   254	`pulls/N/reviews` — and PRs were merged with comments nobody had read.  The
   255	GraphQL `reviewThreads` `isResolved` / `isOutdated` pair was the only reliable
   256	status signal; the REST `line` field lied.
   257	
   258	Locally there is **one** surface.  Every finding lives on one line of the
   259	`## Findings` section of the exact-head `COMMENT` review body, between
   260	`<!-- findings:begin -->` and `<!-- findings:end -->`:
   261	
   262	    - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Basic.lean:120` — adds a non-paper hypothesis
   263	
   264	| Box | Meaning | Blocks merge |
   265	|---|---|---|
   266	| `[ ]` | unresolved | **yes** |
   267	| `[x]` | resolved — a human or an agent addressed it and says so | no |
   268	| `[-]` | outdated — the cited lines were rewritten since the reviewed SHA | no |
   269	
   270	`[ ]` → `[x]` is a human judgement, or a claim by the fixer that a human is
   340	`[codex-review-fix]` prefixes, because a human-directed commit must be
   341	reviewable and those prefixes make the reviewer skip.  The script warns if the
   342	session used one anyway.
   343	
   344	The auto-create-PR step of `claude.yml` becomes a printed instruction rather
   345	than an action: when a session on an issue branch produces commits, `agent.sh`
   346	tells the operator to open the PR with `local/bin/pr_open.py`, which pushes the
   347	branch and owns the branch-name lint (`local/protocols/issues-prs.md`).
   348	
   349	## 11. Operating it
   350	
   351	    local/bin/review.sh 7                # review PR 0007 at its current head
   352	    local/bin/review.sh 7 --dry-run      # build diff and prompts, dispatch nothing
   353	    LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED=false local/bin/review.sh 7    # confirm the kill switch
   354	
   355	Exit codes: `0` reviewed or intentionally skipped · `1` usage/environment ·
   356	`3` gate blocked (CI not green for this head) · `4` no parseable verdict.
   357	Code 3 publishes nothing at all — the missing green `local-review/summary` is
   358	the block.  Only code 4 publishes a `failure` `local-review/summary`, and
   359	neither publishes a review.
   360	
   361	Artefacts:
   362	
   363	| Path | Committed | Contents |
   364	|---|---|---|
   365	| the exact-head `COMMENT` review on the PR | on GitHub | combined verdict, ledger, prose |
   366	| `local-review/summary` on the head SHA | on GitHub | the gate-readable verdict |
   367	| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/` | no | diff, prompts, raw agent output |
   368	| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/blueprint-citations.md` | no | bounded, sanitized label-derived blueprint spans |
   369	| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/blueprint-citations.raw.md` | no | complete resolver output retained locally |
   370	| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/review-<pr>.lock` | no | the review lock |
   371	
   372	Every codex invocation goes through `local/bin/dispatch.sh` when it exists, so
   373	the session is named, captured to `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl` and
   374	summarised into `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`
   375	(`local/protocols/sessions.md`).  Without the dispatcher, `review.sh` falls
   376	back to a direct `codex exec` and says loudly that the session will not appear
   377	in the registry — an untracked session is lost research data, so the fallback
   378	is a degradation, not an alternative.  `dispatch.sh` enforces
   379	`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` for reviewer-role sessions independently; the two checks
   380	agreeing is intentional redundancy.
   381	
   382	Missing pieces degrade with a message, never silently: missing CI statuses
   383	block, no `worktree-setup.sh` warns about a cold build cache, no codex CLI is a
   384	hard error.  A GitHub failure is fatal — a verdict that cannot be published is
   385	not a verdict.
   386	
   387	## 12. Deliberately not ported
   388	
   389	Untouched-code or new-mechanism findings are "out of scope -> issue #N".

set -euo pipefail

PROG="review.sh"
BIN_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
SELF_ROOT="$(cd "$BIN_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
ROOT="$SELF_ROOT"
# Worktrees are administered from the PRIMARY checkout: when this script runs
# from a linked worktree copy, re-point the git root at the primary (same
# resolution as cache-warmer.sh resolve_primary_repo; EVOLUTION.md 2026-08-30).
# Git operations AND the telemetry ledger copy follow the re-point (telemetry
# is single-instance in the primary, like builds.jsonl); gh_common.py ships
# beside this script and needs no re-point.
_common="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null || true)"
case "$_common" in
  */.git) ROOT="$(dirname "$_common")" ;;
esac
unset _common
if [ "$ROOT" != "$SELF_ROOT" ] && [ "${MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_REEXEC:-0}" != 1 ] &&
   [ -x "$ROOT/local/bin/review.sh" ]; then
  MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_REEXEC=1 exec "$ROOT/local/bin/review.sh" "$@"
fi

# The one GitHub layer (gh_common.py:6-8); it ships beside this script.
GH_COMMON="$BIN_DIR/gh_common.py"
if grep -q '^blueprint/' "$RUN_DIR/files.txt"; then TOUCHES_BLUEPRINT=1; fi

WORKTREE="$(resolve_worktree "$BRANCH")"
# The reviewer also reads worktree FILES, not just the diff: dirty bytes could
# hide or fabricate findings for a verdict bound to the clean head (PR 7, F2).
REVIEW_DIRTY="$(git -C "$WORKTREE" status --porcelain)"
[ -z "$REVIEW_DIRTY" ] ||
  die "worktree $WORKTREE is dirty; commit or stash before reviewing PR #$PR_NUM:
$REVIEW_DIRTY"
[ -d "$WORKTREE" ] || die "worktree resolution failed for branch $BRANCH"

# Stored blueprint citations are labels; their numeric source spans are derived
# for the reviewer from the current worktree.  The helper executable is read
# from the trusted primary checkout, while the branch files it parses remain
# untrusted review data (review.md section 4).
BLUEPRINT_CITATION_MAP_RAW="$RUN_DIR/blueprint-citations.raw.md"
BLUEPRINT_CITATION_MAP="$RUN_DIR/blueprint-citations.md"
TRUSTED_HELPER_DIR="$RUN_DIR/trusted-blueprint-citations"
mkdir -p "$TRUSTED_HELPER_DIR"
fetch_trusted "$BLUEPRINT_CITATION_PATH" \
  "$TRUSTED_HELPER_DIR/blueprint_citations.py"
fetch_trusted "scripts/tex_utils.py" "$TRUSTED_HELPER_DIR/tex_utils.py"
CITATION_RC=0
PYTHONPATH="$TRUSTED_HELPER_DIR" python3 \
  "$TRUSTED_HELPER_DIR/blueprint_citations.py" --root "$WORKTREE" resolve \
  --files-from "$RUN_DIR/files.txt" --format markdown \
  >"$BLUEPRINT_CITATION_MAP_RAW" || CITATION_RC=$?
case "$CITATION_RC" in
  0) ;;
  1)
    warn "one or more blueprint labels did not resolve uniquely; the generated map records them"
    ;;
  *)
    die "blueprint citation resolver failed with status $CITATION_RC;" \
      "refusing review without citation evidence"
    ;;
esac
sanitize_to "$BLUEPRINT_CITATION_MAP_RAW" "$BLUEPRINT_CITATION_MAP" \
  0 "$CITATION_MAX_BYTES"

   234	
   235	Two asymmetric channels reach the model, and confusing them is how agent
   236	systems get exploited.
   237	
   238	**Persona (trusted).** A repo-relative `--persona` path — including an
   239	absolute path that resolves inside the repository — is read with
   240	`git show <ref>:<path>`, default ref `main`, never from the working tree. A
   241	branch under review can therefore not rewrite the persona of the session
   242	reviewing it (`DESIGN.md` invariant 5; the parent repository checked prompts

   245	trusted ref does not resolve — as in a repository with no commits yet —

   249	characters, have their code fences and our own envelope markers broken so the

     1	# Protocol: issues and pull requests
     2	
     3	Normative for the GitHub-backed issue and PR lifecycle and the automation in
     4	`local/bin/`; read `local/protocols/meta.md` first. The repository is
     5	`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`, and GitHub is the **single source of truth** for
     6	issues, PRs, CI and review evidence, and merges; CI and reviews still *execute*
     7	here and publish their results there. No active `issues/` or `prs/` tree, no
     8	shadow record, no write-through cache, no offline mutation mode: a GitHub error
     9	fails the operation, never a local success (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-01).
    10	
    11	## 1. Records, names, tools
    12	
    13	Issues and PRs are GitHub's, identified by their numbers — no zero-padded ids,
    14	no frontmatter. Parent/child structure is the native sub-issue relation
    15	(`POST …/issues/{parent}/sub_issues`), one parent per issue exactly as the
    16	retired `parent:` scalar allowed; discussion is comments; labels come from the
    17	repository (`list-labels`, paginated), so `local/labels.yml` is retired and a
    18	label absent from GitHub is reported, never invented. Briefs (the design record
    19	per issue) live in `local/briefs/`: agent input, not lifecycle state.
    20	
    21	Prerequisites between issues are **GitHub issue dependencies**
    22	(`GET`/`POST …/issues/{n}/dependencies/blocked_by`), one edge per prerequisite.
    23	The edge is retained even when the prerequisite closes, so reopening it restores the block.
    24	A prerequisite carried by a pull request is the packet issue that PR closes. The
    25	"Dependencies" bullets in an issue body are commentary on those edges, never
    26	the record. A packet is **ready** when it is an open leaf of the tracker tree
    27	and every issue blocking it is closed; `local/bin/ready_packets.py` computes
    28	that list, and the operator launches lanes from it rather than from a
    29	hand-kept order or a dependency table in a comment (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-04).
    30	Establish or adopt each edge with
    31	`local/bin/gh_common.py add-blocked-by ISSUE PREREQUISITE`. The command first
    32	reads the edge, makes at most one mutation, and re-reads after an ambiguous
    33	failure; it is therefore safe to repeat. Record closed prerequisites too.
    34	
    35	Every GitHub call goes through `local/bin/gh_common.py` — a module for Python
    36	callers, and for the shell scripts a CLI (`pr-view`, `post-status`,
    37	`latest-statuses`, `ensure-pr-comment`, `post-review`, `merge-pr`,
    38	`issue-create`, `add-blocked-by`, `issue-close`, `snapshot`, …; `--help` lists
    39	them) owning CLI discovery, repository resolution, API version headers,
    40	bounded retry of transient failures and the exit-2-with-stderr convention.
    41	Nothing else shells out to `gh`. `issue_new.py`, `issue_close.py`, `pr_open.py`,
    42	`ci.sh`, `review.sh`, `autofix.sh`, `pr_merge.py`, `github-sync.sh` take GitHub
    43	numbers; `track.py`, `validate_tree.py` and `export_issues.py` are deleted.
    44	
    45	* Branches: `issue-<github-number>-<slug>`, or `codex/issue-<number>-<slug>`
    46	  from an agent; `pr_open.py` rejects what `git check-ref-format` would.
    47	* Titles, slugs and branch names are **bracket-free**: bot-generated branch
    48	  names inherit those characters and "`]` breaks part of the PR automation
    49	  stack" (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124). A `:` in a *title* is fine
    50	  (`Tracking: …`), but not in a branch.
    51	* `autofix.sh`'s automated fix commits keep the exact subject prefixes
    52	  `[codex-auto-fix]` and `[codex-review-fix]`; its iteration counter and the
    53	  review skip key on them.  Operator and worker repairs use plain
    54	  `fix(review): …` / `fix(ci): …` subjects so the reviewer sees them.
    55	* `Closes #N` / `Fixes #N` auto-closes the issue on merge, `Addresses #N` does
    56	  not (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:61-62) — and the numbers being GitHub's, that
    57	  footer is now literally what GitHub itself reads.
    58	
    59	## 2. Evidence contracts
    60	
    61	All evidence binds to the **exact head SHA** (DESIGN.md invariant 2).
    62	
    63	**Commit statuses.** Ten canonical contexts, posted by `post-status`: one
    64	`local-ci/<step>` per CI step (`build`, `blueprint-render`, `paper-gaps`,
    65	`blueprint-sync`, `file-length`, `proof-debt`, `proof-evasion`,
    66	`statement-origin`), plus `local-ci/summary` and `local-review/summary`.
    67	`ci.sh` posts `pending` before each gate step and `success | failure | error`
    68	after it; a gated-out step is a `success` saying it was skipped. The gate reads
    69	the *latest* status per context (`latest-statuses`), never GitHub's combined
    70	status, silent as that is about contexts never posted. The run manifest is one
    71	PR comment marked `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, kept current by
    72	`ensure-pr-comment`: evidence for humans, while the statuses are the gate.
    73	
    74	**Review verdict.** One `COMMENT` review per head SHA, bound to `commit_id`,
    75	carrying `<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`, the findings ledger, and the
    76	line `VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED (code=…, prose=…)`.
    77	Unchecked findings are ledger lines matching `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`; clean means
    78	`APPROVED`, or `COMMENTED` with none of them. Adverse verdicts post as `COMMENT`
    79	too — a **single account** cannot approve its own pull request, so the review
    80	event carries no authority — and adverseness travels in `local-review/summary`
    81	(`failure` for unresolved findings), which is the gate's review evidence.
    82	
    83	**Adjudication** (review.md §12) is a PR comment whose body starts with
    84	`ADJUDICATION` and contains `head=<SHA>` for the current head, one disposition
    85	line per remaining finding; `--adjudicated` takes nothing else.
    86	
    87	**Idempotency.** Every publishing step is **at most one mutation**: a paginated
    88	read finds the stable marker first and adopts that record instead of duplicating
    89	it (`commentOnce`, issue-automation.yml:403-417, now guarding retries rather than
    90	webhook redelivery); an ambiguous write stays pending for adoption.

1	# Local operations — operator guide
     2	
     3	This directory is the operative workflow of the repository: the local
     4	replacement for the parent project's GitHub Actions layer. Architecture and
     5	invariants: [`DESIGN.md`](DESIGN.md). Protocol changes: follow
     6	[`protocols/meta.md`](protocols/meta.md).
     7	
     8	## The lifecycle at a glance
     9	
    10	```
    11	issue  →  branch + worktree  →  agent session(s)  →  local CI  →  review
    12	  →  (auto-fix loop)  →  merge gate  →  main  →  cache warmer refresh
    13	```
    14	
    15	1. **File an issue**: `local/bin/issue_new.py --title "..." --body-file b.md --label ...` opens
    16	   a GitHub issue and prints its number; `--parent N` attaches it as a native
    17	   sub-issue. Record each prerequisite, including one already closed, with
    18	   `local/bin/gh_common.py add-blocked-by ISSUE PREREQUISITE`; the command is
    19	   safe to repeat. The brief for the issue goes in `local/briefs/`.
    20	2. **Open a PR**: create branch `issue-<number>-slug`, worktree under
    21	   `.worktrees/`, run `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` there, then
    22	   `local/bin/pr_open.py --branch issue-<number>-slug --title "..." --body-file pr.md --issue N` (the body follows the PR template in `local/protocols/issues-prs.md`),
    23	   which pushes the branch and opens the GitHub PR.
    24	3. **Dispatch agents**: only via `local/bin/dispatch.sh --role prover
    25	   --issue NNNN --worktree .worktrees/<name> -- "task"`. Session telemetry
    26	   lands in `results/telemetry/`.
    27	4. **CI**: `local/bin/ci.sh PPPP` (build via hot cache + audits + blueprint
    28	   checks) → per-step `local-ci/*` statuses and the manifest PR comment.
    29	5. **Review**: `local/bin/review.sh PPPP` — runs only after green CI; publishes
    30	   one exact-head COMMENT review plus the `local-review/summary` status.
    31	6. **Auto-fix** (optional, the repository's auto-fix label on the PR):
    32	   `local/bin/autofix.sh PPPP --mode auto`, capped, serialized.
    33	7. **Merge**: `local/bin/pr_merge.py PPPP` — the gate; refuses on red CI,
    34	   missing review, or unresolved findings, and merges via GitHub with the
    35	   exact-SHA guard. Then pokes the cache warmer.
    36	8. **Housekeeping / site**: `local/bin/housekeeping.sh all`,
    37	   `local/bin/site.sh all`.
    38	
    39	**Choosing the next packet.** `local/bin/ready_packets.py` walks the packet tree
    40	under the Stage 4.3 tracker #47 — chapter trackers, their packets, and nested
    41	chains such as Magic Square rigidity — and prints the open leaf packets whose
    42	GitHub issue dependencies (`blocked_by`) are all closed. `--all` adds the
    43	blocked packets with their open blockers, `--json` feeds the lane launcher, and
    44	`--root N` restricts the walk to one tracker. Prerequisites live in those edges
    45	only: the "Dependencies" bullets in a packet body are commentary
    46	(`protocols/issues-prs.md` §1). A merged packet closes its issue and therefore
    47	unblocks its dependents with no edit anywhere.
    48	
    49	## Ground rules for agents
    50	
    51	- Read `AGENTS.md` first; the faithfulness policy and proof-integrity
    52	  blockers are unchanged from the parent project.
    53	- Never run `lake update`. Never write to the hot cache. Full `lake build`
    54	  goes through the machine-wide lock (`warm-worktree.sh`/`ci.sh` handle it).
    55	- One session never reviews its own diff.
    56	- Sessions are dispatched, resumed, and archived only via `dispatch.sh`.
    57	- Invoke workflow tools through the primary checkout's path
    58	  (`/…/MIPStarRE-dev/local/bin/…`), never through a worktree's copy — a
    59	  branch's copy can predate protocol fixes (EVOLUTION.md, 2026-08-30).
    60	- Friction with any protocol → log it in `results/telemetry/events.md`;
    61	  propose amendments per `protocols/meta.md`.
    35	local/briefs/          # per-issue design briefs (committed)
    36	results/telemetry/     # sessions/stages/builds logs, GitHub snapshot (committed)
    37	```
    38	
    39	Runtime state that must never be committed lives in `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/`
    40	(hot cache, snapshots, locks, served site) and `.worktrees/` (gitignored).
    41	
    42	## GitHub → local mapping
    43	
    44	| GitHub mechanism | Local replacement |
    45	|---|---|
    46	| PR CI (`pr-ci.yml`) on push/PR events | `local/bin/ci.sh <pr-id>` run by the PR lifecycle scripts |
    47	| Main-build actions cache (main-only save, PR restore) | Hot main cache: single-writer warmer + read-only snapshots + APFS copy-on-write clones per worktree (`build-cache.md`) |
    48	| `lake exe cache get` (Mathlib cloud cache) | Unchanged — already local |
    49	| Model-backed PR review chained on CI success | `local/bin/review.sh <pr-number>`: codex CLI with the same `.github/prompts/` review personas, invoked only from green exact-head CI statuses; one COMMENT review plus `local-review/summary` |
    50	| Auto-fix workflows (CI-fix, blueprint-fix, review-fix) | `local/bin/autofix.sh <pr-id> --mode {ci,blueprint,review,auto}` with the same commit-prefix guards and a combined iteration cap |
    51	| `@claude`/`@codex` mention responders | `local/bin/agent.sh <id> "instruction"` — human-invoked codex session on the branch worktree |
    52	| GitHub issues + sub-issues + labels | unchanged — GitHub is the record again (`issues-prs.md`); `issue_new.py` / `issue_close.py` drive it through `gh_common.py` |
    53	| GitHub PRs | GitHub PRs, branch-per-issue, merge gate in `pr_merge.py` (REST merge with the exact-SHA guard) |
    54	| Issue automation (classify/scout/track/followups) | `local/bin/` Python ports; LLM steps optional behind `MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED` |
    55	| Housekeeping crons (standup, stale audit, linter sweep, README freshness) | `local/bin/housekeeping.sh <job>` on demand |
    56	| Badges + Pages site (blueprint/docs/badges components) | `local/bin/site.sh` → component store + assembled site in `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/site/` |
    57	| Codex cloud env setup (`.codex/setup.sh`) | `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` per worktree |
    58	| Reviewer/bot identity via tokens | codex CLI sessions; `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` registry |
    59	
    60	## Core invariants (inherited from the parent workflow's post-mortems)
    61	
    62	These encode incidents the parent repo paid for; violating them re-introduces
    63	documented failure modes. Sources are cited in `local/protocols/*.md`.
    64	
    65	1. **Single cache writer.** Only the warmer writes the hot main cache; agent
    66	   worktrees consume copy-on-write clones and never write back. (GitHub's
    67	   per-PR cache saves evicted the main entry: pr-ci.yml:138-142.)
    68	2. **Review only after green CI, on the same head SHA.** The gate reads the
    69	   exact-head `local-ci/*` statuses; a failed or absent CI summary blocks the
    70	   review, which then publishes nothing at all — the *absence* of a green
    71	   `local-review/summary` is the block, never a silent skip. Bot commits with prefix
    72	   `[codex-auto-fix]`/`[codex-review-fix]` are not re-reviewed except the final
    73	   fix at the iteration cap, which gets one forced review.
    74	3. **Serialized fixes.** ci-fix → blueprint-fix → review-fix strictly in order,
    75	   one branch at a time; combined iteration cap (default 5) across all fix
   130	  kind (warm, rebuild, cache-get), duration, outcome, trigger.
   131	- `results/telemetry/events.md` — dated free-form incident log (what broke,
   132	  diagnosis, fix); the raw feed for `protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.
   133	- `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md` — dated protocol amendments: cause (cite an
   134	  `events.md` entry or telemetry), the change, expected effect. This file is
   135	  the primary record of workflow self-evolution.
   136	
   137	## Model policy
   138	
   139	- codex CLI (`gpt-5.6-sol`, ultra effort) drives orchestrator/prover/reviewer/
   140	  simplifier sessions (`codex exec`, `codex exec review`).
   141	- Claude-side subagents: easy/mechanical tasks run on Opus-tier; Fable-tier is
   142	  reserved for hard reasoning (proof strategy, protocol synthesis, adversarial
   143	  verification).
   144	- Reviewer and prover roles must be **different sessions** — a session never
   145	  reviews its own diff.

     9	# The directly indexed low-degree game
    10	
    11	The low-degree game used by the Pauli-basis combining argument is needed in
    12	dimension `2 * m + 2`.  The existing conditionally linear game represents a
    13	coordinate index by an equally sized fiber in the scalar field and therefore
    14	requires the dimension to divide the field size.  This file gives the separate
    15	directly indexed variant which samples that index directly.
    16	
    17	The geometric line carrier records the sampled coordinate, and line evaluation
    18	uses an `Option` outcome rather than assigning a value when a point does not
    19	determine one.  The game retains the point, axis-line, and diagonal-line answer
    20	formats and the nine ordered type branches of the original low-degree game.
    21	
    22	The `Transport` modules relate the direct game to the seed-indexed game and to
    23	the mature low individual degree test interface: `Transport.Correspondence`
    24	identifies coordinates, answers, and the question law of the two QPBT
    25	presentations; `Transport.SeedFiber` dilates a seed-indexed strategy to a
    26	direct strategy by a correlated residue register, and `Transport.SeedFiberValue`
    27	shows that the dilation preserves the value exactly; `Transport.Questions`
    28	reads mature lines as canonical direct questions and rebases direct answers;
    29	`Transport.Strategy` reads one coordinate of a projective direct strategy as a
    30	mature `ProjStrat`, with exact Born-weight formulas for both adapters; and
    31	`Transport.BranchComparison`, `Transport.DiagonalRecursion`, and
    32	`Transport.PassConversion` convert a value bound of the direct game into the
    33	pass hypothesis of the mature low individual degree theorem for every
    34	coordinate strategy.  `GameValue` supplies the rejection calculus relating the
    35	direct value to the mature branch weights.  `Transport.Error` carries the
    36	scalar half of the transport: the auxiliary sampling parameter with which
    37	the mature theorem is applied, bounds on the three terms of its error
    38	function, and the absorption of the resulting simultaneous-measurement
    39	estimate into the error function of `lem:ld-soundness`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Regression tests for ``scripts/blueprint_citations.py``."""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import io
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

SCRIPT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(SCRIPT_DIR))

from blueprint_citations import (  # noqa: E402
    LabelLocation,
    build_label_index,
    collect_input_files,
    find_citation_uses,
    main,
    rewrite_text,
)


def _write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")


class BlueprintCitationTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        holder = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(holder.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(holder.name)
        self.chapter = self.root / "blueprint" / "src" / "chapter"
        _write(
            self.chapter / "ch12_example.tex",
            """\\section{Example}\\label{sec:example}

\\begin{lemma}[Alpha]\\label{lem:alpha}
  Alpha statement.
\\end{lemma}
\\begin{proof}
  Alpha proof.
\\end{proof}

% \\label{lem:commented-out}
\\begin{definition}
  \\label{def:beta}
  Beta definition.
\\end{definition}
""",
        )

    def test_index_resolves_statement_and_following_proof(self) -> None:
        index = build_label_index(self.root)

        self.assertEqual(index["lem:alpha"][0].locator,
                         "blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:3-8")
        self.assertEqual(index["def:beta"][0].locator,
                         "blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:11-14")
        self.assertEqual(index["sec:example"][0].locator,
                         "blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:1")
        self.assertNotIn("lem:commented-out", index)

    def test_duplicate_labels_remain_visible_to_resolver(self) -> None:
        _write(
            self.chapter / "ch13_duplicate.tex",
            "\\begin{lemma}\\label{lem:alpha}Duplicate.\\end{lemma}\n",
        )

        index = build_label_index(self.root)

        self.assertEqual(len(index["lem:alpha"]), 2)

    def test_scan_finds_known_tokens_and_unknown_blueprint_labels(self) -> None:
        lean = self.root / "MIPStarRE" / "Example.lean"
        _write(
            lean,
            "/-- See blueprint `lem:alpha`, `def:missing`, and bare "
            "`rem:missing`; ignore Lean name `Example.value`. -/\n",
        )
        index = build_label_index(self.root)

        uses, unknown = find_citation_uses([lean], self.root, index)

        self.assertEqual([(use.label, use.line) for use in uses], [("lem:alpha", 1)])
        self.assertEqual(
            [(use.label, use.line) for use in unknown],
            [("def:missing", 1), ("rem:missing", 1)],
        )

    def test_rewrite_uses_label_named_in_same_docstring(self) -> None:
        text = (
            "/-- Lean support for `lem:alpha`, blueprint "
            "`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:20-26`. -/\n"
        )

        rewritten, unresolved = rewrite_text(text, build_label_index(self.root))

        self.assertEqual(unresolved, [])
        self.assertEqual(rewritten, "/-- Lean support for blueprint `lem:alpha`. -/\n")

    def test_rewrite_prefers_an_exact_node_to_a_nearby_label(self) -> None:
        text = (
            "/-- Lean support for `lem:alpha`, blueprint "
            "`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:11-14`. -/\n"
        )

        rewritten, unresolved = rewrite_text(text, build_label_index(self.root))

        self.assertEqual(unresolved, [])
        self.assertEqual(
            rewritten,
            "/-- Lean support for `lem:alpha`, blueprint `def:beta`. -/\n",
        )

    def test_rewrite_can_use_an_exact_current_span(self) -> None:
        text = "/-- See `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:11-14`. -/\n"

        rewritten, unresolved = rewrite_text(text, build_label_index(self.root))

        self.assertEqual(unresolved, [])
        self.assertEqual(rewritten, "/-- See `def:beta`. -/\n")

    def test_rewrite_accepts_a_single_line_locator(self) -> None:
        text = "/-- See `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:1`. -/\n"

        rewritten, unresolved = rewrite_text(text, build_label_index(self.root))

        self.assertEqual(unresolved, [])
        self.assertEqual(rewritten, "/-- See `sec:example`. -/\n")

    def test_rewrite_collapses_duplicate_parenthetical_label(self) -> None:
        text = (
            "/-- The source is `lem:alpha` "
            "(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:20-26`). -/\n"
        )

        rewritten, unresolved = rewrite_text(text, build_label_index(self.root))

        self.assertEqual(unresolved, [])
        self.assertEqual(rewritten, "/-- The source is blueprint `lem:alpha`. -/\n")

    def test_rewrite_refuses_an_unanchored_stale_locator(self) -> None:
        text = "/-- See `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:80-90`. -/\n"

        rewritten, unresolved = rewrite_text(text, build_label_index(self.root))

        self.assertEqual(rewritten, text)
        self.assertEqual(
            unresolved,
            ["`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:80-90`"],
        )

    def test_rewrite_refuses_containment_in_a_current_span(self) -> None:
        text = "/-- See `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:4-6`. -/\n"

        rewritten, unresolved = rewrite_text(text, build_label_index(self.root))

        self.assertEqual(rewritten, text)
        self.assertEqual(
            unresolved,
            ["`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:4-6`"],
        )

    def test_rewrite_does_not_guess_from_decoding_docstring_proximity(self) -> None:
        index = {
            "lem:qld-decoder-linearity": [LabelLocation(
                "lem:qld-decoder-linearity", "blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_analysis.tex",
                30, 30, 46,
            )],
            "lem:qld-construct-the-paulis": [LabelLocation(
                "lem:qld-construct-the-paulis", "blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_analysis.tex",
                193, 193, 261,
            )],
        }
        text = (
            "/-- This is blueprint `lem:qld-decoder-linearity`, used in the symmetry "
            "step at blueprint `ch16_qpbt_analysis.tex:239-244`. -/\n"
        )

        rewritten, unresolved = rewrite_text(text, index)

        self.assertIn("`ch16_qpbt_analysis.tex:239-244`", rewritten)
        self.assertEqual(rewritten.count("`lem:qld-decoder-linearity`"), 1)
        self.assertEqual(unresolved, ["`ch16_qpbt_analysis.tex:239-244`"])

    def test_rewrite_uses_exact_given_strategy_support_node(self) -> None:
        index = {
            "lem:symmetric-strat": [LabelLocation(
                "lem:symmetric-strat", "blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex",
                116, 116, 134,
            )],
            "lem:symmetric-strat-given-strategy": [LabelLocation(
                "lem:symmetric-strat-given-strategy",
                "blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex", 140, 140, 154,
            )],
        }
        text = (
            "/-- Formalization-only form of `lem:symmetric-strat`; blueprint "
            "`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:140-154`. -/\n"
        )

        rewritten, unresolved = rewrite_text(text, index)

        self.assertEqual(unresolved, [])
        self.assertEqual(
            rewritten,
            "/-- Formalization-only form of `lem:symmetric-strat`; blueprint\n"
            "`lem:symmetric-strat-given-strategy`. -/\n",
        )

    def test_rewrite_wraps_long_blueprint_citation_lines_idempotently(self) -> None:
        text = (
            "/-- The source-facing nodes are blueprint `def:one`, blueprint `def:two`, "
            "blueprint `lem:three`, and blueprint `def:a-very-long-fourth-label`. -/\n"
        )

        rewritten, unresolved = rewrite_text(text, {})
        second, second_unresolved = rewrite_text(rewritten, {})

        self.assertEqual(unresolved, [])
        self.assertEqual(second_unresolved, [])
        self.assertEqual(second, rewritten)
        self.assertTrue(all(len(line) <= 100 for line in rewritten.splitlines()))

    def test_resolve_scan_fails_for_bare_and_list_unknown_labels(self) -> None:
        lean = self.root / "MIPStarRE" / "Example.lean"
        _write(
            lean,
            "/-- Blueprint `lem:alpha`, `def:missing`; bare `rem:missing`. -/\n",
        )
        stdout = io.StringIO()

        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(stdout):
            result = main([
                "--root", str(self.root), "resolve", "--path",
                "MIPStarRE/Example.lean", "--format", "plain",
            ])

        self.assertEqual(result, 1)
        self.assertIn("def:missing\tUNRESOLVED", stdout.getvalue())
        self.assertIn("rem:missing\tUNRESOLVED", stdout.getvalue())

    def test_rewrite_refuses_proximity_with_multiple_labels(self) -> None:
        text = (
            "/-- Compare `lem:alpha` with `def:beta`. The first source is "
            "`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:80-90`; the second is "
            "`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:91-100`. -/\n"
        )

        rewritten, unresolved = rewrite_text(text, build_label_index(self.root))

        self.assertEqual(
            rewritten,
            "/-- Compare `lem:alpha` with `def:beta`. The first source is\n"
            "`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:80-90`; the second is\n"
            "`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:91-100`. -/\n",
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            unresolved,
            [
                "`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:80-90`",
                "`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:91-100`",
            ],
        )

            "/-- See `lem:alpha` "

            "blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:91-100`. -/\n"

                "--root", str(self.root), "resolve", "lem:alpha", "--format", "plain"

            stdout.getvalue(),

        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(stdout):

            ])

        self.assertEqual(result, 1)
        self.assertEqual(stdout.getvalue(), "lem:missing\tUNRESOLVED\n")

    def test_rewrite_cli_refuses_partial_writes_without_opt_in(self) -> None:
        lean = self.root / "MIPStarRE" / "Example.lean"
        original = (
            "/-- See `lem:alpha`, blueprint "
            "`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:80-90`. -/\n"
            "/-- See `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_example.tex:91-100`. -/\n"
        )
        _write(lean, original)
        stderr = io.StringIO()

        with contextlib.redirect_stderr(stderr):
            refused = main([
                "--root", str(self.root), "rewrite", "MIPStarRE/Example.lean", "--write"

def _format_resolutions(
    labels: list[str],
    origins: dict[str, list[CitationUse]],
    index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]],
    output_format: str,
) -> tuple[str, bool]:
    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    failed = False
    for label in labels:
        locations = index.get(label, [])
        if len(locations) != 1:
            failed = True
        rows.append({
            "label": label,
            "locations": [location.locator for location in locations],
            "cited_at": [f"{use.path}:{use.line}" for use in origins.get(label, [])],
        })

    if output_format == "json":
        return json.dumps(rows, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", failed

    if output_format == "plain":
        rendered = []
        for row in rows:
            locations = row["locations"]
            value = ", ".join(locations) if locations else "UNRESOLVED"
            rendered.append(f"{row['label']}\t{value}")
        return "\n".join(rendered) + ("\n" if rendered else ""), failed

    rendered = [
        "# Resolved blueprint citations",
        "",
        "Numeric spans below are derived from durable labels; they are not stored citations.",
        "",
    ]
    if not rows:
        rendered.append("_No blueprint labels were found in the selected files._")
    for row in rows:
        locations = row["locations"]
        location_text = ", ".join(f"`{item}`" for item in locations) or "**UNRESOLVED**"
        origin_text = row["cited_at"]
        suffix = ""
        if origin_text:
            suffix = "; cited at " + ", ".join(f"`{item}`" for item in origin_text)
        rendered.append(f"- `{row['label']}` -> {location_text}{suffix}")
    return "\n".join(rendered) + "\n", failed


def _comment_bounds(text: str, position: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
    start = text.rfind("/-", 0, position)
    end = text.find("-/", position)
    if start >= 0 and end >= 0:
        return start, end + 2
    line_start = text.rfind("\n", 0, position) + 1
    line_end = text.find("\n", position)
    return line_start, len(text) if line_end < 0 else line_end


def _candidate_for_locator(
    text: str,
    match: re.Match[str],
    index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]],
) -> str | None:
    # One label cannot faithfully replace a locator that deliberately names
    # several disjoint spans. Such citations require a manual label list.
    if match.group("extra"):
        return None

    target_name = Path(match.group("path")).name
    old_start = int(match.group("start"))
    old_end = int(match.group("end") or match.group("start"))
    exact = [
        label
        for label, locations in index.items()
        if len(locations) == 1
        and Path(locations[0].path).name == target_name
        and (locations[0].start, locations[0].end) == (old_start, old_end)
    ]
    if exact:
        return exact[0] if len(exact) == 1 else None

    block_start, block_end = _comment_bounds(text, match.start())
    block = text[block_start:block_end]
    candidates: dict[str, list[re.Match[str]]] = {}
    for label_match in CODE_LABEL_RE.finditer(block):
        label = label_match.group("label")
        locations = index.get(label, [])
        if len(locations) != 1 or Path(locations[0].path).name != target_name:
            continue
        candidates.setdefault(label, []).append(label_match)

    if candidates:
        linked: set[str] = set()
        relative_start = match.start() - block_start
        relative_end = match.end() - block_start
        for label, label_matches in candidates.items():
            for label_match in label_matches:
                if label_match.end() <= relative_start:
                    between = block[label_match.end():relative_start]
                    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*\(\s*|\s*[,;]\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+", between):
                        linked.add(label)
                elif label_match.start() >= relative_end:
                    between = block[relative_end:label_match.start()]
                    after = block[label_match.end():]
                    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*\(\s*", between) and re.match(r"\s*\)", after):
                        linked.add(label)
        return next(iter(linked)) if len(linked) == 1 else None

    return None


def _wrap_blueprint_citation_lines(text: str) -> str:
    """Wrap generated blueprint-citation prose at the Lean line limit."""

    wrapped: list[str] = []
    for raw_line in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
        ending = "\n" if raw_line.endswith("\n") else ""
        line = raw_line[:-1] if ending else raw_line
        if (len(line) <= LEAN_LINE_WIDTH
                or not re.search(r"\b[Bb]lueprint\b", line)
                or CODE_LABEL_RE.search(line) is None):
            wrapped.append(raw_line)
            continue
        indent = line[:len(line) - len(line.lstrip())]
        current = line
        while len(current) > LEAN_LINE_WIDTH:
            split_at = current.rfind(" ", len(indent) + 1, LEAN_LINE_WIDTH + 1)
            if split_at < 0:
                break
            wrapped.append(current[:split_at].rstrip() + "\n")
            current = indent + current[split_at + 1:].lstrip()
        wrapped.append(current + ending)
    return "".join(wrapped)


def rewrite_text(
    text: str, index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]]
) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
    """Rewrite unambiguous legacy locators and return unresolved locator text."""

    replacements: list[tuple[int, int, str]] = []
    unresolved: list[str] = []
    for match in LEGACY_LOCATOR_RE.finditer(text):
        label = _candidate_for_locator(text, match, index)
        if label is None:
            unresolved.append(match.group(0))
            continue
        replacements.append((match.start(), match.end(), f"`{label}`"))

    rewritten = text
    for start, end, replacement in reversed(replacements):
        rewritten = rewritten[:start] + replacement + rewritten[end:]

    # Collapse the common legacy wording after the locator itself is replaced.
    def collapse_duplicate(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
        link = match.group("link")
        label = match.group("label")
        if "\n" not in link:
            return f"blueprint `{label}`"
        indent_match = re.search(r"\n(?P<indent>[ \t]*)", link)
        indent = indent_match.group("indent") if indent_match else ""
        return f"blueprint\n{indent}`{label}`"

    rewritten = re.sub(
        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`"
        r"(?P<link>,\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+|;\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+|\s+in\s+)"
        r"`(?P=label)`",
        collapse_duplicate,
        rewritten,
    )
    rewritten = re.sub(
        r"(?P<prefix>\b[Bb]lueprint\s+)"
        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`\s*[,;]\s*`(?P=label)`",
        lambda match: f"{match.group('prefix')}`{match.group('label')}`",
        rewritten,
    )
    def collapse_parenthetical(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
        label = match.group("label")
        whitespace = match.group("whitespace")
        if "\n" not in whitespace:
            return f"blueprint `{label}`"
        indent_match = re.search(r"\n(?P<indent>[ \t]*)", whitespace)
        indent = indent_match.group("indent") if indent_match else ""
        return f"blueprint\n{indent}`{label}`"

    rewritten = re.sub(
        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`\s*"
        r"(?P<whitespace>\(\s*)`(?P=label)`\s*\)",
        collapse_parenthetical,
        rewritten,
    )
    return _wrap_blueprint_citation_lines(rewritten), unresolved


def _resolve_command(args: argparse.Namespace, root: Path) -> int:
    index = build_label_index(root)
    files = collect_input_files(root, args.paths, args.files_from)
    uses, unknown = find_citation_uses(files, root, index)
    labels = list(args.labels)
    origins: dict[str, list[CitationUse]] = {}
    for use in uses:
        if use.label not in labels:
            labels.append(use.label)
        origins.setdefault(use.label, []).append(use)
    for use in unknown:
        if use.label not in labels:
            labels.append(use.label)
        origins.setdefault(use.label, []).append(use)
    rendered, failed = _format_resolutions(labels, origins, index, args.format)
    sys.stdout.write(rendered)
    return 1 if failed else 0


def _rewrite_command(args: argparse.Namespace, root: Path) -> int:
    index = build_label_index(root)
    files = collect_input_files(root, args.paths, args.files_from)
    changes: list[tuple[Path, str, str]] = []
    unresolved: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []
    for path in files:
        old = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        new, missing = rewrite_text(old, index)
        if old != new:
            changes.append((path, old, new))
        unresolved.extend((path, locator) for locator in missing)

    for path, locator in unresolved:
        rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
        print(f"unresolved: {rel_path}: {locator}", file=sys.stderr)
    if unresolved and not args.allow_unresolved:
        print("refusing partial rewrite; pass --allow-unresolved to rewrite safe matches",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    if args.write:
        for path, _old, new in changes:
            path.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8")
    else:
        for path, old, new in changes:
            rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
            sys.stdout.writelines(difflib.unified_diff(
                old.splitlines(keepends=True),
                new.splitlines(keepends=True),
                fromfile=rel_path,
                tofile=rel_path,
            ))
    action = "rewrote" if args.write else "would rewrite"
    print(f"{action} {len(changes)} file(s); {len(unresolved)} unresolved locator(s)",
          file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--root",
        type=Path,
        default=Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent,
        help="repository root (default: parent of scripts/)",
    )
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    resolve = subparsers.add_parser("resolve", help="resolve labels to current spans")
    resolve.add_argument("labels", nargs="*", help="blueprint labels to resolve")
    resolve.add_argument("--path", dest="paths", action="append", default=[],
                         help="scan a repository file or directory for label tokens")
    resolve.add_argument("--files-from", type=Path,
                         help="scan repository paths listed one per line")
    resolve.add_argument("--format", choices=("markdown", "plain", "json"),
                         default="plain")

    rewrite = subparsers.add_parser("rewrite", help="replace unambiguous legacy locators")
    rewrite.add_argument("paths", nargs="*", help="repository files or directories to rewrite")
    rewrite.add_argument("--files-from", type=Path,
                         help="rewrite repository paths listed one per line")
    rewrite.add_argument("--write", action="store_true",
                         help="write changes in place (default: print a diff)")
    rewrite.add_argument("--allow-unresolved", action="store_true",
                         help="rewrite safe matches while reporting unresolved locators")

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    root = args.root.resolve()
    try:
        if args.command == "resolve":
            return _resolve_command(args, root)
        return _rewrite_command(args, root)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

            # nearby added lines in hunk +/- 12
            for q in chunk.splitlines()[max(0,i-5):min(len(chunk.splitlines()),i+6)]:
                if q.startswith('+') and not q.startswith('+++'):
                    print(' NEW',q)
