+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Resolve durable blueprint labels and migrate legacy numeric locators.
+
+Lean docstrings should store blueprint labels, not line ranges.  This helper
+derives the current source span of each label from ``blueprint/src/chapter``.
+It can also conservatively rewrite old ``chNN_*.tex:START-END`` citations when
+the span exactly identifies a node or the surrounding syntax pairs it with one
+unambiguous label from that chapter.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import difflib
+import json
+import re
+import sys
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from tex_utils import strip_tex_comment
+
+
+TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"\\(?P<kind>begin|end|label)\{(?P<value>[^}]+)\}")
+CODE_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`")
+CANONICAL_CITATION_RE = re.compile(
+    r"\b[Bb]lueprint(?:\s+(?:node|nodes|label|labels|entry|entries))?\s+"
+    r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`"
+)
+LEGACY_LOCATOR_RE = re.compile(
+    r"`(?P<path>(?:blueprint/src/chapter/)?ch[0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*\.tex):"
+    r"(?P<start>[0-9]+)(?:(?P<dash>--|-|\u2013|\u2014)(?P<end>[0-9]+))?"
+    r"(?P<extra>(?:,[0-9]+(?:--|-|\u2013|\u2014)[0-9]+)*)`"
+)
+STATEMENT_ENVS = {
+    "definition",
+    "theorem",
+    "lemma",
+    "proposition",
+    "corollary",
+    "remark",
+    "example",
+}
+LEAN_LINE_WIDTH = 100
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class EnvironmentSpan:
+    """One balanced TeX environment."""
+
+    name: str
+    start: int
+    end: int
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class LabelLocation:
+    """The current source span anchored by one active ``\\label``."""
+
+    label: str
+    path: str
+    label_line: int
+    start: int
+    end: int
+
+    @property
+    def locator(self) -> str:
+        suffix = str(self.start) if self.start == self.end else f"{self.start}-{self.end}"
+        return f"{self.path}:{suffix}"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class CitationUse:
+    """A label token found in a file that a reviewer will inspect."""
+
+    label: str
+    path: str
+    line: int
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _OpenEnvironment:
+    name: str
+    start: int
+
+
+def _active_lines(path: Path) -> list[str]:
+    return [strip_tex_comment(line) for line in path.read_text(
+        encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"
+    ).splitlines()]
+
+
+def _parse_tex_file(path: Path, root: Path) -> list[LabelLocation]:
+    """Return active labels in *path*, with enclosing statement/proof spans."""
+
+    lines = _active_lines(path)
+    stack: list[_OpenEnvironment] = []
+    environments: list[EnvironmentSpan] = []
+    labels: list[tuple[str, int]] = []
+
+    for line_no, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
+        for token in TOKEN_RE.finditer(line):
+            kind = token.group("kind")
+            value = token.group("value")
+            if kind == "begin":
+                stack.append(_OpenEnvironment(value, line_no))
+            elif kind == "label":
+                labels.append((value, line_no))
+            else:
+                match_at = next(
+                    (index for index in range(len(stack) - 1, -1, -1)
+                     if stack[index].name == value),
+                    None,
+                )
+                if match_at is None:
+                    continue
+                opened = stack[match_at]
+                del stack[match_at:]
+                environments.append(EnvironmentSpan(value, opened.start, line_no))
+
+    environments.sort(key=lambda span: (span.start, span.end - span.start))
+    proof_spans = [span for span in environments if span.name == "proof"]
+    rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+    locations: list[LabelLocation] = []
+
+    for label, label_line in labels:
+        enclosing = [
+            span for span in environments
+            if span.start <= label_line <= span.end
+        ]
+        if enclosing:
+            span = min(enclosing, key=lambda item: (item.end - item.start, -item.start))
+            start, end = span.start, span.end
+            if span.name in STATEMENT_ENVS:
+                following = next(
+                    (proof for proof in proof_spans if proof.start > span.end),
+                    None,
+                )
+                if following is not None:
+                    gap = lines[span.end:following.start - 1]
+                    if all(not item.strip() for item in gap):
+                        end = following.end
+        else:
+            start = end = label_line
+        locations.append(LabelLocation(label, rel_path, label_line, start, end))
+
+    return locations
+
+
+def build_label_index(root: Path) -> dict[str, list[LabelLocation]]:
+    """Index active blueprint labels below ``root/blueprint/src/chapter``."""
+
+    chapter_root = root / "blueprint" / "src" / "chapter"
+    if not chapter_root.is_dir():
+        raise ValueError(f"blueprint chapter directory does not exist: {chapter_root}")
+    index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]] = {}
+    for path in sorted(chapter_root.rglob("*.tex")):
+        for location in _parse_tex_file(path, root):
+            index.setdefault(location.label, []).append(location)
+    return index
+
+
+def _inside_root(path: Path, root: Path) -> bool:
+    try:
+        path.relative_to(root)
+    except ValueError:
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def collect_input_files(root: Path, paths: list[str], files_from: Path | None) -> list[Path]:
+    """Resolve explicit repository paths without permitting traversal."""
+
+    raw_paths = list(paths)
+    if files_from is not None:
+        raw_paths.extend(
+            line.strip() for line in files_from.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
+            if line.strip()
+        )
+
+    files: set[Path] = set()
+    for raw_path in raw_paths:
+        candidate = Path(raw_path)
+        if not candidate.is_absolute():
+            candidate = root / candidate
+        candidate = candidate.resolve(strict=False)
+        if not _inside_root(candidate, root):
+            raise ValueError(f"input path escapes repository root: {raw_path}")
+        if candidate.is_dir():
+            files.update(path for path in candidate.rglob("*") if path.is_file())
+        elif candidate.is_file():
+            files.add(candidate)
+        # Deleted paths from a changed-file list are intentionally ignored.
+    return sorted(files)
+
+
+def find_citation_uses(
+    files: list[Path], root: Path, index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]]
+) -> tuple[list[CitationUse], list[CitationUse]]:
+    """Find resolvable label tokens and unknown blueprint-label tokens."""
+
+    uses: set[CitationUse] = set()
+    unknown: set[CitationUse] = set()
+    for path in files:
+        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
+        rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+        for match in CODE_LABEL_RE.finditer(text):
+            label = match.group("label")
+            if label in index:
+                uses.add(CitationUse(label, rel_path, text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1))
+            elif ":" in label:
+                unknown.add(
+                    CitationUse(label, rel_path, text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1)
+                )
+        for match in CANONICAL_CITATION_RE.finditer(text):
+            label = match.group("label")
+            if label not in index:
+                unknown.add(
+                    CitationUse(label, rel_path, text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1)
+                )
+    return sorted(uses, key=lambda use: (use.label, use.path, use.line)), sorted(
+        unknown, key=lambda use: (use.label, use.path, use.line)
+    )
+
+
+def _format_resolutions(
+    labels: list[str],
+    origins: dict[str, list[CitationUse]],
+    index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]],
+    output_format: str,
+) -> tuple[str, bool]:
+    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
+    failed = False
+    for label in labels:
+        locations = index.get(label, [])
+        if len(locations) != 1:
+            failed = True
+        rows.append({
+            "label": label,
+            "locations": [location.locator for location in locations],
+            "cited_at": [f"{use.path}:{use.line}" for use in origins.get(label, [])],
+        })
+
+    if output_format == "json":
+        return json.dumps(rows, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", failed
+
+    if output_format == "plain":
+        rendered = []
+        for row in rows:
+            locations = row["locations"]
+            value = ", ".join(locations) if locations else "UNRESOLVED"
+            rendered.append(f"{row['label']}\t{value}")
+        return "\n".join(rendered) + ("\n" if rendered else ""), failed
+
+    rendered = [
+        "# Resolved blueprint citations",
+        "",
+        "Numeric spans below are derived from durable labels; they are not stored citations.",
+        "",
+    ]
+    if not rows:
+        rendered.append("_No blueprint labels were found in the selected files._")
+    for row in rows:
+        locations = row["locations"]
+        location_text = ", ".join(f"`{item}`" for item in locations) or "**UNRESOLVED**"
+        origin_text = row["cited_at"]
+        suffix = ""
+        if origin_text:
+            suffix = "; cited at " + ", ".join(f"`{item}`" for item in origin_text)
+        rendered.append(f"- `{row['label']}` -> {location_text}{suffix}")
+    return "\n".join(rendered) + "\n", failed
+
+
+def _comment_bounds(text: str, position: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    start = text.rfind("/-", 0, position)
+    end = text.find("-/", position)
+    if start >= 0 and end >= 0:
+        return start, end + 2
+    line_start = text.rfind("\n", 0, position) + 1
+    line_end = text.find("\n", position)
+    return line_start, len(text) if line_end < 0 else line_end
+
+
+def _candidate_for_locator(
+    text: str,
+    match: re.Match[str],
+    index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]],
+) -> str | None:
+    # One label cannot faithfully replace a locator that deliberately names
+    # several disjoint spans. Such citations require a manual label list.
+    if match.group("extra"):
+        return None
+
+    target_name = Path(match.group("path")).name
+    old_start = int(match.group("start"))
+    old_end = int(match.group("end") or match.group("start"))
+    exact = [
+        label
+        for label, locations in index.items()
+        if len(locations) == 1
+        and Path(locations[0].path).name == target_name
+        and (locations[0].start, locations[0].end) == (old_start, old_end)
+    ]
+    if exact:
+        return exact[0] if len(exact) == 1 else None
+
+    block_start, block_end = _comment_bounds(text, match.start())
+    block = text[block_start:block_end]
+    candidates: dict[str, list[re.Match[str]]] = {}
+    for label_match in CODE_LABEL_RE.finditer(block):
+        label = label_match.group("label")
+        locations = index.get(label, [])
+        if len(locations) != 1 or Path(locations[0].path).name != target_name:
+            continue
+        candidates.setdefault(label, []).append(label_match)
+
+    if candidates:
+        linked: set[str] = set()
+        relative_start = match.start() - block_start
+        relative_end = match.end() - block_start
+        for label, label_matches in candidates.items():
+            for label_match in label_matches:
+                if label_match.end() <= relative_start:
+                    between = block[label_match.end():relative_start]
+                    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*\(\s*|\s*[,;]\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+", between):
+                        linked.add(label)
+                elif label_match.start() >= relative_end:
+                    between = block[relative_end:label_match.start()]
+                    after = block[label_match.end():]
+                    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*\(\s*", between) and re.match(r"\s*\)", after):
+                        linked.add(label)
+        return next(iter(linked)) if len(linked) == 1 else None
+
+    return None
+
+
+def _wrap_blueprint_citation_lines(text: str) -> str:
+    """Wrap generated blueprint-citation prose at the Lean line limit."""
+
+    wrapped: list[str] = []
+    for raw_line in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
+        ending = "\n" if raw_line.endswith("\n") else ""
+        line = raw_line[:-1] if ending else raw_line
+        if (len(line) <= LEAN_LINE_WIDTH
+                or not re.search(r"\b[Bb]lueprint\b", line)
+                or CODE_LABEL_RE.search(line) is None):
+            wrapped.append(raw_line)
+            continue
+        indent = line[:len(line) - len(line.lstrip())]
+        current = line
+        while len(current) > LEAN_LINE_WIDTH:
+            split_at = current.rfind(" ", len(indent) + 1, LEAN_LINE_WIDTH + 1)
+            if split_at < 0:
+                break
+            wrapped.append(current[:split_at].rstrip() + "\n")
+            current = indent + current[split_at + 1:].lstrip()
+        wrapped.append(current + ending)
+    return "".join(wrapped)
+
+
+def rewrite_text(
+    text: str, index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]]
+) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
+    """Rewrite unambiguous legacy locators and return unresolved locator text."""
+
+    replacements: list[tuple[int, int, str]] = []
+    unresolved: list[str] = []
+    for match in LEGACY_LOCATOR_RE.finditer(text):
+        label = _candidate_for_locator(text, match, index)
+        if label is None:
+            unresolved.append(match.group(0))
+            continue
+        replacements.append((match.start(), match.end(), f"`{label}`"))
+
+    rewritten = text
+    for start, end, replacement in reversed(replacements):
+        rewritten = rewritten[:start] + replacement + rewritten[end:]
+
+    # Collapse the common legacy wording after the locator itself is replaced.
+    def collapse_duplicate(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
+        link = match.group("link")
+        label = match.group("label")
+        if "\n" not in link:
+            return f"blueprint `{label}`"
+        indent_match = re.search(r"\n(?P<indent>[ \t]*)", link)
+        indent = indent_match.group("indent") if indent_match else ""
+        return f"blueprint\n{indent}`{label}`"
+
+    rewritten = re.sub(
+        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`"
+        r"(?P<link>,\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+|;\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+|\s+in\s+)"
+        r"`(?P=label)`",
+        collapse_duplicate,
+        rewritten,
+    )
+    rewritten = re.sub(
+        r"(?P<prefix>\b[Bb]lueprint\s+)"
+        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`\s*[,;]\s*`(?P=label)`",
+        lambda match: f"{match.group('prefix')}`{match.group('label')}`",
+        rewritten,
+    )
+    def collapse_parenthetical(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
+        label = match.group("label")
+        whitespace = match.group("whitespace")
+        if "\n" not in whitespace:
+            return f"blueprint `{label}`"
+        indent_match = re.search(r"\n(?P<indent>[ \t]*)", whitespace)
+        indent = indent_match.group("indent") if indent_match else ""
+        return f"blueprint\n{indent}`{label}`"
+
+    rewritten = re.sub(
+        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`\s*"
+        r"(?P<whitespace>\(\s*)`(?P=label)`\s*\)",
+        collapse_parenthetical,
+        rewritten,
+    )
+    return _wrap_blueprint_citation_lines(rewritten), unresolved
+
+
+def _resolve_command(args: argparse.Namespace, root: Path) -> int:
+    index = build_label_index(root)
+    files = collect_input_files(root, args.paths, args.files_from)
+    uses, unknown = find_citation_uses(files, root, index)
+    labels = list(args.labels)
+    origins: dict[str, list[CitationUse]] = {}
+    for use in uses:
+        if use.label not in labels:
+            labels.append(use.label)
+        origins.setdefault(use.label, []).append(use)
+    for use in unknown:
+        if use.label not in labels:
+            labels.append(use.label)
+        origins.setdefault(use.label, []).append(use)
+    rendered, failed = _format_resolutions(labels, origins, index, args.format)
+    sys.stdout.write(rendered)
+    return 1 if failed else 0
+
+
+def _rewrite_command(args: argparse.Namespace, root: Path) -> int:
+    index = build_label_index(root)
+    files = collect_input_files(root, args.paths, args.files_from)
+    changes: list[tuple[Path, str, str]] = []
+    unresolved: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []
+    for path in files:
+        old = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
+        new, missing = rewrite_text(old, index)
+        if old != new:
+            changes.append((path, old, new))
+        unresolved.extend((path, locator) for locator in missing)
+
+    for path, locator in unresolved:
+        rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+        print(f"unresolved: {rel_path}: {locator}", file=sys.stderr)
+    if unresolved and not args.allow_unresolved:
+        print("refusing partial rewrite; pass --allow-unresolved to rewrite safe matches",
+              file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+
+    if args.write:
+        for path, _old, new in changes:
+            path.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8")
+    else:
+        for path, old, new in changes:
+            rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+            sys.stdout.writelines(difflib.unified_diff(
+                old.splitlines(keepends=True),
+                new.splitlines(keepends=True),
+                fromfile=rel_path,
+                tofile=rel_path,
+            ))
+    action = "rewrote" if args.write else "would rewrite"
+    print(f"{action} {len(changes)} file(s); {len(unresolved)} unresolved locator(s)",
+          file=sys.stderr)
+    return 0
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--root",
+        type=Path,
+        default=Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent,
+        help="repository root (default: parent of scripts/)",
+    )
+    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
+
+    resolve = subparsers.add_parser("resolve", help="resolve labels to current spans")
+    resolve.add_argument("labels", nargs="*", help="blueprint labels to resolve")
+    resolve.add_argument("--path", dest="paths", action="append", default=[],
+                         help="scan a repository file or directory for label tokens")
+    resolve.add_argument("--files-from", type=Path,
+                         help="scan repository paths listed one per line")
+    resolve.add_argument("--format", choices=("markdown", "plain", "json"),
+                         default="plain")
+
+    rewrite = subparsers.add_parser("rewrite", help="replace unambiguous legacy locators")
+    rewrite.add_argument("paths", nargs="*", help="repository files or directories to rewrite")
+    rewrite.add_argument("--files-from", type=Path,
+                         help="rewrite repository paths listed one per line")
+    rewrite.add_argument("--write", action="store_true",
+                         help="write changes in place (default: print a diff)")
+    rewrite.add_argument("--allow-unresolved", action="store_true",
+                         help="rewrite safe matches while reporting unresolved locators")
+
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    root = args.root.resolve()
+    try:
+        if args.command == "resolve":
+            return _resolve_command(args, root)
+        return _rewrite_command(args, root)
+    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
+        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

    15	The classical low individual degree game is a two-player game based on the low individual degree variant of the multilinearity test of Babai, Fortnow, and Lund. In the basic version, one player (the ``points player'') receives a uniformly random point $u \in \F_q^m$ and answers with a value $a \in \F_q$, while the other player (the ``lines player'') receives a random line through $u$ --- either axis-parallel or diagonal --- and answers with a univariate polynomial describing the restriction of a global function to that line. If the players share a polynomial $g\colon \F_q^m \to \F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$ and answer with $g(u)$ and with the restriction $g|_\ell$, they win with probability $1$; the soundness theorem below states that the converse approximately holds. In the simultaneous version, the players' answers are $k$-tuples, checked coordinatewise against a $k$-tuple of low individual degree polynomials.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Resolve durable blueprint labels and migrate legacy numeric locators.
+
+Lean docstrings should store blueprint labels, not line ranges.  This helper
+derives the current source span of each label from ``blueprint/src/chapter``.
+It can also conservatively rewrite old ``chNN_*.tex:START-END`` citations when
+the span exactly identifies a node or the surrounding syntax pairs it with one
+unambiguous label from that chapter.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import difflib
+import json
+import re
+import sys
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from tex_utils import strip_tex_comment
+
+
+TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"\\(?P<kind>begin|end|label)\{(?P<value>[^}]+)\}")
+CODE_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`")
+CANONICAL_CITATION_RE = re.compile(
+    r"\b[Bb]lueprint(?:\s+(?:node|nodes|label|labels|entry|entries))?\s+"
+    r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`"
+)
+LEGACY_LOCATOR_RE = re.compile(
+    r"`(?P<path>(?:blueprint/src/chapter/)?ch[0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*\.tex):"
+    r"(?P<start>[0-9]+)(?:(?P<dash>--|-|\u2013|\u2014)(?P<end>[0-9]+))?"
+    r"(?P<extra>(?:,[0-9]+(?:--|-|\u2013|\u2014)[0-9]+)*)`"
+)
+STATEMENT_ENVS = {
+    "definition",
+    "theorem",
+    "lemma",
+    "proposition",
+    "corollary",
+    "remark",
+    "example",
+}
+LEAN_LINE_WIDTH = 100
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class EnvironmentSpan:
+    """One balanced TeX environment."""
+
+    name: str
+    start: int
+    end: int
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class LabelLocation:
+    """The current source span anchored by one active ``\\label``."""
+
+    label: str
+    path: str
+    label_line: int
+    start: int
+    end: int
+
+    @property
+    def locator(self) -> str:
+        suffix = str(self.start) if self.start == self.end else f"{self.start}-{self.end}"
+        return f"{self.path}:{suffix}"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class CitationUse:
+    """A label token found in a file that a reviewer will inspect."""
+
+    label: str
+    path: str
+    line: int
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _OpenEnvironment:
+    name: str
+    start: int
+
+
+def _active_lines(path: Path) -> list[str]:
+    return [strip_tex_comment(line) for line in path.read_text(
+        encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"
+    ).splitlines()]
+
+
+def _parse_tex_file(path: Path, root: Path) -> list[LabelLocation]:
+    """Return active labels in *path*, with enclosing statement/proof spans."""
+
+    lines = _active_lines(path)
+    stack: list[_OpenEnvironment] = []
+    environments: list[EnvironmentSpan] = []
+    labels: list[tuple[str, int]] = []
+
+    for line_no, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
+        for token in TOKEN_RE.finditer(line):
+            kind = token.group("kind")
+            value = token.group("value")
+            if kind == "begin":
+                stack.append(_OpenEnvironment(value, line_no))
+            elif kind == "label":
+                labels.append((value, line_no))
+            else:
+                match_at = next(
+                    (index for index in range(len(stack) - 1, -1, -1)
+                     if stack[index].name == value),
+                    None,
+                )
+                if match_at is None:
+                    continue
+                opened = stack[match_at]
+                del stack[match_at:]
+                environments.append(EnvironmentSpan(value, opened.start, line_no))
+
+    environments.sort(key=lambda span: (span.start, span.end - span.start))
+    proof_spans = [span for span in environments if span.name == "proof"]
+    rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+    locations: list[LabelLocation] = []
+
+    for label, label_line in labels:
+        enclosing = [
+            span for span in environments
+            if span.start <= label_line <= span.end
+        ]
+        if enclosing:
+            span = min(enclosing, key=lambda item: (item.end - item.start, -item.start))
+            start, end = span.start, span.end
+            if span.name in STATEMENT_ENVS:
+                following = next(
+                    (proof for proof in proof_spans if proof.start > span.end),
+                    None,
+                )
+                if following is not None:
+                    gap = lines[span.end:following.start - 1]
+                    if all(not item.strip() for item in gap):
+                        end = following.end
+        else:
+            start = end = label_line
+        locations.append(LabelLocation(label, rel_path, label_line, start, end))
+
+    return locations
+
+
+def build_label_index(root: Path) -> dict[str, list[LabelLocation]]:
+    """Index active blueprint labels below ``root/blueprint/src/chapter``."""
+
+    chapter_root = root / "blueprint" / "src" / "chapter"
+    if not chapter_root.is_dir():
+        raise ValueError(f"blueprint chapter directory does not exist: {chapter_root}")
+    index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]] = {}
+    for path in sorted(chapter_root.rglob("*.tex")):
+        for location in _parse_tex_file(path, root):
+            index.setdefault(location.label, []).append(location)
+    return index
+
+
+def _inside_root(path: Path, root: Path) -> bool:
+    try:
+        path.relative_to(root)
+    except ValueError:
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def collect_input_files(root: Path, paths: list[str], files_from: Path | None) -> list[Path]:
+    """Resolve explicit repository paths without permitting traversal."""
+
+    raw_paths = list(paths)
+    if files_from is not None:
+        raw_paths.extend(
+            line.strip() for line in files_from.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
+            if line.strip()
+        )
+
+    files: set[Path] = set()
+    for raw_path in raw_paths:
+        candidate = Path(raw_path)
+        if not candidate.is_absolute():
+            candidate = root / candidate
+        candidate = candidate.resolve(strict=False)
+        if not _inside_root(candidate, root):
+            raise ValueError(f"input path escapes repository root: {raw_path}")
+        if candidate.is_dir():
+            files.update(path for path in candidate.rglob("*") if path.is_file())
+        elif candidate.is_file():
+            files.add(candidate)
+        # Deleted paths from a changed-file list are intentionally ignored.
+    return sorted(files)
+
+
+def find_citation_uses(
+    files: list[Path], root: Path, index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]]
+) -> tuple[list[CitationUse], list[CitationUse]]:
+    """Find resolvable label tokens and unknown blueprint-label tokens."""
+
+    uses: set[CitationUse] = set()
+    unknown: set[CitationUse] = set()
+    for path in files:
+        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
+        rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+        for match in CODE_LABEL_RE.finditer(text):
+            label = match.group("label")
+            if label in index:
+                uses.add(CitationUse(label, rel_path, text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1))
+            elif ":" in label:
+                unknown.add(
+                    CitationUse(label, rel_path, text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1)
+                )
+        for match in CANONICAL_CITATION_RE.finditer(text):
+            label = match.group("label")
+            if label not in index:
+                unknown.add(
+                    CitationUse(label, rel_path, text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1)
+                )
+    return sorted(uses, key=lambda use: (use.label, use.path, use.line)), sorted(
+        unknown, key=lambda use: (use.label, use.path, use.line)
+    )
+
+
+def _format_resolutions(
+    labels: list[str],
+    origins: dict[str, list[CitationUse]],
+    index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]],
+    output_format: str,
+) -> tuple[str, bool]:
+    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
+    failed = False
+    for label in labels:
+        locations = index.get(label, [])
+        if len(locations) != 1:
+            failed = True
+        rows.append({
+            "label": label,
+            "locations": [location.locator for location in locations],
+            "cited_at": [f"{use.path}:{use.line}" for use in origins.get(label, [])],
+        })
+
+    if output_format == "json":
+        return json.dumps(rows, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", failed
+
+    if output_format == "plain":
+        rendered = []
+        for row in rows:
+            locations = row["locations"]
+            value = ", ".join(locations) if locations else "UNRESOLVED"
+            rendered.append(f"{row['label']}\t{value}")
+        return "\n".join(rendered) + ("\n" if rendered else ""), failed
+
+    rendered = [
+        "# Resolved blueprint citations",
+        "",
+        "Numeric spans below are derived from durable labels; they are not stored citations.",
+        "",
+    ]
+    if not rows:
+        rendered.append("_No blueprint labels were found in the selected files._")
+    for row in rows:
+        locations = row["locations"]
+        location_text = ", ".join(f"`{item}`" for item in locations) or "**UNRESOLVED**"
+        origin_text = row["cited_at"]
+        suffix = ""
+        if origin_text:
+            suffix = "; cited at " + ", ".join(f"`{item}`" for item in origin_text)
+        rendered.append(f"- `{row['label']}` -> {location_text}{suffix}")
+    return "\n".join(rendered) + "\n", failed
+
+
+def _comment_bounds(text: str, position: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    start = text.rfind("/-", 0, position)
+    end = text.find("-/", position)
+    if start >= 0 and end >= 0:
+        return start, end + 2
+    line_start = text.rfind("\n", 0, position) + 1
+    line_end = text.find("\n", position)
+    return line_start, len(text) if line_end < 0 else line_end
+
+
+def _candidate_for_locator(
+    text: str,
+    match: re.Match[str],
+    index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]],
+) -> str | None:
+    # One label cannot faithfully replace a locator that deliberately names
+    # several disjoint spans. Such citations require a manual label list.
+    if match.group("extra"):
+        return None
+
+    target_name = Path(match.group("path")).name
+    old_start = int(match.group("start"))
+    old_end = int(match.group("end") or match.group("start"))
+    exact = [
+        label
+        for label, locations in index.items()
+        if len(locations) == 1
+        and Path(locations[0].path).name == target_name
+        and (locations[0].start, locations[0].end) == (old_start, old_end)
+    ]
+    if exact:
+        return exact[0] if len(exact) == 1 else None
+
+    block_start, block_end = _comment_bounds(text, match.start())
+    block = text[block_start:block_end]
+    candidates: dict[str, list[re.Match[str]]] = {}
+    for label_match in CODE_LABEL_RE.finditer(block):
+        label = label_match.group("label")
+        locations = index.get(label, [])
+        if len(locations) != 1 or Path(locations[0].path).name != target_name:
+            continue
+        candidates.setdefault(label, []).append(label_match)
+
+    if candidates:
+        linked: set[str] = set()
+        relative_start = match.start() - block_start
+        relative_end = match.end() - block_start
+        for label, label_matches in candidates.items():
+            for label_match in label_matches:
+                if label_match.end() <= relative_start:
+                    between = block[label_match.end():relative_start]
+                    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*\(\s*|\s*[,;]\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+", between):
+                        linked.add(label)
+                elif label_match.start() >= relative_end:
+                    between = block[relative_end:label_match.start()]
+                    after = block[label_match.end():]
+                    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*\(\s*", between) and re.match(r"\s*\)", after):
+                        linked.add(label)
+        return next(iter(linked)) if len(linked) == 1 else None
+
+    return None
+
+
+def _wrap_blueprint_citation_lines(text: str) -> str:
+    """Wrap generated blueprint-citation prose at the Lean line limit."""
+
+    wrapped: list[str] = []
+    for raw_line in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
+        ending = "\n" if raw_line.endswith("\n") else ""
+        line = raw_line[:-1] if ending else raw_line
+        if (len(line) <= LEAN_LINE_WIDTH
+                or not re.search(r"\b[Bb]lueprint\b", line)
+                or CODE_LABEL_RE.search(line) is None):
+            wrapped.append(raw_line)
+            continue
+        indent = line[:len(line) - len(line.lstrip())]
+        current = line
+        while len(current) > LEAN_LINE_WIDTH:
+            split_at = current.rfind(" ", len(indent) + 1, LEAN_LINE_WIDTH + 1)
+            if split_at < 0:
+                break
+            wrapped.append(current[:split_at].rstrip() + "\n")
+            current = indent + current[split_at + 1:].lstrip()
+        wrapped.append(current + ending)
+    return "".join(wrapped)
+
+
+def rewrite_text(
+    text: str, index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]]
+) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
+    """Rewrite unambiguous legacy locators and return unresolved locator text."""
+
+    replacements: list[tuple[int, int, str]] = []
+    unresolved: list[str] = []
+    for match in LEGACY_LOCATOR_RE.finditer(text):
+        label = _candidate_for_locator(text, match, index)
+        if label is None:
+            unresolved.append(match.group(0))
+            continue
+        replacements.append((match.start(), match.end(), f"`{label}`"))
+
+    rewritten = text
+    for start, end, replacement in reversed(replacements):
+        rewritten = rewritten[:start] + replacement + rewritten[end:]
+
+    # Collapse the common legacy wording after the locator itself is replaced.
+    def collapse_duplicate(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
+        link = match.group("link")
+        label = match.group("label")
+        if "\n" not in link:
+            return f"blueprint `{label}`"
+        indent_match = re.search(r"\n(?P<indent>[ \t]*)", link)
+        indent = indent_match.group("indent") if indent_match else ""
+        return f"blueprint\n{indent}`{label}`"
+
+    rewritten = re.sub(
+        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`"
+        r"(?P<link>,\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+|;\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+|\s+in\s+)"
+        r"`(?P=label)`",
+        collapse_duplicate,
+        rewritten,
+    )
+    rewritten = re.sub(
+        r"(?P<prefix>\b[Bb]lueprint\s+)"
+        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`\s*[,;]\s*`(?P=label)`",
+        lambda match: f"{match.group('prefix')}`{match.group('label')}`",
+        rewritten,
+    )
+    def collapse_parenthetical(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
+        label = match.group("label")
+        whitespace = match.group("whitespace")
+        if "\n" not in whitespace:
+            return f"blueprint `{label}`"
+        indent_match = re.search(r"\n(?P<indent>[ \t]*)", whitespace)
+        indent = indent_match.group("indent") if indent_match else ""
+        return f"blueprint\n{indent}`{label}`"
+
+    rewritten = re.sub(
+        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`\s*"
+        r"(?P<whitespace>\(\s*)`(?P=label)`\s*\)",
+        collapse_parenthetical,
+        rewritten,
+    )
+    return _wrap_blueprint_citation_lines(rewritten), unresolved
+
+
+def _resolve_command(args: argparse.Namespace, root: Path) -> int:
+    index = build_label_index(root)
+    files = collect_input_files(root, args.paths, args.files_from)
+    uses, unknown = find_citation_uses(files, root, index)
+    labels = list(args.labels)
+    origins: dict[str, list[CitationUse]] = {}
+    for use in uses:
+        if use.label not in labels:
+            labels.append(use.label)
+        origins.setdefault(use.label, []).append(use)
+    for use in unknown:
+        if use.label not in labels:
+            labels.append(use.label)
+        origins.setdefault(use.label, []).append(use)
+    rendered, failed = _format_resolutions(labels, origins, index, args.format)
+    sys.stdout.write(rendered)
+    return 1 if failed else 0
+
+
+def _rewrite_command(args: argparse.Namespace, root: Path) -> int:
+    index = build_label_index(root)
+    files = collect_input_files(root, args.paths, args.files_from)
+    changes: list[tuple[Path, str, str]] = []
+    unresolved: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []
+    for path in files:
+        old = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
+        new, missing = rewrite_text(old, index)
+        if old != new:
+            changes.append((path, old, new))
+        unresolved.extend((path, locator) for locator in missing)
+
+    for path, locator in unresolved:
+        rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+        print(f"unresolved: {rel_path}: {locator}", file=sys.stderr)
+    if unresolved and not args.allow_unresolved:
+        print("refusing partial rewrite; pass --allow-unresolved to rewrite safe matches",
+              file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+
+    if args.write:
+        for path, _old, new in changes:
+            path.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8")
+    else:
+        for path, old, new in changes:
+            rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+            sys.stdout.writelines(difflib.unified_diff(
+                old.splitlines(keepends=True),
+                new.splitlines(keepends=True),
+                fromfile=rel_path,
+                tofile=rel_path,
+            ))
+    action = "rewrote" if args.write else "would rewrite"
+    print(f"{action} {len(changes)} file(s); {len(unresolved)} unresolved locator(s)",
+          file=sys.stderr)
+    return 0
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--root",
+        type=Path,
+        default=Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent,
+        help="repository root (default: parent of scripts/)",
+    )
+    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
+
+    resolve = subparsers.add_parser("resolve", help="resolve labels to current spans")
+    resolve.add_argument("labels", nargs="*", help="blueprint labels to resolve")
+    resolve.add_argument("--path", dest="paths", action="append", default=[],
+                         help="scan a repository file or directory for label tokens")
+    resolve.add_argument("--files-from", type=Path,
+                         help="scan repository paths listed one per line")
+    resolve.add_argument("--format", choices=("markdown", "plain", "json"),
+                         default="plain")
+
+    rewrite = subparsers.add_parser("rewrite", help="replace unambiguous legacy locators")
+    rewrite.add_argument("paths", nargs="*", help="repository files or directories to rewrite")
+    rewrite.add_argument("--files-from", type=Path,
+                         help="rewrite repository paths listed one per line")
+    rewrite.add_argument("--write", action="store_true",
+                         help="write changes in place (default: print a diff)")
+    rewrite.add_argument("--allow-unresolved", action="store_true",
+                         help="rewrite safe matches while reporting unresolved locators")
+
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    root = args.root.resolve()
+    try:
+        if args.command == "resolve":
+            return _resolve_command(args, root)
+        return _rewrite_command(args, root)
+    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
+        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

 # acquire_lock <lockdir> <wait-seconds> <label>
 # Per-PR review lock.  No cancellation: a queued review waits and then
 # re-checks the head SHA (pr-review.yml:18-20, cancel-in-progress false).
 acquire_lock() {
   local dir="$1" wait_s="$2" label="$3" waited=0 holder=""
   mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dir")"
   while ! mkdir "$dir" 2>/dev/null; do
     holder="$(cat "$dir/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
     if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
       warn "removing stale lock $dir (holder pid $holder is gone)"
       rm -rf "$dir"
       continue
     fi
     if [ "$waited" -ge "$wait_s" ]; then
       die "timed out after ${wait_s}s waiting for the review lock $dir (holder pid ${holder:-unknown})"
     fi
     [ "$waited" = 0 ] && log "another review holds $dir (pid ${holder:-unknown}); queuing"
     sleep 5
     waited=$((waited + 5))
   done
   printf '%s\n' "$$" >"$dir/pid"
   printf '%s\n' "$label" >"$dir/label"
   LOCK_HELD="$dir"
 }

 # resolve_worktree <branch> — same resolution order as ci.sh: git's own
 # registry first, then the .worktrees/<branch> convention.  Creates it if the
 # branch has no worktree yet.
 resolve_worktree() {
   local branch="$1" found="" safe dest have
   found="$(git -C "$ROOT" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null |
     awk -v b="refs/heads/$branch" '
       /^worktree /{p=substr($0,10)}

   if [ -n "$found" ] && [ -d "$found" ]; then
     printf '%s\n' "$found"

   safe="$(printf '%s' "$branch" | tr '/' '-')"
   dest="$ROOT/.worktrees/$safe"
   if [ -e "$dest" ]; then
     have="$(git -C "$dest" rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
     if [ "$have" = "$branch" ]; then
       printf '%s\n' "$dest"
       return 0

     die "$dest exists but is not a worktree of '$branch' (HEAD: ${have:-not a git worktree}); run 'git -C $ROOT worktree prune' or remove it"
   fi
   mkdir -p "$ROOT/.worktrees"
   git -C "$ROOT" worktree add --quiet "$dest" "$branch" ||

   if [ -x "$ROOT/local/bin/worktree-setup.sh" ]; then

    the operator posts an **ADJUDICATION comment** on the PR — a body starting

 3. the merge commit names the adjudication and the issues created;
 4. `pr_merge.py --adjudicated` accepts it in place of a clean verdict, and
    only for the current head — a stale `head=` is a refusal.

 are carried too, so an adjudication at the new head remains possible.  Any
 change to the patch (a repair, a conflict resolution) yields a different
 patch-id and a real review.  `--force-review` bypasses the fast path.

 A script is in scope when it directly parses or validates `blueprint/src/**/*.tex`, checks `\lean{...}` / `\leanok` annotations, or is a wrapper/shared Python utility imported by those checks.

   274	def _comment_bounds(text: str, position: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
   275	    start = text.rfind("/-", 0, position)
   276	    end = text.find("-/", position)
   277	    if start >= 0 and end >= 0:
   278	        return start, end + 2
   279	    line_start = text.rfind("\n", 0, position) + 1

   284	def _candidate_for_locator(
   285	    text: str,
   286	    match: re.Match[str],
   287	    index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]],
   288	) -> str | None:
   289	    # One label cannot faithfully replace a locator that deliberately names
   290	    # several disjoint spans. Such citations require a manual label list.
   291	    if match.group("extra"):
   292	        return None
   293	
   294	    target_name = Path(match.group("path")).name
   295	    old_start = int(match.group("start"))
   296	    old_end = int(match.group("end") or match.group("start"))
   297	    exact = [
   298	        label
   299	        for label, locations in index.items()
   300	        if len(locations) == 1
   301	        and Path(locations[0].path).name == target_name
   302	        and (locations[0].start, locations[0].end) == (old_start, old_end)
   303	    ]
   304	    if exact:
   305	        return exact[0] if len(exact) == 1 else None
   306	
   307	    block_start, block_end = _comment_bounds(text, match.start())
   308	    block = text[block_start:block_end]
   309	    candidates: dict[str, list[re.Match[str]]] = {}
   310	    for label_match in CODE_LABEL_RE.finditer(block):
   311	        label = label_match.group("label")
   312	        locations = index.get(label, [])
   313	        if len(locations) != 1 or Path(locations[0].path).name != target_name:
   314	            continue
   315	        candidates.setdefault(label, []).append(label_match)
   316	
   317	    if candidates:
   318	        linked: set[str] = set()
   319	        relative_start = match.start() - block_start
   320	        relative_end = match.end() - block_start
   321	        for label, label_matches in candidates.items():
   322	            for label_match in label_matches:
   323	                if label_match.end() <= relative_start:
   324	                    between = block[label_match.end():relative_start]
   325	                    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*\(\s*|\s*[,;]\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+", between):
   326	                        linked.add(label)
   327	                elif label_match.start() >= relative_end:
   328	                    between = block[relative_end:label_match.start()]
   329	                    after = block[label_match.end():]
   330	                    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*\(\s*", between) and re.match(r"\s*\)", after):
   331	                        linked.add(label)
   332	        return next(iter(linked)) if len(linked) == 1 else None
   333	
   334	    return None

   337	def _wrap_blueprint_citation_lines(text: str) -> str:
   338	    """Wrap generated blueprint-citation prose at the Lean line limit."""
   339	
   340	    wrapped: list[str] = []
   341	    for raw_line in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
   342	        ending = "\n" if raw_line.endswith("\n") else ""
   343	        line = raw_line[:-1] if ending else raw_line
   344	        if (len(line) <= LEAN_LINE_WIDTH
   345	                or not re.search(r"\b[Bb]lueprint\b", line)
   346	                or CODE_LABEL_RE.search(line) is None):
   347	            wrapped.append(raw_line)
   348	            continue
   349	        indent = line[:len(line) - len(line.lstrip())]
   350	        current = line
   351	        while len(current) > LEAN_LINE_WIDTH:
   352	            split_at = current.rfind(" ", len(indent) + 1, LEAN_LINE_WIDTH + 1)
   353	            if split_at < 0:
   354	                break
   355	            wrapped.append(current[:split_at].rstrip() + "\n")
   356	            current = indent + current[split_at + 1:].lstrip()
   357	        wrapped.append(current + ending)
   358	    return "".join(wrapped)

   364	    """Rewrite unambiguous legacy locators and return unresolved locator text."""

   371	            unresolved.append(match.group(0))

   373	        replacements.append((match.start(), match.end(), f"`{label}`"))

   375	    rewritten = text
   376	    for start, end, replacement in reversed(replacements):
   377	        rewritten = rewritten[:start] + replacement + rewritten[end:]

380	    def collapse_duplicate(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
   381	        link = match.group("link")
   382	        label = match.group("label")
   383	        if "\n" not in link:
   384	            return f"blueprint `{label}`"
   385	        indent_match = re.search(r"\n(?P<indent>[ \t]*)", link)
   386	        indent = indent_match.group("indent") if indent_match else ""
   387	        return f"blueprint\n{indent}`{label}`"
   388	
   389	    rewritten = re.sub(
   390	        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`"
   391	        r"(?P<link>,\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+|;\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+|\s+in\s+)"
   392	        r"`(?P=label)`",
   393	        collapse_duplicate,
   394	        rewritten,
   395	    )
   396	    rewritten = re.sub(
   397	        r"(?P<prefix>\b[Bb]lueprint\s+)"
   398	        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`\s*[,;]\s*`(?P=label)`",
   399	        lambda match: f"{match.group('prefix')}`{match.group('label')}`",
   400	        rewritten,
   401	    )
   402	    def collapse_parenthetical(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
   403	        label = match.group("label")
   404	        whitespace = match.group("whitespace")
   405	        if "\n" not in whitespace:
   406	            return f"blueprint `{label}`"
   407	        indent_match = re.search(r"\n(?P<indent>[ \t]*)", whitespace)
   408	        indent = indent_match.group("indent") if indent_match else ""
   409	        return f"blueprint\n{indent}`{label}`"
   410	
   411	    rewritten = re.sub(
   412	        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`\s*"
   413	        r"(?P<whitespace>\(\s*)`(?P=label)`\s*\)",
   414	        collapse_parenthetical,
   415	        rewritten,
   416	    )

   439	def _rewrite_command(args: argparse.Namespace, root: Path) -> int:
   440	    index = build_label_index(root)
   441	    files = collect_input_files(root, args.paths, args.files_from)
   442	    changes: list[tuple[Path, str, str]] = []
   443	    unresolved: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []
   444	    for path in files:
   445	        old = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
   446	        new, missing = rewrite_text(old, index)
   447	        if old != new:
   448	            changes.append((path, old, new))
   449	        unresolved.extend((path, locator) for locator in missing)
   450	
   451	    for path, locator in unresolved:
   452	        rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
   453	        print(f"unresolved: {rel_path}: {locator}", file=sys.stderr)
   454	    if unresolved and not args.allow_unresolved:
   455	        print("refusing partial rewrite; pass --allow-unresolved to rewrite safe matches",
   456	              file=sys.stderr)
   457	        return 1
   458	
   459	    if args.write:
   460	        for path, _old, new in changes:
   461	            path.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8")
   462	    else:
   463	        for path, old, new in changes:
   464	            rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
   465	            sys.stdout.writelines(difflib.unified_diff(
   466	                old.splitlines(keepends=True),
   467	                new.splitlines(keepends=True),
   468	                fromfile=rel_path,
   469	                tofile=rel_path,
   470	            ))
   471	    action = "rewrote" if args.write else "would rewrite"
   472	    print(f"{action} {len(changes)} file(s); {len(unresolved)} unresolved locator(s)",
   473	          file=sys.stderr)
   474	    return 0

 ### Additional rules:
 - **Section names in Lean**: use mathematical terms (`section QuantumSoundness`, `section SelfImprovement`, `section PastingLemma`), not organizational terms (`section Assembly`, `section Pipeline`).
 - **Internal LaTeX labels** (e.g., `\label{ch:soundness}`) are not reader-facing and need not be renamed if doing so would break cross-references. But NEW labels should follow the standard.
 - **Definitions that are actually theorems**: if a statement asserts a mathematical fact, it must be `\begin{theorem}`, not `\begin{definition}`. Definitions introduce new objects; theorems prove properties.
 
 ## `\uses` Dependency Guidelines
 - **Statement `\uses`**: list only what's needed to *state* the result (typically definitions of the objects involved). Keep minimal — transitive deps are automatic.
 - **Proof `\uses`**: list only what the proof *actually calls*. Don't list definitions unless the proof unfolds that definition.
 - **Never self-reference**: a proof's `\uses` must NOT include the label of the theorem it proves.
 
 ## Recording Formalization-Only Lemmas
 Some Lean lemmas are genuine proof infrastructure rather than named statements
 from the original papers. These must be traceable without making the blueprint
 look as if the paper stated them.

   276	# All codex invocations go through local/bin/dispatch.sh when it exists, so the

   286	    local args

   288	          --worktree "$wt" --sandbox "$sandbox"
   289	          --persona "$persona" --persona-ref "$TRUSTED_REF"
   290	          --effort "$REVIEW_EFFORT")

   292	    # cap cannot let a large diff starve it from the reviewer context.
   293	    if [ -s "$BLUEPRINT_CITATION_MAP" ]; then

   299	      args[${#args[@]}]="$ctx"
   300	    fi

   302	      args[${#args[@]}]="--context-file"
   303	      args[${#args[@]}]="$RUN_DIR/prior-ledger.md"
   304	    fi
   305	    args[${#args[@]}]="--"
   306	    args[${#args[@]}]="$task_text"

   308	    # with zero tokens never reached the model (transient CLI/API hiccup;
   309	    # observed on PR #0003, events.md 2026-08-31), so retrying cannot
   310	    # duplicate a review.
   311	    local attempt started ended tokens
   312	    for attempt in 1 2; do
   313	      started="$(date +%s)"
   314	      set +e
   315	      if [ -n "$model" ]; then
   316	        MIPSTARRE_SESSION_TIMEOUT="$REVIEW_TIMEOUT" MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1 \
   317	          MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL="$model" "$DISPATCH" "${args[@]}" >"$dlog"
   318	      else
   319	        MIPSTARRE_SESSION_TIMEOUT="$REVIEW_TIMEOUT" MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1 \
   320	          "$DISPATCH" "${args[@]}" >"$dlog"

   325	      tokens="$(sed -n 's/^tokens_total: //p' "$dlog" | tail -1)"

   345	  warn "local/bin/dispatch.sh not found; falling back to a direct 'codex exec'. This session will NOT appear in results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl."

     2	
     3	from __future__ import annotations
     4	
     5	
     6	def strip_tex_comment(line: str) -> str:
     7	    r"""Return the active TeX prefix before the first unescaped ``%``.
     8	
     9	    TeX comments start at an unescaped percent sign. A percent sign preceded
    10	    by an odd-length run of backslashes is the literal ``\%`` token and must
    11	    not truncate the line; an even-length run leaves the ``%`` unescaped.
    12	    """
    13	
    14	    for idx, char in enumerate(line):
    15	        if char != "%":
    16	            continue
    17	        backslashes = 0
    18	        j = idx - 1
    19	        while j >= 0 and line[j] == "\\":
    20	            backslashes += 1
    21	            j -= 1
    22	        if backslashes % 2 == 0:
    23	            return line[:idx]
    24	    return line

     2	# dispatch.sh — the only sanctioned way to start a codex agent session.
     3	#
     4	# Usage:
     5	#   local/bin/dispatch.sh --role <orc|prover|reviewer|simplifier|blueprint|splitter|scout>
     6	#                         --issue <id|scope>

     9	#                         [--persona FILE]        repo-relative => read from the trusted ref
    10	#                         [--persona-ref REF]     trusted ref for personas (default: main)
    11	#                         [--no-persona]          dispatch with the built-in role frame only
    12	#                         [--resume THREAD_ID]    continue an existing codex thread
    13	#                         [--effort LEVEL]        model_reasoning_effort override
    14	#                         [--context-file FILE]   untrusted data to attach (repeatable)
    15	#                         [--pr ID]               PR id recorded in the registry line
    16	#                         [--skip-hook-check]     do not install/verify git hooks
    17	#                         [--lock-wait SECONDS]   wait for a busy worktree (default 0)
    18	#                         [--dry-run]             print the composed prompt and exit
    19	#                         -- "task prompt"
    20	#
    21	# Replaces the parent repository's GitHub-hosted agent entry points: the
    22	# @claude/@codex mention responder (.github/workflows/claude.yml) and the
    23	# agent invocations inside pr-review.yml / auto-fix.yml, whose bot identity,
    24	# trusted-prompt checkout and run accounting came from GitHub. Locally the
    25	# equivalents are: this script's single entry point (identity), `git show
    26	# <ref>:<path>` for personas (trusted prompts, DESIGN.md invariant 5), and
    27	# results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl (accounting, DESIGN.md "Agent sessions").
    28	#
    29	# What it does, in order:
    30	#   1. validates the role, sanitizes the scope (bracket-free naming),
    31	#      resolves the sandbox default, honours LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED;
    32	#   2. allocates a session name <role>-<scope>-<yyyymmdd>-<seq> under a lock;
    33	#   3. installs/verifies the per-worktree git hooks for write sessions;
    34	#   4. composes the prompt: persona (from the trusted ref) + session context
    35	#      + sanitized untrusted attachments + the task;
    36	#   5. runs `codex exec --json -C <worktree> --sandbox <mode> </dev/null`,
    37	#      teeing live events to the cache and publishing the final capture to
    38	#      results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl;
    39	#   6. appends the registry line via local/bin/telemetry.py and prints
    40	#      name, thread_id and the last-message path.
    41	#
    42	# Exit codes: 0 ok · 2 usage · 3 disabled by kill switch · 4 preflight failure
    43	#   · 5 worktree busy · 6 telemetry failure · otherwise codex's own status.
    44	#
    45	# Environment: MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT (runtime state root, default
    46	#   ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev), MIPSTARRE_PERSONA_REF, MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL,
    47	#   MIPSTARRE_SESSION (dispatching session name), MIPSTARRE_DISPATCH_LOCK_WAIT,

     4	/-!
     5	# Pauli basis test soundness interface
     6	
     7	This module contains the quantitative error function and the closed definitions
     8	used to state Pauli basis test soundness.  The carriers are concrete
     9	finite-dimensional vectors and matrices so that the soundness proof can use the
    10	existing Hilbert-space API without introducing a dependency cycle.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The interface supports blueprint
    15	`thm:pauli`, with paper origin
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    17	The distance functionals use blueprint `def:state-distance` and
    18	`def:povm-distance`.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    26	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27

    29	
    30	/-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;
    31	the powers are real `rpow`s and the asymptotic constants are absorbed into `a`,
    32	as specified by blueprint `thm:pauli`,
    33	paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    34	-/
    35	noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    36	  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
    37	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
    38	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
    39	
    40	/-- Monotonicity obligation for adjusting the universal constants in
    41	`deltaQld` on the source parameter domain. This Lean-only helper supports the
    42	enlargement of `a` and shrinkage of `b` for `0 ≤ ε ≤ 1` described in blueprint
    43	`lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`; the source makes this constant adjustment at
    44	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1402`. It is not
    45	an additional hypothesis of `thm:pauli` or `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
    46	theorem deltaQld_mono {P : AdmissibleParams} {a a' b b' ε : ℝ}
    47	    (ha0 : 1 ≤ a) (ha : a ≤ a') (hb : b' ≤ b) (hb' : 0 < b')
    48	    (hε0 : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1) :
    49	    deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ≤ deltaQld a' b' ε P.m P.d P.q := by
    50	  sorry
    51	
    52	/-- The ideal auxiliary state `aux ⊗ EPR_q^{⊗M}` in the shuffled register
    53	ordering.  The EPR factor is the concrete `eprState` from blueprint
    54	`def:EPR`; paper
    55	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`).
    56	-/
    57	noncomputable def idealState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    58	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    59	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    60	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
    61	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    62	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) ×
    63	      (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) ℂ).symm
    64	    (fun p =>
    65	      ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ) aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
    66	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P) ℂ)
    67	          (eprState (PauliRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
    68	
    69	/-- The A-side ideal Pauli projector, with identities on the auxiliary and
    70	B-side registers.  This is a concrete matrix form of the operator comparison
    71	in blueprint `thm:pauli`; paper
    72	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    73	-/
    74	noncomputable def pauliProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    75	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    76	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    77	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    78	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    79	  fun p q =>
    80	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
    81	      pauliProj W u p.1.2 q.1.2
    82	    else 0
    83	
    84	/-- The symmetric B-side ideal Pauli projector from blueprint
    85	`thm:pauli`, paper origin
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    87	-/
    88	noncomputable def pauliProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    89	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    90	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    91	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    92	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    93	  fun p q =>
    94	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
    95	      pauliProj W u p.2.2 q.2.2
    96	    else 0
    97	
    98	/-- Lift a conjugated A-side effect to the full ideal register in blueprint
    99	`thm:pauli`, paper origin
   100	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   101	-/
   102	noncomputable def liftedAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   103	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   104	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   105	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   106	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P))
   107	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
   108	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   109	  fun p q =>
   110	    if p.2 = q.2 then
   111	      (conjIsometry φA M) p.1 q.1
   112	    else 0
   113	
   114	/-- Lift a conjugated B-side effect to the full ideal register in blueprint
   115	`thm:pauli`, paper origin
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   117	-/
   118	noncomputable def liftedBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   119	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   120	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   121	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   122	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P))
   123	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   124	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   125	  fun p q =>
   126	    if p.1 = q.1 then
   127	      (conjIsometry φB M) p.2 q.2
   128	    else 0
   129	
   130	/-- A finite witness packaging the auxiliary dimensions, isometries, and state
   131	from `thm:pauli`.  This structure is a Lean-only encoding of the existential
   132	data in the paper theorem; it introduces no extra hypothesis.  Blueprint
   133	`thm:pauli`, paper origin
   134	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   135	-/
   136	structure PauliSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
   137	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
   138	  ιA' : Type
   139	  ιB' : Type
   140	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
   141	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
   142	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
   143	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
   144	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   145	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P)
   146	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   147	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P)
   148	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
   149	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
   150	
   151	attribute [instance] PauliSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype
   152	  PauliSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
   153	
   154	/-- The A-side operator-distance quantity appearing in the soundness
   155	conclusion.  It is the finite-sum realization of `def:povm-distance` from
   156	`def:povm-distance`, paper origin
   157	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   158	-/
   159	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceA
   160	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   161	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   162	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   163	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   164	        (((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).postprocess pauliAnswerOrZero).effect u) -
   165	      pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   166	
   167	/-- The symmetric B-side operator-distance quantity from blueprint
   168	`def:povm-distance`, paper origin
   169	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   170	-/
   171	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceB
   172	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   173	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   174	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   175	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedBEffect S w.φB
   176	        (((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).postprocess pauliAnswerOrZero).effect u) -
   177	      pauliProjOnB'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   178	
   179	end

    14	## References

    29	/-- The numerical admissible Pauli-test parameter package.  Its scalar carrier
    30	uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel q hq`, so the paper's fixed
    31	self-dual-normal identification is not quantified in the test statement.  This
    32	is blueprint
    33	`def:admissible`, paper origin
    34	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    35	-/
    36	structure AdmissibleParams where
    37	  q : ℕ
    38	  m : ℕ
    39	  d : ℕ
    40	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    41	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    42	  hdvd : m ∣ q

    46	`def:admissible`, paper origin

    50	  sorry

    52	/-- The fixed model accessor for an admissible parameter package.  It is a
    53	compatibility view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently
    54	quantified field representation.  Blueprint `def:admissible`; paper
    55	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    56	-/
    57	noncomputable def AdmissibleParams.model (P : AdmissibleParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
    58	  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq

    60	/-- The low-degree parameter view of an admissible Pauli-test package.  This is
    61	a Lean-only bridge supporting the statement closure; it is not an additional
    62	hypothesis of `thm:pauli`.  Blueprint
    63	`thm:pauli`, paper origin
    64	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.

    66	def AdmissibleParams.toLdParams (P : AdmissibleParams) : LdParams where
    67	  q := P.q

    71	  hm := P.one_le_m
    72	  hd := P.hd

    74	  hq := P.hq
    75	  hdvd := P.hdvd

    77	/-- The scalar carrier associated with an admissible parameter package.  It is
    78	the globally fixed field carrier selected by `AdmissibleParams.model` in

    80	`def:admissible`, paper origin
    81	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.

    86	blueprint `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
    87	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
    88	-/
    89	inductive PauliType where
    90	  | point (W : PauliKind)
    91	  | aline (W : PauliKind)
    92	  | dline (W : PauliKind)
    93	  | pauli (W : PauliKind)
    94	  | pairW (W : PauliKind)
    95	  | pair
    96	  | ms (t : MsType)

    99	/-- The register blocks used by the Pauli question space.  These are the

   102	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.

   104	abbrev PauliIndex (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   105	  (((((Fin P.m ⊕ Fin P.m) ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m) ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Unit)
   106	
   107	/-- The ambient Pauli question coefficient space (blueprint
   108	`def:pauli-question-distribution`; paper origin
   109	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).

   560	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   561	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   562	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   563	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   564	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   565	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   566	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
   567	      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
   568	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   569	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   570	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
   571	          else true
   572	      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
   573	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   574	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   575	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
   576	          else true
   577	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   578	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   579	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   580	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)

   582	    else false

   584	/-- The Pauli basis test game packages blueprint
   585	`def:pauli-question-distribution` and `def:pauli-win-predicate` as a symmetric game;
   586	paper origin
   587	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   588	-/
   589	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   590	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   591	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   592	  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   593	  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   594	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   595	  μ_prob := by sorry
   596	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P

   598	end
