1	\chapter{Strategy observables and the expanded space}
     2	\label{chap:qpbt-observables}
     3	% This chapter covers the first three subsections of the source appendix
     4	% ``Analysis of the Pauli basis test''
     5	% (references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex, lines 1-679).
     6	% The paper's subsection labels sec:qld-prelim, sec:commutation and
     7	% sec:expanding are kept on the sections below for cross-reference fidelity.
     8	% The source restates thm:pauli verbatim at the head of the appendix under the

    10	% all references here are to thm:pauli as stated in Chapter chap:qpbt-test.
    11	
    12	This chapter and the two that follow contain the proof of the soundness
    13	theorem for the Pauli basis test, Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}, stated in
    14	Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-test}. Starting from a strategy that succeeds in the
    15	game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ with high probability, the proof
    16	constructs a representation of the Pauli group on the players' Hilbert space
    17	in several stages. In Section~\ref{sec:commutation} the strategy measurements
    18	are used to define a set of observables that correspond to a subset of the
    19	Pauli $X$ and $Z$ observables, and these observables are shown to
    20	approximately satisfy the associated Pauli group relations. In
    21	Section~\ref{sec:expanding}, ancillary registers containing EPR states are
    22	adjoined to the players' state, and a new set of approximately commuting
    23	observables acting on the expanded state is defined.
    24	Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-combining} combines the approximately commuting
    25	observables into a strategy for the \emph{classical} low individual degree
    26	test and applies the soundness theorem of that test to construct a single
    27	projective measurement that simultaneously measures all of them.
    28	Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction} uses this simultaneous measurement to
    29	construct an exact representation of the Pauli group, shows that it is close
    30	to the original strategy observables on the expanded state, and deduces
    31	Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}. Section~\ref{sec:qld-prelim} below collects
    32	preliminary definitions and lemmas used throughout the analysis.
    33

    37	\begin{definition}[Individual and total degree polynomial classes]
    38		\label{def:ideg-deg-polynomials}
    39		\lean{MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc}
    40		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.TotalDegreePoly}

    44		\uses{def:line, def:line-representative, def:polyfunc}
    45		Given integers $d, m \geq 0$ and a prime power $q$, denote by
    46		$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ the set of polynomials in $m$ variables over
    47		$\F_q$ with \emph{individual} degree at most $d$ in each variable. When
    48		the field is clear from context we write $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}$, and when
    49		the number of variables is also clear from context, $\mathrm{ideg}_d$. We
    50		denote by $\deg_d$ the set of polynomials with \emph{total} degree at
    51		most $d$.
    52		% The line-restricted classes below are introduced only implicitly in the
    53		% source, in the statement of the lemma labelled lem:qld-comm-line-cons,
    54		% which reads them as polynomials "defined on the line". The coefficient
    55		% reading adopted here follows the answer format of the decision procedure
    56		% of the low individual degree game (source figure fig:ld-decider) and the
    57		% representative convention of def:polyfunc; see the remark following this
    58		% definition.
    59		For a line $\ell \subseteq \F_q^m$ (Definition~\ref{def:line}) presented
    60		by a base point $u_0$ and a direction $v$ --- for the lines arising as
    61		question contents, the pair read off the line's description, whose base
    62		point is the canonical representative of
    63		Definition~\ref{def:line-representative} --- and an integer $c \geq 0$,
    64		we write $\deg_c(\ell)$ for the set of univariate polynomials of degree
    65		at most $c$, each given by its list of $c+1$ coefficients and identified
    66		by its polynomial representative rather than by the function it induces,
    67		as in Definition~\ref{def:polyfunc}; the argument $\ell$ records the
    68		line to which such an answer refers, through the parameterization
    69		$t \mapsto u_0 + tv$. The cases used below are $\deg_d(\ell)$ and
    70		$\deg_{md}(\ell)$; whenever $d \leq md$, extending coefficient lists by
    71		zeros gives the inclusion $\deg_d(\ell) \subseteq \deg_{md}(\ell)$. For
    72		$f \in \deg_c(\ell)$, $u \in \ell$, and $a \in \F_q$, we say that $f$
    73		\emph{evaluates to $a$ at $u$}, written $f(u) = a$, if $f(t) = a$ for
    74		every $t \in \F_q$ with $u = u_0 + tv$. When $v \neq 0$ this $t$ is
    75		unique, so every $f$ evaluates at every point of $\ell$; when $v = 0$,
    76		so that $\ell = \{u_0\}$, exactly those $f$ that induce a constant
    77		function on $\F_q$ evaluate at $u_0$, to their constant value. An
    78		operator indexed by $f(u)$ is understood to be the zero operator when
    79		$f$ does not evaluate at $u$, and for a family $\{N_f\}$ indexed by
    80		$f \in \deg_c(\ell)$ we write
    81		$N_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=a]} = \sum_{f \colon f(u) = a} N_f$; when
    82		$v = 0$ the classes indexed by $a \in \F_q$ form a sub-measurement
    83		rather than a partition of the outcomes. The \emph{completed} family of
    84		evaluation classes is the family indexed by $a \in \F_q \cup \{\bot\}$
    85		obtained by adjoining the additional class
    86		$N_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=\bot]} = \sum_{f} N_f$, the sum over those
    87		$f$ that do not evaluate at $u$; when $\{N_f\}$ is a POVM,
    88		respectively a projective measurement, the completed classes form one
    89		as well, and when $v \neq 0$ the class
    90		$N_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=\bot]}$ is the zero operator.
    91	\end{definition}

    94		\label{rem:deg-line-representatives}

    96		``defined on the line $\ell$'', that is, as functions on the point set
    97		of $\ell$, while its decision procedure expects each line answer as a
    98		list of coefficients. The two readings differ. When $md \geq q$,

   600		\begin{equation}\label{eq:qld-strat-obs}

   607		$M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$ denotes.

   711		bounded below by a universal constant.

  1362		than $\simeq$ and its right-hand side is not of the form
  1363		$\Id \ot B$; instead, a direct computation from
  1364		item~\ref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons} together with projectivity gives
  1365		% The source ends this display with the exact upper bound eps; the bound
  1366		% inherited from item 2 carries the hidden universal constant of
  1367		% def:povm-distance, which is retained inside the O(.).
  1368		\[
  1369			\E_{(\ell,u)} \sum_{a \in \F_q}
  1370			\bra{\hat{\psi}}\, \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},W),\ell}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=a]}
  1371			\ot \big( \Id - \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a \big) \ket{\hat{\psi}}
  1372			\,\leq\, O(\eps)\,,
  1373		\]
  1374		while the mass bound of the previous paragraph controls the outcomes
  1375		omitted from every class,
  1376		$\E_{(\ell,u)} \bra{\hat{\psi}} \big( \Id - \sum_a
  1377		\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},W),\ell}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=a]} \big)
  1378		\ot \Id \ket{\hat{\psi}} \leq O(\eps)$; both terms are needed because
  1379		for a zero-direction $\ell$ the classes
  1380		$[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=a]$ need not exhaust $\deg_{md}(\ell)$.
  1381		An elementary bound for projective sub-measurements $\{A_i\}$,
  1382		$\{B_i\}$ and a state $\ket{\varphi}$, namely
  1383		$\sum_i \bra{\varphi}(A_i - B_i)\ket{\varphi} \leq 2 \big( \sum_i \big\|(A_i - B_i)\ket{\varphi}\big\|^2 \big)^{1/2}$,
  1384		upgrades these two bounds to
  1385		$\Id \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} \sum_a \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},W),\ell}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=a]} \ot \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$.
  1386		A second elementary fact about projective measurements --- if
  1387		$\Id \approx_\delta \sum_i A^x_i \ot B^x_i$ for families of projective
  1388		measurements $\{A^x_i\}$ and $\{B^x_i\}$ acting on separate registers
  1389		of a bipartite state, then $A^x_i \ot \Id \simeq_\delta \Id \ot B^x_i$,
  1390		and hence $A^x_i \ot \Id \approx_\delta \Id \ot B^x_i$ by item~1 of
  1391		Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement} --- is then applied to the two families
  1392		completed as in Definition~\ref{def:ideg-deg-polynomials}: the
  1393		evaluation classes of the expanded line measurement together with
  1394		$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},W),\ell}_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=\bot]}$,
  1395		and the expanded point measurement together with
  1396		$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_{\bot} = 0$. Both completed families
  1397		are projective measurements, and the completion leaves the sum in the
  1398		hypothesis unchanged, since the term for the outcome $\bot$ vanishes.
  1399		Restricted to the outcomes in $\F_q$, the conclusion yields
  1400		item~\ref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2} with error $\sqrt{\eps}$, so that
  1401		$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps) = \sqrt{\eps}$. The symmetric
  1402		equivalents follow from
  1403		Lemma~\ref{lem:symmetric-equivalents-transfer}.
  1404	\end{proof}
  1405	
  1406	The expanded point and line measurements constructed in this section, being
  1407	approximately consistent and approximately commuting, are combined into a
  1408	single strategy for the classical low individual degree test in
  1409	Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-combining}.

     3

     5	derives the current source span of each label from ``blueprint/src/chapter``.
     6	It can also conservatively rewrite old ``chNN_*.tex:START-END`` citations when

    93	def _parse_tex_file(path: Path, root: Path) -> list[LabelLocation]:
    94	    """Return active labels in *path*, with enclosing statement/proof spans."""
    95	
    96	    lines = _active_lines(path)
    97	    stack: list[_OpenEnvironment] = []
    98	    environments: list[EnvironmentSpan] = []
    99	    labels: list[tuple[str, int]] = []
   100	
   101	    for line_no, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
   102	        for token in TOKEN_RE.finditer(line):
   103	            kind = token.group("kind")
   104	            value = token.group("value")
   105	            if kind == "begin":
   106	                stack.append(_OpenEnvironment(value, line_no))
   107	            elif kind == "label":
   108	                labels.append((value, line_no))
   109	            else:
   110	                match_at = next(
   111	                    (index for index in range(len(stack) - 1, -1, -1)
   112	                     if stack[index].name == value),
   113	                    None,
   114	                )
   115	                if match_at is None:
   116	                    continue
   117	                opened = stack[match_at]
   118	                del stack[match_at:]
   119	                environments.append(EnvironmentSpan(value, opened.start, line_no))
   120	
   121	    environments.sort(key=lambda span: (span.start, span.end - span.start))
   122	    proof_spans = [span for span in environments if span.name == "proof"]
   123	    rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
   124	    locations: list[LabelLocation] = []
   125	
   126	    for label, label_line in labels:
   127	        enclosing = [
   128	            span for span in environments
   129	            if span.start <= label_line <= span.end
   130	        ]
   131	        if enclosing:
   132	            span = min(enclosing, key=lambda item: (item.end - item.start, -item.start))
   133	            start, end = span.start, span.end
   134	            if span.name in STATEMENT_ENVS:
   135	                following = next(
   136	                    (proof for proof in proof_spans if proof.start > span.end),
   137	                    None,
   138	                )
   139	                if following is not None:
   140	                    gap = lines[span.end:following.start - 1]
   141	                    if all(not item.strip() for item in gap):
   142	                        end = following.end
   143	        else:
   144	            start = end = label_line
   145	        locations.append(LabelLocation(label, rel_path, label_line, start, end))
   146	
   147	    return locations

   150	def build_label_index(root: Path) -> dict[str, list[LabelLocation]]:
   151	    """Index active blueprint labels below ``root/blueprint/src/chapter``."""
   152	
   153	    chapter_root = root / "blueprint" / "src" / "chapter"
   154	    if not chapter_root.is_dir():
   155	        raise ValueError(f"blueprint chapter directory does not exist: {chapter_root}")
   156	    index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]] = {}
   157	    for path in sorted(chapter_root.rglob("*.tex")):
   158	        for location in _parse_tex_file(path, root):
   159	            index.setdefault(location.label, []).append(location)
   160	    return index

   164	    try:
   165	        path.relative_to(root)

   171	def collect_input_files(root: Path, paths: list[str], files_from: Path | None) -> list[Path]:
   172	    """Resolve explicit repository paths without permitting traversal."""
   173	
   174	    raw_paths = list(paths)
   175	    if files_from is not None:
   176	        raw_paths.extend(
   177	            line.strip() for line in files_from.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
   178	            if line.strip()
   179	        )
   180	
   181	    files: set[Path] = set()
   182	    for raw_path in raw_paths:
   183	        candidate = Path(raw_path)
   184	        if not candidate.is_absolute():
   185	            candidate = root / candidate
   186	        candidate = candidate.resolve(strict=False)
   187	        if not _inside_root(candidate, root):
   188	            raise ValueError(f"input path escapes repository root: {raw_path}")
   189	        if candidate.is_dir():
   190	            files.update(path for path in candidate.rglob("*") if path.is_file())
   191	        elif candidate.is_file():
   192	            files.add(candidate)
   193	        # Deleted paths from a changed-file list are intentionally ignored.
   194	    return sorted(files)

   197	def find_citation_uses(
   198	    files: list[Path], root: Path, index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]]
   199	) -> tuple[list[CitationUse], list[CitationUse]]:
   200	    """Find resolvable label tokens and unknown blueprint-label tokens."""
   201	
   202	    uses: set[CitationUse] = set()
   203	    unknown: set[CitationUse] = set()
   204	    for path in files:
   205	        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
   206	        rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
   207	        for match in CODE_LABEL_RE.finditer(text):
   208	            label = match.group("label")
   209	            if label in index:
   210	                uses.add(CitationUse(label, rel_path, text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1))
   211	            elif ":" in label:
   212	                unknown.add(
   213	                    CitationUse(label, rel_path, text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1)
   214	                )
   215	        for match in CANONICAL_CITATION_RE.finditer(text):
   216	            label = match.group("label")
   217	            if label not in index:
   218	                unknown.add(
   219	                    CitationUse(label, rel_path, text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1)
   220	                )
   221	    return sorted(uses, key=lambda use: (use.label, use.path, use.line)), sorted(
   222	        unknown, key=lambda use: (use.label, use.path, use.line)
   223	    )

   226	def _format_resolutions(
   227	    labels: list[str],
   228	    origins: dict[str, list[CitationUse]],
   229	    index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]],
   230	    output_format: str,
   231	) -> tuple[str, bool]:
   232	    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   233	    failed = False
   234	    for label in labels:
   235	        locations = index.get(label, [])
   236	        if len(locations) != 1:
   237	            failed = True
   238	        rows.append({
   239	            "label": label,
   240	            "locations": [location.locator for location in locations],
   241	            "cited_at": [f"{use.path}:{use.line}" for use in origins.get(label, [])],
   242	        })
   243	
   244	    if output_format == "json":
   245	        return json.dumps(rows, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", failed
   246	
   247	    if output_format == "plain":
   248	        rendered = []
   249	        for row in rows:
   250	            locations = row["locations"]
   251	            value = ", ".join(locations) if locations else "UNRESOLVED"
   252	            rendered.append(f"{row['label']}\t{value}")
   253	        return "\n".join(rendered) + ("\n" if rendered else ""), failed
   254	
   255	    rendered = [
   256	        "# Resolved blueprint citations",
   257	        "",
   258	        "Numeric spans below are derived from durable labels; they are not stored citations.",
   259	        "",
   260	    ]
   261	    if not rows:
   262	        rendered.append("_No blueprint labels were found in the selected files._")
   263	    for row in rows:
   264	        locations = row["locations"]
   265	        location_text = ", ".join(f"`{item}`" for item in locations) or "**UNRESOLVED**"
   266	        origin_text = row["cited_at"]
   267	        suffix = ""
   268	        if origin_text:
   269	            suffix = "; cited at " + ", ".join(f"`{item}`" for item in origin_text)
   270	        rendered.append(f"- `{row['label']}` -> {location_text}{suffix}")
   271	    return "\n".join(rendered) + "\n", failed

   274	def _comment_bounds(text: str, position: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
   275	    start = text.rfind("/-", 0, position)
   276	    end = text.find("-/", position)
   277	    if start >= 0 and end >= 0:
   278	        return start, end + 2
   279	    line_start = text.rfind("\n", 0, position) + 1
   280	    line_end = text.find("\n", position)
   281	    return line_start, len(text) if line_end < 0 else line_end

   284	def _candidate_for_locator(
   285	    text: str,
   286	    match: re.Match[str],
   287	    index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]],
   288	) -> str | None:
   289	    # One label cannot faithfully replace a locator that deliberately names
   290	    # several disjoint spans. Such citations require a manual label list.
   291	    if match.group("extra"):
   292	        return None
   293	
   294	    target_name = Path(match.group("path")).name
   295	    old_start = int(match.group("start"))
   296	    old_end = int(match.group("end") or match.group("start"))
   297	    exact = [
   298	        label
   299	        for label, locations in index.items()
   300	        if len(locations) == 1
   301	        and Path(locations[0].path).name == target_name
   302	        and (locations[0].start, locations[0].end) == (old_start, old_end)
   303	    ]
   304	    if exact:
   305	        return exact[0] if len(exact) == 1 else None
   306	
   307	    block_start, block_end = _comment_bounds(text, match.start())
   308	    block = text[block_start:block_end]
   309	    candidates: dict[str, list[re.Match[str]]] = {}
   310	    for label_match in CODE_LABEL_RE.finditer(block):
   311	        label = label_match.group("label")
   312	        locations = index.get(label, [])
   313	        if len(locations) != 1 or Path(locations[0].path).name != target_name:
   314	            continue
   315	        candidates.setdefault(label, []).append(label_match)
   316	
   317	    if candidates:
   318	        linked: set[str] = set()
   319	        relative_start = match.start() - block_start
   320	        relative_end = match.end() - block_start
   321	        for label, label_matches in candidates.items():
   322	            for label_match in label_matches:
   323	                if label_match.end() <= relative_start:
   324	                    between = block[label_match.end():relative_start]
   325	                    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*\(\s*|\s*[,;]\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+", between):
   326	                        linked.add(label)
   327	                elif label_match.start() >= relative_end:
   328	                    between = block[relative_end:label_match.start()]
   329	                    after = block[label_match.end():]
   330	                    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*\(\s*", between) and re.match(r"\s*\)", after):
   331	                        linked.add(label)
   332	        return next(iter(linked)) if len(linked) == 1 else None
   333	
   334	    return None
   335

   337	def _wrap_blueprint_citation_lines(text: str) -> str:
   338	    """Wrap generated blueprint-citation prose at the Lean line limit."""
   339	
   340	    wrapped: list[str] = []
   341	    for raw_line in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
   342	        ending = "\n" if raw_line.endswith("\n") else ""
   343	        line = raw_line[:-1] if ending else raw_line
   344	        if (len(line) <= LEAN_LINE_WIDTH
   345	                or not re.search(r"\b[Bb]lueprint\b", line)
   346	                or CODE_LABEL_RE.search(line) is None):
   347	            wrapped.append(raw_line)
   348	            continue
   349	        indent = line[:len(line) - len(line.lstrip())]
   350	        current = line
   351	        while len(current) > LEAN_LINE_WIDTH:
   352	            split_at = current.rfind(" ", len(indent) + 1, LEAN_LINE_WIDTH + 1)
   353	            if split_at < 0:
   354	                break
   355	            wrapped.append(current[:split_at].rstrip() + "\n")
   356	            current = indent + current[split_at + 1:].lstrip()
   357	        wrapped.append(current + ending)
   358	    return "".join(wrapped)

   361	def rewrite_text(
   362	    text: str, index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]]
   363	) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
   364	    """Rewrite unambiguous legacy locators and return unresolved locator text."""
   365	
   366	    replacements: list[tuple[int, int, str]] = []
   367	    unresolved: list[str] = []
   368	    for match in LEGACY_LOCATOR_RE.finditer(text):
   369	        label = _candidate_for_locator(text, match, index)
   370	        if label is None:
   371	            unresolved.append(match.group(0))
   372	            continue
   373	        replacements.append((match.start(), match.end(), f"`{label}`"))
   374	
   375	    rewritten = text
   376	    for start, end, replacement in reversed(replacements):
   377	        rewritten = rewritten[:start] + replacement + rewritten[end:]
   378	
   379	    # Collapse the common legacy wording after the locator itself is replaced.
   380	    def collapse_duplicate(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
   381	        link = match.group("link")
   382	        label = match.group("label")
   383	        if "\n" not in link:
   384	            return f"blueprint `{label}`"
   385	        indent_match = re.search(r"\n(?P<indent>[ \t]*)", link)
   386	        indent = indent_match.group("indent") if indent_match else ""
   387	        return f"blueprint\n{indent}`{label}`"
   388	
   389	    rewritten = re.sub(
   390	        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`"
   391	        r"(?P<link>,\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+|;\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+|\s+in\s+)"
   392	        r"`(?P=label)`",
   393	        collapse_duplicate,
   394	        rewritten,
   395	    )
   396	    rewritten = re.sub(
   397	        r"(?P<prefix>\b[Bb]lueprint\s+)"
   398	        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`\s*[,;]\s*`(?P=label)`",
   399	        lambda match: f"{match.group('prefix')}`{match.group('label')}`",
   400	        rewritten,
   401	    )
   402	    def collapse_parenthetical(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
   403	        label = match.group("label")
   404	        whitespace = match.group("whitespace")
   405	        if "\n" not in whitespace:
   406	            return f"blueprint `{label}`"
   407	        indent_match = re.search(r"\n(?P<indent>[ \t]*)", whitespace)
   408	        indent = indent_match.group("indent") if indent_match else ""
   409	        return f"blueprint\n{indent}`{label}`"
   410	
   411	    rewritten = re.sub(
   412	        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`\s*"
   413	        r"(?P<whitespace>\(\s*)`(?P=label)`\s*\)",
   414	        collapse_parenthetical,
   415	        rewritten,
   416	    )
   417	    return _wrap_blueprint_citation_lines(rewritten), unresolved
   418

   420	def _resolve_command(args: argparse.Namespace, root: Path) -> int:
   421	    index = build_label_index(root)
   422	    files = collect_input_files(root, args.paths, args.files_from)
   423	    uses, unknown = find_citation_uses(files, root, index)
   424	    labels = list(args.labels)
   425	    origins: dict[str, list[CitationUse]] = {}
   426	    for use in uses:
   427	        if use.label not in labels:
   428	            labels.append(use.label)
   429	        origins.setdefault(use.label, []).append(use)
   430	    for use in unknown:
   431	        if use.label not in labels:
   432	            labels.append(use.label)
   433	        origins.setdefault(use.label, []).append(use)
   434	    rendered, failed = _format_resolutions(labels, origins, index, args.format)
   435	    sys.stdout.write(rendered)
   436	    return 1 if failed else 0
   437	
   438	
   439	def _rewrite_command(args: argparse.Namespace, root: Path) -> int:
   440	    index = build_label_index(root)
   441	    files = collect_input_files(root, args.paths, args.files_from)
   442	    changes: list[tuple[Path, str, str]] = []
   443	    unresolved: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []
   444	    for path in files:
   445	        old = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
   446	        new, missing = rewrite_text(old, index)
   447	        if old != new:
   448	            changes.append((path, old, new))
   449	        unresolved.extend((path, locator) for locator in missing)
   450	
   451	    for path, locator in unresolved:
   452	        rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
   453	        print(f"unresolved: {rel_path}: {locator}", file=sys.stderr)
   454	    if unresolved and not args.allow_unresolved:
   455	        print("refusing partial rewrite; pass --allow-unresolved to rewrite safe matches",
   456	              file=sys.stderr)
   457	        return 1
   458	
   459	    if args.write:
   460	        for path, _old, new in changes:
   461	            path.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8")
   462	    else:
   463	        for path, old, new in changes:
   464	            rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
   465	            sys.stdout.writelines(difflib.unified_diff(
   466	                old.splitlines(keepends=True),
   467	                new.splitlines(keepends=True),
   468	                fromfile=rel_path,
   469	                tofile=rel_path,
   470	            ))
   471	    action = "rewrote" if args.write else "would rewrite"
   472	    print(f"{action} {len(changes)} file(s); {len(unresolved)} unresolved locator(s)",
   473	          file=sys.stderr)
   474	    return 0
   475	
   476	
   477	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   478	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
   479	    parser.add_argument(
   480	        "--root",
   481	        type=Path,
   482	        default=Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent,
   483	        help="repository root (default: parent of scripts/)",
   484	    )
   485	    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
   486	
   487	    resolve = subparsers.add_parser("resolve", help="resolve labels to current spans")
   488	    resolve.add_argument("labels", nargs="*", help="blueprint labels to resolve")
   489	    resolve.add_argument("--path", dest="paths", action="append", default=[],
   490	                         help="scan a repository file or directory for label tokens")
   491	    resolve.add_argument("--files-from", type=Path,
   492	                         help="scan repository paths listed one per line")
   493	    resolve.add_argument("--format", choices=("markdown", "plain", "json"),
   494	                         default="plain")
   495	
   496	    rewrite = subparsers.add_parser("rewrite", help="replace unambiguous legacy locators")
   497	    rewrite.add_argument("paths", nargs="*", help="repository files or directories to rewrite")
   498	    rewrite.add_argument("--files-from", type=Path,
   499	                         help="rewrite repository paths listed one per line")
   500	    rewrite.add_argument("--write", action="store_true",
   501	                         help="write changes in place (default: print a diff)")
   502	    rewrite.add_argument("--allow-unresolved", action="store_true",
   503	                         help="rewrite safe matches while reporting unresolved locators")
   504	
   505	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
   506	    root = args.root.resolve()
   507	    try:
   508	        if args.command == "resolve":
   509	            return _resolve_command(args, root)
   510	        return _rewrite_command(args, root)
   511	    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
   512	        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
   513	        return 2
   514	
   515	
   516	if __name__ == "__main__":
   517	    raise SystemExit(main())

     3	# review.sh — model-backed review of a GitHub PR, chained after a green CI.
     4	#
     5	# Usage:
     6	#   local/bin/review.sh <pr-number> [--force-review] [--dry-run]

     8	#   <pr-number>      GitHub PR number ("12").  Branch, base and head SHA come

    10	#                    exactly the GitHub head before anything is reviewed.
    11	#   --force-review   Review even when the head commit is a bot fix commit.
    12	#                    Used by autofix.sh for the single forced review at the
    13	#                    iteration cap (local/protocols/autofix.md).
    14	#   --dry-run        Resolve the worktree, diff and prompts, print where they
    15	#                    landed, and stop before dispatching an agent.
    16	#
    17	# Local replacement for .github/workflows/pr-review.yml (gate + code-review +
    18	# prose-review jobs).  Protocol: local/protocols/review.md.
    19	#
    20	# GitHub is the record (gh_common.py:4-8).  The gate reads the local-ci/summary
    21	# commit status on the exact head SHA; the verdict is published as ONE COMMENT
    22	# review bound to that SHA plus a local-review/summary status.  Single-account
    23	# repos cannot self-APPROVE, so adverseness travels in the status, never in a
    24	# review state.  There is no local PR record: a GitHub failure fails this
    25	# script closed rather than leaving a fallback record behind.
    26	#
    27	# Exit codes:
    28	#   0  review published, or an intentional skip (kill switch, bot commit, stale
    29	#      head, empty diff)
    30	#   1  usage or environment error
    31	#   3  gate blocked: local-ci/summary is not success for the head SHA.  Nothing
    32	#      is published — the absence of a green local-review/summary is the block.
    33	#   4  the reviewer returned no machine-parseable verdict trailer.  A failing
    34	#      local-review/summary is posted so the PR never reads as green.

   149	# sanitize_to <src> <dest> <max-lines> [max-bytes] — control-char strip, fence
   150	# breaking, and bounded output (DESIGN.md invariant 6).  A zero bound disables
   151	# that dimension. dispatch.sh sanitizes attachments again; this copy also
   152	# protects the no-dispatcher fallback path.
   153	sanitize_to() {
   154	  python3 - "$1" "$2" "$3" "${4:-0}" <<'PY'
   155	import sys
   156	src, dest = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   157	max_lines, max_bytes = int(sys.argv[3]), int(sys.argv[4])
   158	try:
   159	    raw = open(src, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
   160	except OSError:
   161	    raw = ""
   162	raw = raw.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")
   163	keep = []
   164	for ch in raw:
   165	    o = ord(ch)
   166	    if ch in "\n\t" or (32 <= o < 127) or o > 159:
   167	        keep.append(ch)
   168	lines = "".join(keep).split("\n")
   169	truncated = 0
   170	if max_lines > 0 and len(lines) > max_lines:
   171	    truncated = len(lines) - max_lines
   172	    lines = lines[:max_lines]
   173	out = []
   174	for line in lines:
   175	    line = line.replace("```", "'''").replace("~~~", "'''")
   176	    if line.startswith("<<<") or line.startswith("# Task"):
   177	        line = " " + line
   178	    out.append(line)
   179	if truncated:
   180	    out.append("... [%d further lines omitted by review.sh; full text on disk]"
   181	               % truncated)
   182	rendered = "\n".join(out) + "\n"
   183	encoded = rendered.encode("utf-8")
   184	if max_bytes > 0 and len(encoded) > max_bytes:
   185	    marker = b"\n... [truncated by review.sh attachment budget; full text on disk]\n"
   186	    keep_bytes = max(0, max_bytes - len(marker))
   187	    prefix = encoded[:keep_bytes].decode("utf-8", errors="ignore").rstrip()
   188	    rendered = prefix + marker.decode("ascii")
   189	open(dest, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(rendered)
   190	PY
   191	}

   193	# acquire_lock <lockdir> <wait-seconds> <label>
   194	# Per-PR review lock.  No cancellation: a queued review waits and then
   195	# re-checks the head SHA (pr-review.yml:18-20, cancel-in-progress false).
   196	acquire_lock() {
   197	  local dir="$1" wait_s="$2" label="$3" waited=0 holder=""
   198	  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dir")"
   199	  while ! mkdir "$dir" 2>/dev/null; do
   200	    holder="$(cat "$dir/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   201	    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
   202	      warn "removing stale lock $dir (holder pid $holder is gone)"
   203	      rm -rf "$dir"
   204	      continue
   205	    fi
   206	    if [ "$waited" -ge "$wait_s" ]; then
   207	      die "timed out after ${wait_s}s waiting for the review lock $dir (holder pid ${holder:-unknown})"
   208	    fi
   209	    [ "$waited" = 0 ] && log "another review holds $dir (pid ${holder:-unknown}); queuing"
   210	    sleep 5
   211	    waited=$((waited + 5))
   212	  done
   213	  printf '%s\n' "$$" >"$dir/pid"
   214	  printf '%s\n' "$label" >"$dir/label"
   215	  LOCK_HELD="$dir"
   216	}

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Resolve durable blueprint labels and migrate legacy numeric locators.
+
+Lean docstrings should store blueprint labels, not line ranges.  This helper
+derives the current source span of each label from ``blueprint/src/chapter``.
+It can also conservatively rewrite old ``chNN_*.tex:START-END`` citations when
+the span exactly identifies a node or the surrounding syntax pairs it with one
+unambiguous label from that chapter.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import difflib
+import json
+import re
+import sys
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from tex_utils import strip_tex_comment
+
+
+TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"\\(?P<kind>begin|end|label)\{(?P<value>[^}]+)\}")
+CODE_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`")
+CANONICAL_CITATION_RE = re.compile(
+    r"\b[Bb]lueprint(?:\s+(?:node|nodes|label|labels|entry|entries))?\s+"
+    r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`"
+)
+LEGACY_LOCATOR_RE = re.compile(
+    r"`(?P<path>(?:blueprint/src/chapter/)?ch[0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*\.tex):"
+    r"(?P<start>[0-9]+)(?:(?P<dash>--|-|\u2013|\u2014)(?P<end>[0-9]+))?"
+    r"(?P<extra>(?:,[0-9]+(?:--|-|\u2013|\u2014)[0-9]+)*)`"
+)
+STATEMENT_ENVS = {
+    "definition",
+    "theorem",
+    "lemma",
+    "proposition",
+    "corollary",
+    "remark",
+    "example",
+}
+LEAN_LINE_WIDTH = 100
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class EnvironmentSpan:
+    """One balanced TeX environment."""
+
+    name: str
+    start: int
+    end: int
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class LabelLocation:
+    """The current source span anchored by one active ``\\label``."""
+
+    label: str
+    path: str
+    label_line: int
+    start: int
+    end: int
+
+    @property
+    def locator(self) -> str:
+        suffix = str(self.start) if self.start == self.end else f"{self.start}-{self.end}"
+        return f"{self.path}:{suffix}"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class CitationUse:
+    """A label token found in a file that a reviewer will inspect."""
+
+    label: str
+    path: str
+    line: int
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _OpenEnvironment:
+    name: str
+    start: int
+
+
+def _active_lines(path: Path) -> list[str]:
+    return [strip_tex_comment(line) for line in path.read_text(
+        encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"
+    ).splitlines()]
+
+
+def _parse_tex_file(path: Path, root: Path) -> list[LabelLocation]:
+    """Return active labels in *path*, with enclosing statement/proof spans."""
+
+    lines = _active_lines(path)
+    stack: list[_OpenEnvironment] = []
+    environments: list[EnvironmentSpan] = []
+    labels: list[tuple[str, int]] = []
+
+    for line_no, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
+        for token in TOKEN_RE.finditer(line):
+            kind = token.group("kind")
+            value = token.group("value")
+            if kind == "begin":
+                stack.append(_OpenEnvironment(value, line_no))
+            elif kind == "label":
+                labels.append((value, line_no))
+            else:
+                match_at = next(
+                    (index for index in range(len(stack) - 1, -1, -1)
+                     if stack[index].name == value),
+                    None,
+                )
+                if match_at is None:
+                    continue
+                opened = stack[match_at]
+                del stack[match_at:]
+                environments.append(EnvironmentSpan(value, opened.start, line_no))
+
+    environments.sort(key=lambda span: (span.start, span.end - span.start))
+    proof_spans = [span for span in environments if span.name == "proof"]
+    rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+    locations: list[LabelLocation] = []
+
+    for label, label_line in labels:
+        enclosing = [
+            span for span in environments
+            if span.start <= label_line <= span.end
+        ]
+        if enclosing:
+            span = min(enclosing, key=lambda item: (item.end - item.start, -item.start))
+            start, end = span.start, span.end
+            if span.name in STATEMENT_ENVS:
+                following = next(
+                    (proof for proof in proof_spans if proof.start > span.end),
+                    None,
+                )
+                if following is not None:
+                    gap = lines[span.end:following.start - 1]
+                    if all(not item.strip() for item in gap):
+                        end = following.end
+        else:
+            start = end = label_line
+        locations.append(LabelLocation(label, rel_path, label_line, start, end))
+
+    return locations
+
+
+def build_label_index(root: Path) -> dict[str, list[LabelLocation]]:
+    """Index active blueprint labels below ``root/blueprint/src/chapter``."""
+
+    chapter_root = root / "blueprint" / "src" / "chapter"
+    if not chapter_root.is_dir():
+        raise ValueError(f"blueprint chapter directory does not exist: {chapter_root}")
+    index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]] = {}
+    for path in sorted(chapter_root.rglob("*.tex")):
+        for location in _parse_tex_file(path, root):
+            index.setdefault(location.label, []).append(location)
+    return index
+
+
+def _inside_root(path: Path, root: Path) -> bool:
+    try:
+        path.relative_to(root)
+    except ValueError:
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def collect_input_files(root: Path, paths: list[str], files_from: Path | None) -> list[Path]:
+    """Resolve explicit repository paths without permitting traversal."""
+
+    raw_paths = list(paths)
+    if files_from is not None:
+        raw_paths.extend(
+            line.strip() for line in files_from.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
+            if line.strip()
+        )
+
+    files: set[Path] = set()
+    for raw_path in raw_paths:
+        candidate = Path(raw_path)
+        if not candidate.is_absolute():
+            candidate = root / candidate
+        candidate = candidate.resolve(strict=False)
+        if not _inside_root(candidate, root):
+            raise ValueError(f"input path escapes repository root: {raw_path}")
+        if candidate.is_dir():
+            files.update(path for path in candidate.rglob("*") if path.is_file())
+        elif candidate.is_file():
+            files.add(candidate)
+        # Deleted paths from a changed-file list are intentionally ignored.
+    return sorted(files)
+
+
+def find_citation_uses(
+    files: list[Path], root: Path, index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]]
+) -> tuple[list[CitationUse], list[CitationUse]]:
+    """Find resolvable label tokens and unknown blueprint-label tokens."""
+
+    uses: set[CitationUse] = set()
+    unknown: set[CitationUse] = set()
+    for path in files:
+        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
+        rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+        for match in CODE_LABEL_RE.finditer(text):
+            label = match.group("label")
+            if label in index:
+                uses.add(CitationUse(label, rel_path, text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1))
+            elif ":" in label:
+                unknown.add(
+                    CitationUse(label, rel_path, text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1)
+                )
+        for match in CANONICAL_CITATION_RE.finditer(text):
+            label = match.group("label")
+            if label not in index:
+                unknown.add(
+                    CitationUse(label, rel_path, text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1)
+                )
+    return sorted(uses, key=lambda use: (use.label, use.path, use.line)), sorted(
+        unknown, key=lambda use: (use.label, use.path, use.line)
+    )
+
+
+def _format_resolutions(
+    labels: list[str],
+    origins: dict[str, list[CitationUse]],
+    index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]],
+    output_format: str,
+) -> tuple[str, bool]:
+    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
+    failed = False
+    for label in labels:
+        locations = index.get(label, [])
+        if len(locations) != 1:
+            failed = True
+        rows.append({
+            "label": label,
+            "locations": [location.locator for location in locations],
+            "cited_at": [f"{use.path}:{use.line}" for use in origins.get(label, [])],
+        })
+
+    if output_format == "json":
+        return json.dumps(rows, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", failed
+
+    if output_format == "plain":
+        rendered = []
+        for row in rows:
+            locations = row["locations"]
+            value = ", ".join(locations) if locations else "UNRESOLVED"
+            rendered.append(f"{row['label']}\t{value}")
+        return "\n".join(rendered) + ("\n" if rendered else ""), failed
+
+    rendered = [
+        "# Resolved blueprint citations",
+        "",
+        "Numeric spans below are derived from durable labels; they are not stored citations.",
+        "",
+    ]
+    if not rows:
+        rendered.append("_No blueprint labels were found in the selected files._")
+    for row in rows:
+        locations = row["locations"]
+        location_text = ", ".join(f"`{item}`" for item in locations) or "**UNRESOLVED**"
+        origin_text = row["cited_at"]
+        suffix = ""
+        if origin_text:
+            suffix = "; cited at " + ", ".join(f"`{item}`" for item in origin_text)
+        rendered.append(f"- `{row['label']}` -> {location_text}{suffix}")
+    return "\n".join(rendered) + "\n", failed
+
+
+def _comment_bounds(text: str, position: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    start = text.rfind("/-", 0, position)
+    end = text.find("-/", position)
+    if start >= 0 and end >= 0:
+        return start, end + 2
+    line_start = text.rfind("\n", 0, position) + 1
+    line_end = text.find("\n", position)
+    return line_start, len(text) if line_end < 0 else line_end
+
+
+def _candidate_for_locator(
+    text: str,
+    match: re.Match[str],
+    index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]],
+) -> str | None:
+    # One label cannot faithfully replace a locator that deliberately names
+    # several disjoint spans. Such citations require a manual label list.
+    if match.group("extra"):
+        return None
+
+    target_name = Path(match.group("path")).name
+    old_start = int(match.group("start"))
+    old_end = int(match.group("end") or match.group("start"))
+    exact = [
+        label
+        for label, locations in index.items()
+        if len(locations) == 1
+        and Path(locations[0].path).name == target_name
+        and (locations[0].start, locations[0].end) == (old_start, old_end)
+    ]
+    if exact:
+        return exact[0] if len(exact) == 1 else None
+
+    block_start, block_end = _comment_bounds(text, match.start())
+    block = text[block_start:block_end]
+    candidates: dict[str, list[re.Match[str]]] = {}
+    for label_match in CODE_LABEL_RE.finditer(block):
+        label = label_match.group("label")
+        locations = index.get(label, [])
+        if len(locations) != 1 or Path(locations[0].path).name != target_name:
+            continue
+        candidates.setdefault(label, []).append(label_match)
+
+    if candidates:
+        linked: set[str] = set()
+        relative_start = match.start() - block_start
+        relative_end = match.end() - block_start
+        for label, label_matches in candidates.items():
+            for label_match in label_matches:
+                if label_match.end() <= relative_start:
+                    between = block[label_match.end():relative_start]
+                    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*\(\s*|\s*[,;]\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+", between):
+                        linked.add(label)
+                elif label_match.start() >= relative_end:
+                    between = block[relative_end:label_match.start()]
+                    after = block[label_match.end():]
+                    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*\(\s*", between) and re.match(r"\s*\)", after):
+                        linked.add(label)
+        return next(iter(linked)) if len(linked) == 1 else None
+
+    return None
+
+
+def _wrap_blueprint_citation_lines(text: str) -> str:
+    """Wrap generated blueprint-citation prose at the Lean line limit."""
+
+    wrapped: list[str] = []
+    for raw_line in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
+        ending = "\n" if raw_line.endswith("\n") else ""
+        line = raw_line[:-1] if ending else raw_line
+        if (len(line) <= LEAN_LINE_WIDTH
+                or not re.search(r"\b[Bb]lueprint\b", line)
+                or CODE_LABEL_RE.search(line) is None):
+            wrapped.append(raw_line)
+            continue
+        indent = line[:len(line) - len(line.lstrip())]
+        current = line
+        while len(current) > LEAN_LINE_WIDTH:
+            split_at = current.rfind(" ", len(indent) + 1, LEAN_LINE_WIDTH + 1)
+            if split_at < 0:
+                break
+            wrapped.append(current[:split_at].rstrip() + "\n")
+            current = indent + current[split_at + 1:].lstrip()
+        wrapped.append(current + ending)
+    return "".join(wrapped)
+
+
+def rewrite_text(
+    text: str, index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]]
+) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
+    """Rewrite unambiguous legacy locators and return unresolved locator text."""
+
+    replacements: list[tuple[int, int, str]] = []
+    unresolved: list[str] = []
+    for match in LEGACY_LOCATOR_RE.finditer(text):
+        label = _candidate_for_locator(text, match, index)
+        if label is None:
+            unresolved.append(match.group(0))
+            continue
+        replacements.append((match.start(), match.end(), f"`{label}`"))
+
+    rewritten = text
+    for start, end, replacement in reversed(replacements):
+        rewritten = rewritten[:start] + replacement + rewritten[end:]
+
+    # Collapse the common legacy wording after the locator itself is replaced.
+    def collapse_duplicate(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
+        link = match.group("link")
+        label = match.group("label")
+        if "\n" not in link:
+            return f"blueprint `{label}`"
+        indent_match = re.search(r"\n(?P<indent>[ \t]*)", link)
+        indent = indent_match.group("indent") if indent_match else ""
+        return f"blueprint\n{indent}`{label}`"
+
+    rewritten = re.sub(
+        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`"
+        r"(?P<link>,\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+|;\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+|\s+in\s+)"
+        r"`(?P=label)`",
+        collapse_duplicate,
+        rewritten,
+    )
+    rewritten = re.sub(
+        r"(?P<prefix>\b[Bb]lueprint\s+)"
+        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`\s*[,;]\s*`(?P=label)`",
+        lambda match: f"{match.group('prefix')}`{match.group('label')}`",
+        rewritten,
+    )
+    def collapse_parenthetical(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
+        label = match.group("label")
+        whitespace = match.group("whitespace")
+        if "\n" not in whitespace:
+            return f"blueprint `{label}`"
+        indent_match = re.search(r"\n(?P<indent>[ \t]*)", whitespace)
+        indent = indent_match.group("indent") if indent_match else ""
+        return f"blueprint\n{indent}`{label}`"
+
+    rewritten = re.sub(
+        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`\s*"
+        r"(?P<whitespace>\(\s*)`(?P=label)`\s*\)",
+        collapse_parenthetical,
+        rewritten,
+    )
+    return _wrap_blueprint_citation_lines(rewritten), unresolved
+
+
+def _resolve_command(args: argparse.Namespace, root: Path) -> int:
+    index = build_label_index(root)
+    files = collect_input_files(root, args.paths, args.files_from)
+    uses, unknown = find_citation_uses(files, root, index)
+    labels = list(args.labels)
+    origins: dict[str, list[CitationUse]] = {}
+    for use in uses:
+        if use.label not in labels:
+            labels.append(use.label)
+        origins.setdefault(use.label, []).append(use)
+    for use in unknown:
+        if use.label not in labels:
+            labels.append(use.label)
+        origins.setdefault(use.label, []).append(use)
+    rendered, failed = _format_resolutions(labels, origins, index, args.format)
+    sys.stdout.write(rendered)
+    return 1 if failed else 0
+
+
+def _rewrite_command(args: argparse.Namespace, root: Path) -> int:
+    index = build_label_index(root)
+    files = collect_input_files(root, args.paths, args.files_from)
+    changes: list[tuple[Path, str, str]] = []
+    unresolved: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []
+    for path in files:
+        old = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
+        new, missing = rewrite_text(old, index)
+        if old != new:
+            changes.append((path, old, new))
+        unresolved.extend((path, locator) for locator in missing)
+
+    for path, locator in unresolved:
+        rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+        print(f"unresolved: {rel_path}: {locator}", file=sys.stderr)
+    if unresolved and not args.allow_unresolved:
+        print("refusing partial rewrite; pass --allow-unresolved to rewrite safe matches",
+              file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+
+    if args.write:
+        for path, _old, new in changes:
+            path.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8")
+    else:
+        for path, old, new in changes:
+            rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+            sys.stdout.writelines(difflib.unified_diff(
+                old.splitlines(keepends=True),
+                new.splitlines(keepends=True),
+                fromfile=rel_path,
+                tofile=rel_path,
+            ))
+    action = "rewrote" if args.write else "would rewrite"
+    print(f"{action} {len(changes)} file(s); {len(unresolved)} unresolved locator(s)",
+          file=sys.stderr)
+    return 0
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--root",
+        type=Path,
+        default=Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent,
+        help="repository root (default: parent of scripts/)",
+    )
+    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
+
+    resolve = subparsers.add_parser("resolve", help="resolve labels to current spans")
+    resolve.add_argument("labels", nargs="*", help="blueprint labels to resolve")
+    resolve.add_argument("--path", dest="paths", action="append", default=[],
+                         help="scan a repository file or directory for label tokens")
+    resolve.add_argument("--files-from", type=Path,
+                         help="scan repository paths listed one per line")
+    resolve.add_argument("--format", choices=("markdown", "plain", "json"),
+                         default="plain")
+
+    rewrite = subparsers.add_parser("rewrite", help="replace unambiguous legacy locators")
+    rewrite.add_argument("paths", nargs="*", help="repository files or directories to rewrite")
+    rewrite.add_argument("--files-from", type=Path,
+                         help="rewrite repository paths listed one per line")
+    rewrite.add_argument("--write", action="store_true",
+                         help="write changes in place (default: print a diff)")
+    rewrite.add_argument("--allow-unresolved", action="store_true",
+                         help="rewrite safe matches while reporting unresolved locators")
+
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    root = args.root.resolve()
+    try:
+        if args.command == "resolve":
+            return _resolve_command(args, root)
+        return _rewrite_command(args, root)
+    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
+        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

1	"""Shared helpers for parsing active TeX source lines."""
     2	
     3	from __future__ import annotations
     4	
     5	
     6	def strip_tex_comment(line: str) -> str:
     7	    r"""Return the active TeX prefix before the first unescaped ``%``.
     8	
     9	    TeX comments start at an unescaped percent sign. A percent sign preceded
    10	    by an odd-length run of backslashes is the literal ``\%`` token and must
    11	    not truncate the line; an even-length run leaves the ``%`` unescaped.
    12	    """
    13	
    14	    for idx, char in enumerate(line):
    15	        if char != "%":
    16	            continue
    17	        backslashes = 0
    18	        j = idx - 1
    19	        while j >= 0 and line[j] == "\\":
    20	            backslashes += 1
    21	            j -= 1
    22	        if backslashes % 2 == 0:
    23	            return line[:idx]
    24	    return line

+`scripts/blueprint_citations.py` and its TeX helper from the committed trusted
+ref, applies them to the reviewed worktree as untrusted data, and attaches

+attachment budget; the direct-execution fallback receives this same bounded
+artifact rather than the raw resolver output.

/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess,re,sys,difflib
sys.path.insert(0,'scripts')
from blueprint_citations import build_label_index
root=Path('.'); idx=build_label_index(root)
base='8bcb447'; head='8939102'
files=subprocess.check_output(['git','diff','--name-only',base,head],text=True).splitlines()
loc_re=re.compile(r'(?:(?:blueprint/src/chapter/)?(ch[0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*\\.tex)):(\\d+)(?:--|-|–|—)(\\d+)')
label_re=re.compile(r'"'`([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`'"')
for f in files:
 if not f.endswith('.lean'): continue
 try: old=subprocess.check_output(['git','show',f'{base}:{f}'],text=True)
 except: continue
 new=Path(f).read_text(errors='replace')
 # find old lines with locators and approximate changed hunk chunks via SequenceMatcher opcodes
 oldlines=old.splitlines(); newlines=new.splitlines()
 sm=difflib.SequenceMatcher(None,oldlines,newlines,autojunk=False)
 for tag,i1,i2,j1,j2 in sm.get_opcodes():
  if tag=='equal': continue
  och='\\n'.join(oldlines[i1:i2]); nch='\\n'.join(newlines[j1:j2])
  ol=loc_re.findall(och)
  if not ol: continue
  # Include context +/- 8 new lines around hunk to capture labels retained
  ctxt='\\n'.join(newlines[max(0,j1-8):min(len(newlines),j2+8)])
  labs=label_re.findall(ctxt)
  print(f'\\n{f} old {i1+1}-{i2} new {j1+1}-{j2}')
  print(' old locs:',ol)
  print(' new labels:',labs)
  for fn,s,e in ol:

import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Algebra.LowDegreeCodeTheorems
import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.Defs

/-! # Polynomial decoding for Pauli extraction

This module provides the Chapter 16 decoder on the Chapter 15 bounded
polynomial representative type.  The generic retained-value decoder and its
specialization to polynomial representatives live in
`Algebra/LowDegreeCodeTheorems`; this module states the corresponding maps on
`Poly P` used in the extraction chapter.

## References

The decoder is `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:446-457`, with the extraction use
at `blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:11-20` and paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1419-1450`.
The restricted decoder identity and its encoding hypothesis are documented in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

/-! ## Representative evaluation and decoding -/

/-- Evaluate the polynomial representative carried by `Poly P`.

This is polynomial evaluation on the source's `\ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)` carrier.  It
does not identify representatives that induce the same polynomial function. -/
noncomputable def evalPoly {P : AdmissibleParams} (g : Poly P)
    (x : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) : PauliScalar P :=
  MvPolynomial.eval x g.1

/-- Decode a bounded polynomial while retaining only values in `H`.

This is the `H`-parameterized form of `def:decoding-map`; `decodeAt` remains
the decoding map for arbitrary functions.  The Boolean cube is embedded in
`PauliScalar P` by `cubeEmbed`. -/
noncomputable def decodeOn {P : AdmissibleParams}
    (H : Finset (PauliScalar P)) (g : Poly P) : PauliRegister P :=
  decodeAt H (fun x => evalPoly g x)

/-- Full-field specialization of `decodeOn` used in Chapter 16.

The retained-value set is `Finset.univ`, so every field value is kept.  This
choice is the correction recorded in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`. -/
noncomputable abbrev decodeOnUniv {P : AdmissibleParams} (g : Poly P) :
    PauliRegister P :=
  decodeOn (Finset.univ : Finset (PauliScalar P)) g

/-- The full-field decoder `\operatorname{Dec}_{\F_q}` on `Poly P`.

The map `decodeFqRep` has the same definition on arbitrary polynomial
representatives; `decodeFq` restricts its domain to the bounded-degree class
`Poly P`. -/
noncomputable abbrev decodeFq {P : AdmissibleParams} (g : Poly P) :
    PauliRegister P :=
  decodeOnUniv g

/-! ## The encoding image -/

/-- Membership of a multilinear encoding in the bounded representative class.

Each indicator factor has degree zero away from its own variable and degree at
most one in that variable, so the multilinear encoding has individual degree at
most one, and hence at most `P.d` using `P.hd`.  This is the degree
side-condition implicit in the source's `g_h` construction, not an extra
hypothesis of the decoding identity.  See `def:low-degree-encoding`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:404-424`, and paper
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`. -/
theorem lowDegreeEncoding_mem_poly {P : AdmissibleParams}
    (h : PauliRegister P) :
    lowDegreeEncoding h ∈
      MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc P.m (PauliScalar P) P.d := by
  rw [MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree]
  intro s hs i
  apply (MvPolynomial.monomial_le_degreeOf i hs).trans
  rw [lowDegreeEncoding]
  refine (MvPolynomial.degreeOf_sum_le i Finset.univ _).trans ?_
  refine Finset.sup_le fun y _ => ?_
  refine (show MvPolynomial.degreeOf i
      (h y • indicatorPoly (K := PauliScalar P) y) ≤
      MvPolynomial.degreeOf i (indicatorPoly (K := PauliScalar P) y) from ?_).trans ?_
  · simpa only [MvPolynomial.smul_eq_C_mul] using
      MvPolynomial.degreeOf_C_mul_le (indicatorPoly (K := PauliScalar P) y) i (h y)
  rw [indicatorPoly]
  refine (MvPolynomial.degreeOf_prod_le i Finset.univ _).trans ?_
  calc
    ∑ j, MvPolynomial.degreeOf i
        (if y j then
          (MvPolynomial.X j : MvPolynomial (Fin P.m) (PauliScalar P))
        else 1 - MvPolynomial.X j) ≤
        ∑ j, if i = j then 1 else 0 := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro j _
      split
      · exact le_of_eq (MvPolynomial.degreeOf_X i j)
      · exact (MvPolynomial.degreeOf_sub_le i 1 (MvPolynomial.X j)).trans_eq (by
          simp [MvPolynomial.degreeOf_X])
    _ = 1 := by simp
    _ ≤ P.d := P.hd

/-- The multilinear encoding as a bounded polynomial representative.

The individual-degree bound is supplied by `lowDegreeEncoding_mem_poly`. -/
noncomputable def encodingPoly {P : AdmissibleParams} (h : PauliRegister P) :
    Poly P :=
  ⟨lowDegreeEncoding h, lowDegreeEncoding_mem_poly h⟩

/-- A `Poly P` outcome is an encoding when its decoder reconstructs the same
underlying polynomial representative.

This is the explicit support restriction required by the corrected Chapter 16
decoding argument.  It is the `Poly` view of `IsEncodingRep`; no unrestricted
decoder/evaluation identity is asserted.  See
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`. -/
def IsEncoding {P : AdmissibleParams} (g : Poly P) : Prop :=
  lowDegreeEncoding (decodeFq g) = g.1

/-! ## Decoder companions -/

/-- Linearity of the full-field decoder on bounded representatives.

This is the additive linearity of `lem:qld-decoder-linearity`, blueprint
`ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:30-40`, used in the symmetry step of the source
argument at
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1546-1550`
and blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:239-244`.  It does not assert
evaluation equality for non-encoding representatives.  See
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`. -/
theorem decodeFq_add {P : AdmissibleParams} (g h : Poly P) :
    decodeFq (g + h) = decodeFq g + decodeFq h := by
  funext y
  simp [decodeOn, decodeAt, evalPoly, MvPolynomial.eval_add]

/-- Scalar linearity of the full-field decoder on bounded representatives.

This companion has the same source scope as `decodeFq_add` and does not
strengthen the restricted decoder identity.  See
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`. -/
theorem decodeFq_smul {P : AdmissibleParams} (c : PauliScalar P) (g : Poly P) :
    decodeFq (c • g) = c • decodeFq g := by
  funext y
  simp [decodeOn, decodeAt, evalPoly, MvPolynomial.smul_eval]

/-- The full-field decoder is a left inverse to `encodingPoly`.

This is the identity `\operatorname{Dec}(g_h)=h` of
`lem:qld-decoder-linearity`, blueprint `ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:30-40`, for
the full-field decoder specified at
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1419-1420`.
The degree proof is separated into `lowDegreeEncoding_mem_poly`; no additional
encoding or interpolation hypothesis is introduced.  See
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`. -/
theorem decodeFq_lowDegreeEncoding {P : AdmissibleParams}
    (h : PauliRegister P) :
    decodeFq (encodingPoly h) = h := by
  funext y
  simpa only [decodeFq, decodeOnUniv, decodeOn, decodeAt, evalPoly,
    encodingPoly, lowDegreeEnc, Finset.mem_univ, if_true] using
      congrFun
        (decodeAt_lowDegreeEnc
          (Finset.univ : Finset (PauliScalar P)) h
            (fun z => Finset.mem_univ (h z))) y

/-- Decoder/evaluation agreement for an encoding representative only.

The hypothesis `hg : IsEncoding g` is mandatory.  For a general bounded
polynomial, Boolean-cube values determine its multilinear interpolant, which
need not equal the original representative.  This is the corrected form of

`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1483-1492`;

/-- A `Poly P` outcome is an encoding when its decoder reconstructs the same
underlying polynomial representative.

This is the explicit support restriction required by the corrected Chapter 16
decoding argument.  It is the `Poly` view of `IsEncodingRep`; no unrestricted
decoder/evaluation identity is asserted.  See
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`. -/
def IsEncoding {P : AdmissibleParams} (g : Poly P) : Prop :=
  lowDegreeEncoding (decodeFq g) = g.1

/-- Linearity of the full-field decoder on bounded representatives.

This is the additive linearity of blueprint

argument at
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1546-1550`
and blueprint `lem:qld-construct-the-paulis`.  It does not assert
evaluation equality for non-encoding representatives.  See
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`. -/
theorem decodeFq_add {P : AdmissibleParams} (g h : Poly P) :
    decodeFq (g + h) = decodeFq g + decodeFq h := by
  funext y
  simp [decodeOn, decodeAt, evalPoly, MvPolynomial.eval_add]

/-- Scalar linearity of the full-field decoder on bounded representatives.

This companion has the same source scope as `decodeFq_add` and does not
strengthen the restricted decoder identity.  See
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-123`. -/
theorem decodeFq_smul {P : AdmissibleParams} (c : PauliScalar P) (g : Poly P) :
    decodeFq (c • g) = c • decodeFq g := by
  funext y
  simp [decodeOn, decodeAt, evalPoly, MvPolynomial.smul_eval]

loc_re=re.compile(r'(?:(?:blueprint/src/chapter/)?(ch[0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*\\.tex)):(\\d+)(?:--|-|–|—)(\\d+)(?:,["'^`'"\\s]+)?')
lab_re=re.compile(r'"'`([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`'"')
seen=set()
for f in files:
 if not f.endswith('.lean'): continue
 try:o=subprocess.check_output(['git','show',f'{base}:{f}'],text=True)
 except:continue
 n=Path(f).read_text(errors='replace'); ol=o.splitlines(); nl=n.splitlines()
 for tag,i1,i2,j1,j2 in difflib.SequenceMatcher(None,ol,nl,autojunk=False).get_opcodes():
  if tag=='equal':continue
  oldtxt='\\n'.join(ol[i1:i2]); locs=loc_re.findall(oldtxt)

  # labels in all new lines of changed block, known and dedup
  labs=[]

   if key in seen:continue
   seen.add(key)
   desc=[]
   for l in labs:
    desc.append(l+'['+','.join(x.locator.rsplit(':',1)[-1] for x in idx[l])+']')
   print(f'{f}|{fn}:{s}-{e}|{\" \".join(desc) or \"(none)\"}')

# Pauli basis test soundness interface

This module contains the quantitative error function and the closed definitions
used to state Pauli basis test soundness.  The carriers are concrete
finite-dimensional vectors and matrices so that the soundness proof can use the
existing Hilbert-space API without introducing a dependency cycle.

## References

The interface supports `thm:pauli` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`, with paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
The distance functionals use `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` from
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:187-226`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.Quantum

/-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;
the powers are real `rpow`s and the asymptotic constants are absorbed into `a`,
as specified by `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`,
paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
-/
noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))

/-- Monotonicity obligation for adjusting the universal constants in
`deltaQld` on the source parameter domain. This Lean-only helper supports the
enlargement of `a` and shrinkage of `b` for `0 ≤ ε ≤ 1` described in the
Chapter 16 preamble (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:101-104`);
the source makes this constant adjustment at
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1402`. It is not
an additional hypothesis of `thm:pauli` or `lem:qld-4-7`. -/
theorem deltaQld_mono {P : AdmissibleParams} {a a' b b' ε : ℝ}
    (ha0 : 1 ≤ a) (ha : a ≤ a') (hb : b' ≤ b) (hb' : 0 < b')
    (hε0 : 0 ≤ ε) (hε1 : ε ≤ 1) :
    deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ≤ deltaQld a' b' ε P.m P.d P.q := by
  sorry

/-- The ideal auxiliary state `aux ⊗ EPR_q^{⊗M}` in the shuffled register
ordering.  The EPR factor is the concrete `eprState` from
`def:EPR` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:537-547`; paper
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`).

noncomputable def idealState (P : AdmissibleParams)

/-- The numerical admissible Pauli-test parameter package.  Its scalar carrier
uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel q hq`, so the paper's fixed
self-dual-normal identification is not quantified in the test statement.  This
is `def:admissible` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.

structure AdmissibleParams where
  q : ℕ
  m : ℕ
  d : ℕ
  hd : 1 ≤ d
  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
  hdvd : m ∣ q

/-- The positivity of the ambient dimension is a proof obligation implicit in

`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
theorem AdmissibleParams.one_le_m (P : AdmissibleParams) : 1 ≤ P.m := by
  sorry

/-- The fixed model accessor for an admissible parameter package.  It is a
compatibility view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently
quantified field representation.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`; paper
origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
noncomputable def AdmissibleParams.model (P : AdmissibleParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq

/-- The low-degree parameter view of an admissible Pauli-test package.  This is
