audits/2026-03-21_blueprint-maintainability-audit.md:16:The chapter split is mostly sound. I did not find broken `\uses` references, and I did not find a bad ownership choice for the duplicated pasting theorem: the single blueprint node for `thm:ld-pasting` is still safe against the source paper. The main structural problems are dependency bookkeeping, label hygiene, and stale support notes.
audits/2026-03-21_blueprint-maintainability-audit.md:27:- Label prefixes do not match the actual environments. I counted 26 mismatches: 20 `prop:` labels attached to `lemma` environments and 6 `cor:` labels attached to `lemma` environments. Examples include `prop:simeq-for-measurements`, `prop:eigenvectors`, `cor:laplacian-spectral-gap`, and `cor:ld-pasting-N-completeness`. The style guide explicitly asks for label prefixes that match the environment. Right now the label taxonomy is halfway between the source paper and the local blueprint convention.
audits/2026-03-21_blueprint-maintainability-audit.md:31:- The support notes under `docs/` are partly stale relative to the active blueprint. `audits/2026-03-20_ldt-source-map.md` still says the blueprint uses a single `thm:self-improvement` node carrying both Lean links. The active blueprint now has a separate `thm:self-improvement-in-induction-section` node in `ch10_induction.tex`. `audits/2026-03-20_ldt-blueprint-dependency-review.md` still treats the merged self-improvement node and the missing Schwartz–Zippel edge as open problems, but both are already fixed in the active blueprint. That makes the maintenance notes unreliable as a guide to the current state.
audits/2026-03-21_blueprint-maintainability-audit.md:39:- The bibliography is too thin for the prose. `references.bib` has only four entries. The blueprint cites Kempe--Vidick for orthogonalization and Schwartz–Zippel for the polynomial bound, but later chapters use substantial outside material without saying so: the NW19-style measurement-comparison background mirrored by `preliminaries.tex`, the scalar Chernoff input used in `lem:chernoff-bernoulli-matrix`, and the convex-optimization background behind `lem:sdp`.
audits/2026-03-21_blueprint-maintainability-audit.md:47:- Chapter 4 still hides a large amount of proof burden behind `lem:orthonormalization-main-lemma`. The source file `orthonormalization.tex` contains a long internal chain before that lemma closes. As a high-level blueprint this compression is understandable, but it will age badly once real proof filling starts: contributors will underestimate how much work sits behind one node.
audits/2026-03-21_blueprint-maintainability-audit.md:49:- The same risk appears in Chapter 7 and Chapter 9 for `lem:sdp`, `lem:from-H-to-G`, and `lem:chernoff-bernoulli-matrix`. These are not routine one-lemma tasks. If the blueprint keeps them as single nodes, it at least needs explicit citations or an internal checklist so later maintainers know what mathematical subproblems are bundled inside.
audits/2026-03-21_blueprint-maintainability-audit.md:51:- Because many helper nodes inherit hypotheses from a chapter preamble or from `thm:ld-pasting`, small changes to one umbrella hypothesis will force a broad manual audit. That is exactly the kind of hidden coupling that makes blueprints drift.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Resolve durable blueprint labels and migrate legacy numeric locators.
+
+Lean docstrings should store blueprint labels, not line ranges.  This helper
+derives the current source span of each label from ``blueprint/src/chapter``.
+It can also conservatively rewrite old ``chNN_*.tex:START-END`` citations when
+the surrounding comment names one unambiguous label from that chapter.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import difflib
+import json
+import re
+import sys
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from tex_utils import strip_tex_comment
+
+
+TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"\\(?P<kind>begin|end|label)\{(?P<value>[^}]+)\}")
+CODE_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`")
+CANONICAL_CITATION_RE = re.compile(
+    r"\b[Bb]lueprint(?:\s+(?:node|nodes|label|labels|entry|entries))?\s+"
+    r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`"
+)
+LEGACY_LOCATOR_RE = re.compile(
+    r"`(?P<path>(?:blueprint/src/chapter/)?ch[0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*\.tex):"
+    r"(?P<start>[0-9]+)(?:(?P<dash>--|-|\u2013|\u2014)(?P<end>[0-9]+))?"
+    r"(?P<extra>(?:,[0-9]+(?:--|-|\u2013|\u2014)[0-9]+)*)`"
+)
+STATEMENT_ENVS = {
+    "definition",
+    "theorem",
+    "lemma",
+    "proposition",
+    "corollary",
+    "remark",
+    "example",
+}
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class EnvironmentSpan:
+    """One balanced TeX environment."""
+
+    name: str
+    start: int
+    end: int
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class LabelLocation:
+    """The current source span anchored by one active ``\\label``."""
+
+    label: str
+    path: str
+    label_line: int
+    start: int
+    end: int
+
+    @property
+    def locator(self) -> str:
+        suffix = str(self.start) if self.start == self.end else f"{self.start}-{self.end}"
+        return f"{self.path}:{suffix}"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class CitationUse:
+    """A label token found in a file that a reviewer will inspect."""
+
+    label: str
+    path: str
+    line: int
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _OpenEnvironment:
+    name: str
+    start: int
+
+
+def _active_lines(path: Path) -> list[str]:
+    return [strip_tex_comment(line) for line in path.read_text(
+        encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"
+    ).splitlines()]
+
+
+def _parse_tex_file(path: Path, root: Path) -> list[LabelLocation]:
+    """Return active labels in *path*, with enclosing statement/proof spans."""
+
+    lines = _active_lines(path)
+    stack: list[_OpenEnvironment] = []
+    environments: list[EnvironmentSpan] = []
+    labels: list[tuple[str, int]] = []
+
+    for line_no, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
+        for token in TOKEN_RE.finditer(line):
+            kind = token.group("kind")
+            value = token.group("value")
+            if kind == "begin":
+                stack.append(_OpenEnvironment(value, line_no))
+            elif kind == "label":
+                labels.append((value, line_no))
+            else:
+                match_at = next(
+                    (index for index in range(len(stack) - 1, -1, -1)
+                     if stack[index].name == value),
+                    None,
+                )
+                if match_at is None:
+                    continue
+                opened = stack[match_at]
+                del stack[match_at:]
+                environments.append(EnvironmentSpan(value, opened.start, line_no))
+
+    environments.sort(key=lambda span: (span.start, span.end - span.start))
+    proof_spans = [span for span in environments if span.name == "proof"]
+    rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+    locations: list[LabelLocation] = []
+
+    for label, label_line in labels:
+        enclosing = [
+            span for span in environments
+            if span.start <= label_line <= span.end
+        ]
+        if enclosing:
+            span = min(enclosing, key=lambda item: (item.end - item.start, -item.start))
+            start, end = span.start, span.end
+            if span.name in STATEMENT_ENVS:
+                following = next(
+                    (proof for proof in proof_spans if proof.start > span.end),
+                    None,
+                )
+                if following is not None:
+                    gap = lines[span.end:following.start - 1]
+                    if all(not item.strip() for item in gap):
+                        end = following.end
+        else:
+            start = end = label_line
+        locations.append(LabelLocation(label, rel_path, label_line, start, end))
+
+    return locations
+
+
+def build_label_index(root: Path) -> dict[str, list[LabelLocation]]:
+    """Index active blueprint labels below ``root/blueprint/src/chapter``."""
+
+    chapter_root = root / "blueprint" / "src" / "chapter"
+    if not chapter_root.is_dir():
+        raise ValueError(f"blueprint chapter directory does not exist: {chapter_root}")
+    index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]] = {}
+    for path in sorted(chapter_root.rglob("*.tex")):
+        for location in _parse_tex_file(path, root):
+            index.setdefault(location.label, []).append(location)
+    return index
+
+
+def _inside_root(path: Path, root: Path) -> bool:
+    try:
+        path.relative_to(root)
+    except ValueError:
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def collect_input_files(root: Path, paths: list[str], files_from: Path | None) -> list[Path]:
+    """Resolve explicit repository paths without permitting traversal."""
+
+    raw_paths = list(paths)
+    if files_from is not None:
+        raw_paths.extend(
+            line.strip() for line in files_from.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
+            if line.strip()
+        )
+
+    files: set[Path] = set()
+    for raw_path in raw_paths:
+        candidate = Path(raw_path)
+        if not candidate.is_absolute():
+            candidate = root / candidate
+        candidate = candidate.resolve(strict=False)
+        if not _inside_root(candidate, root):
+            raise ValueError(f"input path escapes repository root: {raw_path}")
+        if candidate.is_dir():
+            files.update(path for path in candidate.rglob("*") if path.is_file())
+        elif candidate.is_file():
+            files.add(candidate)
+        # Deleted paths from a changed-file list are intentionally ignored.
+    return sorted(files)
+
+
+def find_citation_uses(
+    files: list[Path], root: Path, index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]]
+) -> tuple[list[CitationUse], list[CitationUse]]:
+    """Find resolvable label tokens and unknown canonical blueprint citations."""
+
+    uses: set[CitationUse] = set()
+    unknown: set[CitationUse] = set()
+    for path in files:
+        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
+        rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+        for match in CODE_LABEL_RE.finditer(text):
+            label = match.group("label")
+            if label in index:
+                uses.add(CitationUse(label, rel_path, text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1))
+        for match in CANONICAL_CITATION_RE.finditer(text):
+            label = match.group("label")
+            if label not in index:
+                unknown.add(
+                    CitationUse(label, rel_path, text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1)
+                )
+    return sorted(uses, key=lambda use: (use.label, use.path, use.line)), sorted(
+        unknown, key=lambda use: (use.label, use.path, use.line)
+    )
+
+
+def _format_resolutions(
+    labels: list[str],
+    origins: dict[str, list[CitationUse]],
+    index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]],
+    output_format: str,
+) -> tuple[str, bool]:
+    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
+    failed = False
+    for label in labels:
+        locations = index.get(label, [])
+        if len(locations) != 1:
+            failed = True
+        rows.append({
+            "label": label,
+            "locations": [location.locator for location in locations],
+            "cited_at": [f"{use.path}:{use.line}" for use in origins.get(label, [])],
+        })
+
+    if output_format == "json":
+        return json.dumps(rows, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", failed
+
+    if output_format == "plain":
+        rendered = []
+        for row in rows:
+            locations = row["locations"]
+            value = ", ".join(locations) if locations else "UNRESOLVED"
+            rendered.append(f"{row['label']}\t{value}")
+        return "\n".join(rendered) + ("\n" if rendered else ""), failed
+
+    rendered = [
+        "# Resolved blueprint citations",
+        "",
+        "Numeric spans below are derived from durable labels; they are not stored citations.",
+        "",
+    ]
+    if not rows:
+        rendered.append("_No blueprint labels were found in the selected files._")
+    for row in rows:
+        locations = row["locations"]
+        location_text = ", ".join(f"`{item}`" for item in locations) or "**UNRESOLVED**"
+        origin_text = row["cited_at"]
+        suffix = ""
+        if origin_text:
+            suffix = "; cited at " + ", ".join(f"`{item}`" for item in origin_text)
+        rendered.append(f"- `{row['label']}` -> {location_text}{suffix}")
+    return "\n".join(rendered) + "\n", failed
+
+
+def _comment_bounds(text: str, position: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    start = text.rfind("/-", 0, position)
+    end = text.find("-/", position)
+    if start >= 0 and end >= 0:
+        return start, end + 2
+    line_start = text.rfind("\n", 0, position) + 1
+    line_end = text.find("\n", position)
+    return line_start, len(text) if line_end < 0 else line_end
+
+
+def _candidate_for_locator(
+    text: str,
+    match: re.Match[str],
+    index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]],
+) -> str | None:
+    # One label cannot faithfully replace a locator that deliberately names
+    # several disjoint spans. Such citations require a manual label list.
+    if match.group("extra"):
+        return None
+
+    target_name = Path(match.group("path")).name
+    block_start, block_end = _comment_bounds(text, match.start())
+    block = text[block_start:block_end]
+    candidates: dict[str, list[re.Match[str]]] = {}
+    for label_match in CODE_LABEL_RE.finditer(block):
+        label = label_match.group("label")
+        locations = index.get(label, [])
+        if len(locations) != 1 or Path(locations[0].path).name != target_name:
+            continue
+        candidates.setdefault(label, []).append(label_match)
+
+    if len(candidates) == 1:
+        return next(iter(candidates))
+    if candidates:
+        linked: set[str] = set()
+        relative_start = match.start() - block_start
+        relative_end = match.end() - block_start
+        for label, label_matches in candidates.items():
+            for label_match in label_matches:
+                if label_match.end() <= relative_start:
+                    between = block[label_match.end():relative_start]
+                    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*\(\s*|\s*[,;]\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+", between):
+                        linked.add(label)
+                elif label_match.start() >= relative_end:
+                    between = block[relative_end:label_match.start()]
+                    after = block[label_match.end():]
+                    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*\(\s*", between) and re.match(r"\s*\)", after):
+                        linked.add(label)
+        return next(iter(linked)) if len(linked) == 1 else None
+
+    old_start = int(match.group("start"))
+    old_end = int(match.group("end") or match.group("start"))
+    exact = [
+        label
+        for label, locations in index.items()
+        if len(locations) == 1
+        and Path(locations[0].path).name == target_name
+        and (locations[0].start, locations[0].end) == (old_start, old_end)
+    ]
+    return exact[0] if len(exact) == 1 else None
+
+
+def rewrite_text(
+    text: str, index: dict[str, list[LabelLocation]]
+) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
+    """Rewrite unambiguous legacy locators and return unresolved locator text."""
+
+    replacements: list[tuple[int, int, str]] = []
+    unresolved: list[str] = []
+    for match in LEGACY_LOCATOR_RE.finditer(text):
+        label = _candidate_for_locator(text, match, index)
+        if label is None:
+            unresolved.append(match.group(0))
+            continue
+        replacements.append((match.start(), match.end(), f"`{label}`"))
+
+    rewritten = text
+    for start, end, replacement in reversed(replacements):
+        rewritten = rewritten[:start] + replacement + rewritten[end:]
+
+    # Collapse the common legacy wording after the locator itself is replaced.
+    def collapse_duplicate(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
+        link = match.group("link")
+        label = match.group("label")
+        if "\n" not in link:
+            return f"blueprint `{label}`"
+        indent_match = re.search(r"\n(?P<indent>[ \t]*)", link)
+        indent = indent_match.group("indent") if indent_match else ""
+        return f"blueprint\n{indent}`{label}`"
+
+    rewritten = re.sub(
+        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`"
+        r"(?P<link>,\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+|;\s+[Bb]lueprint\s+|\s+in\s+)"
+        r"`(?P=label)`",
+        collapse_duplicate,
+        rewritten,
+    )
+    rewritten = re.sub(
+        r"(?P<prefix>\b[Bb]lueprint\s+)"
+        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`\s*[,;]\s*`(?P=label)`",
+        lambda match: f"{match.group('prefix')}`{match.group('label')}`",
+        rewritten,
+    )
+    def collapse_parenthetical(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
+        label = match.group("label")
+        whitespace = match.group("whitespace")
+        if "\n" not in whitespace:
+            return f"blueprint `{label}`"
+        indent_match = re.search(r"\n(?P<indent>[ \t]*)", whitespace)
+        indent = indent_match.group("indent") if indent_match else ""
+        return f"blueprint\n{indent}`{label}`"
+
+    rewritten = re.sub(
+        r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`\s*"
+        r"(?P<whitespace>\(\s*)`(?P=label)`\s*\)",
+        collapse_parenthetical,
+        rewritten,
+    )
+    return rewritten, unresolved
+
+
+def _resolve_command(args: argparse.Namespace, root: Path) -> int:
+    index = build_label_index(root)
+    files = collect_input_files(root, args.paths, args.files_from)
+    uses, unknown = find_citation_uses(files, root, index)
+    labels = list(args.labels)
+    origins: dict[str, list[CitationUse]] = {}
+    for use in uses:
+        if use.label not in labels:
+            labels.append(use.label)
+        origins.setdefault(use.label, []).append(use)
+    for use in unknown:
+        if use.label not in labels:
+            labels.append(use.label)
+        origins.setdefault(use.label, []).append(use)
+    rendered, failed = _format_resolutions(labels, origins, index, args.format)
+    sys.stdout.write(rendered)
+    return 1 if failed else 0
+
+
+def _rewrite_command(args: argparse.Namespace, root: Path) -> int:
+    index = build_label_index(root)
+    files = collect_input_files(root, args.paths, args.files_from)
+    changes: list[tuple[Path, str, str]] = []
+    unresolved: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []
+    for path in files:
+        old = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
+        new, missing = rewrite_text(old, index)
+        if old != new:
+            changes.append((path, old, new))
+        unresolved.extend((path, locator) for locator in missing)
+
+    for path, locator in unresolved:
+        rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+        print(f"unresolved: {rel_path}: {locator}", file=sys.stderr)
+    if unresolved and not args.allow_unresolved:
+        print("refusing partial rewrite; pass --allow-unresolved to rewrite safe matches",
+              file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+
+    if args.write:
+        for path, _old, new in changes:
+            path.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8")
+    else:
+        for path, old, new in changes:
+            rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
+            sys.stdout.writelines(difflib.unified_diff(
+                old.splitlines(keepends=True),
+                new.splitlines(keepends=True),
+                fromfile=rel_path,
+                tofile=rel_path,
+            ))
+    action = "rewrote" if args.write else "would rewrite"
+    print(f"{action} {len(changes)} file(s); {len(unresolved)} unresolved locator(s)",
+          file=sys.stderr)
+    return 0
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--root",
+        type=Path,
+        default=Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent,
+        help="repository root (default: parent of scripts/)",
+    )
+    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
+
+    resolve = subparsers.add_parser("resolve", help="resolve labels to current spans")
+    resolve.add_argument("labels", nargs="*", help="blueprint labels to resolve")
+    resolve.add_argument("--path", dest="paths", action="append", default=[],
+                         help="scan a repository file or directory for label tokens")
+    resolve.add_argument("--files-from", type=Path,
+                         help="scan repository paths listed one per line")
+    resolve.add_argument("--format", choices=("markdown", "plain", "json"),
+                         default="plain")
+
+    rewrite = subparsers.add_parser("rewrite", help="replace unambiguous legacy locators")
+    rewrite.add_argument("paths", nargs="*", help="repository files or directories to rewrite")
+    rewrite.add_argument("--files-from", type=Path,
+                         help="rewrite repository paths listed one per line")
+    rewrite.add_argument("--write", action="store_true",
+                         help="write changes in place (default: print a diff)")
+    rewrite.add_argument("--allow-unresolved", action="store_true",
+                         help="rewrite safe matches while reporting unresolved locators")
+
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    root = args.root.resolve()
+    try:
+        if args.command == "resolve":
+            return _resolve_command(args, root)
+        return _rewrite_command(args, root)
+    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
+        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

    22	/-- The shift observable in blueprint
    23	`lem:twisted-commutation`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:1056-1089`. -/
    24	noncomputable def primeTauShift {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
    25	    [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K]
    26	    (a : K) : Op K := fun i j => if i = j + a then 1 else 0
    27	
    28	/-- The phase observable in blueprint
    29	`lem:twisted-commutation`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:1056-1089`. -/
    30	noncomputable def primeTauPhase {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
    31	    [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K]
    32	    (b : K) : Op K := fun i j =>
    33	  if i = j then ffChar (p := p) (F := K) (b * j) else 0

    35	/-- The multi-qudit observable in `lem:twisted-commutation`, with `false`
    36	denoting phase; blueprint `lem:twisted-commutation`, paper
    37	`04_preliminaries.tex:1073-1095,1141-1151`. -/
    38	noncomputable def primeTauObservable {p : ℕ} {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
    39	    [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K]
    40	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (W : Bool) (a : ι → K) : Op (ι → K) :=
    41	  fun x y => ∏ i : ι, if W then primeTauShift (p := p) (a i) (x i) (y i)
    42	    else primeTauPhase (p := p) (a i) (x i) (y i)

    44	/-- The coordinatewise tensor-entry presentation used by the Pauli observables. -/
    45	private def productMatrix {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    46	    (A : ι → Matrix κ κ ℂ) : Matrix (ι → κ) (ι → κ) ℂ :=
    47	  fun x y => ∏ i, A i (x i) (y i)
    48	
    49	/-- Matrix multiplication distributes over `productMatrix`. -/
    50	private theorem productMatrix_mul {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    51	    [Fintype κ]
    52	    (A B : ι → Matrix κ κ ℂ) :
    53	    (productMatrix A * productMatrix B : Matrix (ι → κ) (ι → κ) ℂ) =
    54	      productMatrix (fun i => A i * B i) := by
    55	  classical
    56	  ext x y
    57	  simpa only [productMatrix, Matrix.mul_apply, Finset.prod_mul_distrib] using
    58	    (Fintype.prod_sum (fun i z => A i (x i) z * B i z (y i))).symm
    59

    62	    [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K] (a a' : K) :
    63	    primeTauShift (p := p) a * primeTauShift (p := p) a' =
    64	      primeTauShift (p := p) (a + a') := by
    65	  ext x y
    66	  simp [Matrix.mul_apply, primeTauShift, add_comm, add_left_comm]

    71	    primeTauPhase (p := p) b * primeTauPhase (p := p) b' =

    73	  ext x y

    98	theorem primeTauObservable_mul {p : ℕ} {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
    99	    [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K] [Fintype ι]
   100	    [DecidableEq ι] (W : Bool) (a a' : ι → K) :

   121	/-- Natural powers of a generalized Pauli observable multiply its label by
   122	repeated addition. -/
   123	private theorem primeTauObservable_pow_nat {p : ℕ} {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   124	    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K]
   125	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (W : Bool) (a : ι → K) (n : ℕ) :
   126	    (primeTauObservable (p := p) W a) ^ n =
   127	      primeTauObservable (p := p) W (fun i => n • a i) := by
   128	  induction n with
   129	  | zero =>
   130	      rw [pow_zero]
   131	      have hzero : (fun i => (0 : ℕ) • a i) = (0 : ι → K) := by
   132	        funext i
   133	        simp
   134	      rw [hzero]
   135	      exact (primeTauObservable_zero (p := p) (K := K) (ι := ι) W).symm
   136	  | succ n ih =>
   137	      calc
   138	        (primeTauObservable (p := p) W a) ^ (n + 1) =
   139	            (primeTauObservable (p := p) W a) ^ n *
   140	              primeTauObservable (p := p) W a := pow_succ _ _
   141	        _ = primeTauObservable (p := p) W (fun i => n • a i) *
   142	              primeTauObservable (p := p) W a := by rw [ih]
   143	        _ = primeTauObservable (p := p) W ((fun i => n • a i) + a) :=
   144	              primeTauObservable_mul W _ _
   145	        _ = primeTauObservable (p := p) W (fun i => (n + 1) • a i) := by
   146	              have hlabels : ((fun i => n • a i) + a) =
   147	                  (fun i => (n + 1) • a i) := by
   148	                funext i
   149	                rw [Pi.add_apply, add_nsmul, one_nsmul]
   150	              exact congrArg
   151	                (fun c => primeTauObservable (p := p) W c) hlabels

   155	theorem primeTauObservable_pow {p : ℕ} {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]

   157	    [DecidableEq ι] (W : Bool) (a : ι → K) (b : ZMod p) :

   181	private theorem star_primeTauShift {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
   182	    [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K] (a : K) :
   183	    star (primeTauShift (p := p) a) = primeTauShift (p := p) (-a) := by
   184	  ext x y

   187	      rw [h]
   188	      abel
   189	    rw [Matrix.star_apply]

   199	/-- Taking the adjoint of a single-coordinate phase negates its label. -/
   200	private theorem star_primeTauPhase {p : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
   201	    [DecidableEq K] [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) K] (b : K) :
   202	    star (primeTauPhase (p := p) b) = primeTauPhase (p := p) (-b) := by
   203	  ext x y
   204	  by_cases hxy : x = y

   206	    simp only [Matrix.star_apply, primeTauPhase, if_pos]
   207	    rw [Complex.star_def]
   208	    simpa only [neg_mul] using
   209	      (AddChar.map_neg_eq_conj (ffChar (p := p) (F := K)) (b * x)).symm
   210	  · have hyx : y ≠ x := Ne.symm hxy
   211	    simp [Matrix.star_apply, primeTauPhase, hxy, hyx]

   439	def _rewrite_command(args: argparse.Namespace, root: Path) -> int:
   440	    index = build_label_index(root)
   441	    files = collect_input_files(root, args.paths, args.files_from)
   442	    changes: list[tuple[Path, str, str]] = []
   443	    unresolved: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []
   444	    for path in files:
   445	        old = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
   446	        new, missing = rewrite_text(old, index)
   447	        if old != new:
   448	            changes.append((path, old, new))
   449	        unresolved.extend((path, locator) for locator in missing)
   450	
   451	    for path, locator in unresolved:
   452	        rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
   453	        print(f"unresolved: {rel_path}: {locator}", file=sys.stderr)
   454	    if unresolved and not args.allow_unresolved:
   455	        print("refusing partial rewrite; pass --allow-unresolved to rewrite safe matches",
   456	              file=sys.stderr)
   457	        return 1
   458	
   459	    if args.write:
   460	        for path, _old, new in changes:
   461	            path.write_text(new, encoding="utf-8")
   462	    else:
   463	        for path, old, new in changes:
   464	            rel_path = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
   465	            sys.stdout.writelines(difflib.unified_diff(
   466	                old.splitlines(keepends=True),
   467	                new.splitlines(keepends=True),
   468	                fromfile=rel_path,
   469	                tofile=rel_path,
   470	            ))
   471	    action = "rewrote" if args.write else "would rewrite"
   472	    print(f"{action} {len(changes)} file(s); {len(unresolved)} unresolved locator(s)",
   473	          file=sys.stderr)
   474	    return 0

   110	def path_filter_blocks(text: str) -> list[set[str]]:
   111	    """Extract entries from GitHub Actions trigger ``paths:`` filters."""
   112	
   113	    blocks: list[set[str]] = []
   114	    anchors: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
   115	    in_on = False
   116	    on_indent = 0
   117	    event_indent: int | None = None
   118	    event_child_indent: int | None = None
   119	    in_paths = False
   120	    paths_indent = 0
   121	    current_block: set[str] = set()
   122	    current_anchor: str | None = None
   123	
   124	    def finish_current_block() -> None:
   125	        nonlocal current_anchor, current_block, in_paths
   126	        block = set(current_block)
   127	        blocks.append(block)
   128	        if current_anchor is not None:
   129	            anchors[current_anchor] = block
   130	        current_anchor = None
   131	        current_block = set()
   132	        in_paths = False
   133	
   134	    def start_paths_block(match: re.Match[str]) -> None:
   135	        nonlocal current_anchor, current_block, in_paths, paths_indent
   136	        anchor = match.group("anchor")
   137	        anchor_name = anchor.removeprefix("&") if anchor else None
   138	        if alias := match.group("alias"):
   139	            blocks.append(set(anchors.get(alias.removeprefix("*"), set())))
   140	        elif flow := match.group("flow"):
   141	            block = _flow_path_scalars(flow)
   142	            blocks.append(block)
   143	            if anchor_name is not None:
   144	                anchors[anchor_name] = block
   145	        else:
   146	            in_paths = True
   147	            paths_indent = len(match.group("indent"))
   148	            current_block = set()
   149	            current_anchor = anchor_name
   150	
   151	    for raw_line in text.splitlines():
   152	        while True:
   153	            stripped = raw_line.strip()
   154	            if not stripped or stripped.startswith("#"):
   155	                break
   156	            indent = len(raw_line) - len(raw_line.lstrip(" "))
   157	
   158	            if in_paths:
   159	                if indent <= paths_indent:
   160	                    finish_current_block()
   161	                    # Reconsider this same line: it might start another paths block.
   162	                    continue
   163	                if match := _PATH_ENTRY_RE.match(raw_line):
   164	                    path = _unquote_path_scalar(match.group("scalar"))
   165	                    if path:
   166	                        current_block.add(path)
   167	                break
   168	
   169	            if in_on:
   170	                if indent <= on_indent:
   171	                    in_on = False
   172	                    event_indent = None
   173	                    event_child_indent = None
   174	                    # Reconsider this same line: it might start another top-level block.
   175	                    continue
   176	
   177	                if match := _PATHS_KEY_RE.match(raw_line):
   178	                    path_key_indent = len(match.group("indent"))
   179	                    if event_indent is not None and (
   180	                        event_child_indent is None or path_key_indent == event_child_indent
   181	                    ):
   182	                        event_child_indent = path_key_indent
   183	                        start_paths_block(match)
   184	                    break
   185	
   186	                if match := _YAML_KEY_RE.match(raw_line):
   187	                    key_indent = len(match.group("indent"))
   188	                    if event_indent is None or key_indent <= event_indent:
   189	                        event_indent = key_indent
   190	                        event_child_indent = None
   191	                    elif event_child_indent is None:
   192	                        event_child_indent = key_indent
   193	                break
   194	
   195	            if match := _ON_KEY_RE.match(raw_line):
   196	                in_on = True
   197	                on_indent = len(match.group("indent"))
   198	                event_indent = None
   199	                event_child_indent = None
   200	            break
   201	
   202	    if in_paths:
   203	        finish_current_block()

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Resolve durable blueprint labels and migrate legacy numeric locators.
+
+Lean docstrings should store blueprint labels, not line ranges.  This helper
+derives the current source span of each label from ``blueprint/src/chapter``.
+It can also conservatively rewrite old ``chNN_*.tex:START-END`` citations when
+the surrounding comment names one unambiguous label from that chapter.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import difflib
+import json
+import re
+import sys
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from tex_utils import strip_tex_comment
+
+
+TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"\\(?P<kind>begin|end|label)\{(?P<value>[^}]+)\}")
+CODE_LABEL_RE = re.compile(r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`")
+CANONICAL_CITATION_RE = re.compile(
+    r"\b[Bb]lueprint(?:\s+(?:node|nodes|label|labels|entry|entries))?\s+"
+    r"`(?P<label>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)`"
+)
+LEGACY_LOCATOR_RE = re.compile(
+    r"`(?P<path>(?:blueprint/src/chapter/)?ch[0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*\.tex):"
+    r"(?P<start>[0-9]+)(?:(?P<dash>--|-|\u2013|\u2014)(?P<end>[0-9]+))?"
+    r"(?P<extra>(?:,[0-9]+(?:--|-|\u2013|\u2014)[0-9]+)*)`"
+)
+STATEMENT_ENVS = {
+    "definition",
+    "theorem",
+    "lemma",
+    "proposition",
+    "corollary",
+    "remark",
+    "example",
+}
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class EnvironmentSpan:
+    """One balanced TeX environment."""
+
+    name: str
+    start: int
+    end: int
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class LabelLocation:
+    """The current source span anchored by one active ``\\label``."""
+
+    label: str
+    path: str
+    label_line: int
+    start: int
+    end: int
+
+    @property
+    def locator(self) -> str:
+        suffix = str(self.start) if self.start == self.end else f"{self.start}-{self.end}"
+        return f"{self.path}:{suffix}"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class CitationUse:
+    """A label token found in a file that a reviewer will inspect."""
+
+    label: str
+    path: str
+    line: int
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _OpenEnvironment:
+    name: str
+    start: int
+
+
+def _active_lines(path: Path) -> list[str]:
+    return [strip_tex_comment(line) for line in path.read_text(
+        encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"
+    ).splitlines()]

from pathlib import Path
import subprocess,re
base='8bcb447'; head='8939102'
files=subprocess.check_output(['git','diff','--name-only',base,head],text=True).splitlines()
legacy=re.compile(r'"'`(?:(?:blueprint/src/chapter/)?ch[''^`'"\\n]+?\\.tex:[0-9]["'^`]*)`'"')
for fn in files:
 if not fn.endswith('.lean'): continue
 try: old=subprocess.check_output(['git','show',f'{base}:{fn}'],text=True,stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
 except: continue
 ms=list(legacy.finditer(old))
 if not ms: continue
 new=Path(fn).read_text(errors='replace')
 print('\\n###',fn)
 for m in ms:
  ln=old.count('\\n',0,m.start())+1
  ctx=old[max(0,m.start()-180):min(len(old),m.end()+100)].replace('\\n',' ')
  print('old',ln,m.group(0),'context:',ctx)
  # nearest new line around same rough line, print lines containing blueprint labels maybe
  for i,line in enumerate(new.splitlines(),1):
   if 'blueprint' in line.lower() and i>=max(1,ln-4) and i<=ln+4:
    print(' new',i,line.strip())

"""Shared helpers for parsing active TeX source lines."""

from __future__ import annotations


def strip_tex_comment(line: str) -> str:
    r"""Return the active TeX prefix before the first unescaped ``%``.

    TeX comments start at an unescaped percent sign. A percent sign preceded
    by an odd-length run of backslashes is the literal ``\%`` token and must
    not truncate the line; an even-length run leaves the ``%`` unescaped.
    """

    for idx, char in enumerate(line):
        if char != "%":
            continue
        backslashes = 0
        j = idx - 1
        while j >= 0 and line[j] == "\\":
            backslashes += 1
            j -= 1
        if backslashes % 2 == 0:
            return line[:idx]
    return line

A scope-restricted theorem may be marked `\\leanok` only\nagainst a blueprint statement that explicitly states the restriction; it must\nnot be presented as the unrestricted source theorem.\n\nWhen a stricter-hypothesis Lean theorem is the only available version near a\nsource theorem, the discrepancy must have a paper-gap note or tracking issue.\nThe note should identify the missing hypothesis, explain why it is not part of\nthe cited statement, and state the plan for eliminating the restriction,\nderiving it internally, or moving the result out of the source-labelled route.\n\nThis rule applies especially to declarations named after paper labels such as\n`mainFormal`, `selfImprovement`, `mainInduction`, or other theorem names linked\nfrom the blueprint by `\\lean{...}` and `\\leanok`.\n\nBefore editing any theorem tagged with a paper label (`thm:*`, `lem:*`,\n`prop:*`):\n\n1. Preserve the public Lean theorem statement, except for hypotheses that are\n   genuinely part of the faithful encoding of the paper's domain.\n3. Do not add bridge inputs, residual packages, repair hypotheses, producer\n   assumptions, generic hypotheses or assumptions bundles, or arbitrary\n   implication hypotheses to the paper theorem.\n4. If a missing intermediate fact is needed, first state that fact as a named\n   lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.\n5. Do not point a source-labelled blueprint theorem to the conditional helper\n   with `\\leanok`.\n\nWhen reviewing an existing bridge, residual, repair, producer, or package\nhypothesis, first try to recover any genuine proof content from its construction\nand turn that content into a source-faithful lemma. These assumptions\nshould not be introduced merely to keep a file compiling or to avoid a `sorry`;\nthey require explicit mathematical justification and a planned discharge.\n\nFor the current LDT final theorem, `mainFormal` is reserved for the statement of\n`\\Cref{thm:main-formal}`: from a projective strategy passing the low individual\ndegree test, it produces the three final consistency conclusions. These lighter\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\npaper hypotheses.\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Imports\n\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\n- One import per line\n- Follow existing local import style\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\n\n### File structure\n\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\n\n1. imports\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\n3. namespace / opens / variables\n4. declarations\n\n### Formatting\n\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\n  own line\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\n  theorem statement\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Complements\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference, which covers the kernel-level\nblockers; this file covers patterns where the Lean code *compiles and the\ntrick is at the level of what the statement says or what the definitions\nbake in*.\n\nEvery pattern here is **castle-in-the-air in spirit**: a theorem named after a\npaper result that doesn't actually prove it. The named offenders below all\ncross-reference a concrete issue or PR so reviewers can see a real example.\n\n## Why this matters\n\nKernel checks are necessary but not sufficient. A theorem can:\n\n- Be marked `\\leanok` in the blueprint,\n- Have a sorry-free proof body,\n- Have a clean axiom closure (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only),\n\nand still prove **nothing that the paper actually claims**, if the proof\nobligation has been displaced into a hypothesis, a definition, or a sentinel\nbranch. The patterns below are the displacement mechanisms we've seen in this\ncodebase.\n\n## Catalogue\n\n- [A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis](#a1--conclusion-shaped-hypothesis)\n- [A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand](#a2--definitional-sleight-of-hand)\n- [A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions](#a3--zero-fallback-branches-hiding-preconditions)\n- [A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials](#a4--trivial-default-witnesses-for-existentials)\n- [A5 — Castle-in-the-air / bypassing Mathlib](#a5--castle-in-the-air--bypassing-mathlib)\n- [A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles](#a6--external-statement-smuggles)\n\n---\n\n## A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis\n\n**Smell.** The theorem takes a hypothesis whose type is the theorem's own\nconclusion (or an `∃`/function that produces the conclusion). The proof body\nis a trivial `rcases`/`exact`/`.trans`/`simpa using h` and does no\nmathematical work. A variant wraps the hypothesis in a named bundle\n(`*BridgePackage`, `*Statement`); see issues [#449], [#451], [#477] for the\ncatalogue, and [#493] for the inline-existential mutation triggered by\nPR [#491].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\nThe theorem's named mathematical content is never derived from prior lemmas;\nthe caller (who supplies the hypothesis) has to discharge it. In practice the\ncaller then has the same problem, pushing the obligation further up the\nstack. The theorem is true under a vacuous hypothesis and the `\\leanok` tag\nmisrepresents the actual state of the proof.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- The hypothesis type contains, up to `∃` / `∧` / a coercion, the theorem's\n  conclusion.\n- The proof body is one of:\n  - `rcases h with ⟨...⟩; exact ⟨...⟩`\n  - `exact h.fieldName` / `exact h.a.trans h.b`\n  - `by simpa using h.fieldName`\n- The hypothesis is a bundle named `*BridgePackage`, `*Witness`, `*Package`,\n  `*Output`, with a field whose type matches the conclusion structure.\n- Consumers of the bundle are trivial (field projection + return).\n\n### Concrete example\n\nHistorical example (before the MainInductionStep cleanup):\n\n```lean\ntheorem mainInduction\n    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]\n    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)\n    (eps delta gamma : Error) (k : ℕ)\n    (hbridge : MainInductionBridgePackage params strategy eps delta gamma k) :\n    ∃ G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι,\n      ConsRel strategy.state ...\n        (mainInductionError params k eps delta gamma) := by\n  rcases hbridge.witness with ⟨error, G, hG, herror⟩\n  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩\n  exact ⟨le_trans hG.offDiagonalBound herror⟩\n```\n\nHere `MainInductionBridgePackage.witness` has type\n`∃ error, ∃ G, ConsRel ... error ∧ error ≤ mainInductionError ...` — literally\nthe conclusion. The code has since been refactored to remove both this\nspecific MainInductionStep bridge and the interim theorem alias that exposed\nthe same witness shape under the paper theorem's name, but the snippet remains\nthe archetypal example of the anti-pattern.\n\nPR [#491] proposed to delete the `*BridgePackage` by **inlining** the bundle's\nfields as explicit hypotheses. That only scatters the same pattern across\nindividual signatures without producing any proof — it's strictly worse\nbecause the named bundle at least shows up in one tracker. Do not accept PRs\nthat discharge an ungrounded bridge by flattening it into conclusion-shaped\nexistential hypotheses, or by reintroducing the same shape under a theorem name\nthat suggests the paper result has been proved.\n\n### How to fix it\n\nPrefer **proving a real intermediate lemma** — one that the paper also uses\n— and stating its signature with the paper's hypotheses (not the theorem's\nconclusion). Then use it inside the larger theorem. If the missing content\ncannot be formalized yet, state the missing assertion as a named obligation\nto be proved from the paper hypotheses, and leave the corresponding proof open\nunder a tracker. Do not put that obligation on the source-labelled theorem as\nan extra hypothesis. Existing `BridgePackage`-style declarations are proof\ndebt to be removed or converted into source-faithful obligations; they are not\nthe preferred shape for new work.\n\nA signature passes the smell test if:\n\n- Every hypothesis is a **named intermediate fact** that also appears in the\n  paper or blueprint proof, not the theorem's output packaged up, and\n- Replacing a hypothesis with its negation would produce a *different*\n  theorem, not a trivially-false one.\n\n### Related issues and patterns\n\n- [#449] — paper-wide gap tracker\n- [#451] — the tracked `BridgePackage` producer catalogue\n- [#595] — resolved the QXP `ProjectiveNonMeasurementBridgePackage` offender by\n  deleting the bridge and threading `RoundingToProjectorsWitness` directly\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` axiom-field projection (a definitional variant)\n- [#493] — the inline-existential mutation of this pattern\n- [#491] — PR that introduced the mutation\n\n---\n\n## A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand\n\n**Smell.** A `def`/`abbrev` is written so its body is the paper's claim, and\na nearby `theorem` restates that claim and proves it by `rfl` (or a one-line\n`simp [foo]` where `foo` is the defining equation). The \"mathematical\ncontent\" has been baked into the definition; the theorem is a tautology. See\nissues [#477], [#494].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\n`rfl` proves that a definition equals itself. If the definition is chosen\n*so that* it equals the conclusion, the `rfl` \"proof\" transports none of the\npaper's reasoning — it is literally the reflexivity of a shape we invented to\nmatch the conclusion. The real identity the paper proves (e.g.,\n`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ` over an actual inner product) is still not stated\nanywhere in Lean.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- A `theorem` whose body is `rfl` / `by rfl` / `by simp [defName]` where\n  `defName` is the def that unfolds to the conclusion.\n- A `structure` with a `Prop`-typed field whose *role* in the paper is a\n  nontrivial identity (SVD, orthonormality, Cauchy–Schwarz), accompanied by a\n  constructor that discharges that field with `rfl`.\n- A `def foo := if α = β then 1 else 0` followed by a theorem asserting\n  `foo α β = if α = β then 1 else 0`.\n- Bridge-like structures where every field is itself a function\n  `(precondition) → (conclusion-step)` and the consumer applies the field\n  directly.\n\n### Concrete example\n\nFrom `MIPStarRE/LDT/ExpansionHypercubeGraph/Defs/Fourier.lean`:\n\n```lean\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\ndef fourierBasisInnerProduct (params : Parameters)\n    (α β : Point params) : Error :=\n  if α = β then 1 else 0\n\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\nlemma fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq (params : Parameters)\n    (α β : Point params) :\n    fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0 := rfl\n\n/-- `prop:eigenvectors`. -/\ntheorem eigenvectors (params : Parameters) :\n    (∀ α β : Point params,\n      fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0) ∧ ... := by\n  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩\n  · intro α β\n    exact fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq params α β    -- castle: def IS Kronecker delta\n  ...\n```\n\nThe paper's orthonormality claim — that the additive characters `φ_α` form an\northonormal basis under the actual inner product\n`⟨f, g⟩ := (1/|V|) · ∑_u f(u)^* · g(u)` — requires a genuine character-sum\nidentity. The Lean theorem states and proves only the trivial fact that the\ndefinition equals itself.\n\n### Not every `rfl` is a castle\n\nDistinguish from legitimate bookkeeping where a named equation is literally\nhow something was defined. Example: `mainFormalError_eq_envelope` in\n`Test/ErrorCascade/Definitions.lean` unfolds the definition of\n`mainFormalError` to its envelope factorization. The mathematical content is\nelsewhere (the envelope is derived from per-step bounds); the `rfl` theorem is\na naming convenience only. The test is: **does the `def` body encode a paper\nidentity, or does it just name a compound expression?**\n\n### How to fix it\n\n1. Move the paper's real definition to the concrete one: for Fourier, define\n   the inner product as the actual sum over vertices, and the characters\n   `φ_α` as functions from `Point params` to `ℂ`.\n2. State the paper's identity (`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ`) as a theorem over those\n   concrete objects.\n3. Prove it via the standard character-sum derivation (or cite the Mathlib\n   counterpart if one exists — `Matrix.dotProduct` / `Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff`\n   combined with `ZMod.sum_pow_units` style lemmas).\n4. If you want to keep the Kronecker shorthand, define it *afterward* as a\n   consequence, not as the primitive.\n\n### Related issues\n\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` field projections (Ch4 SVD as axiom fields)\n- [#494] — the Fourier case and other candidates\n\n---\n\n## A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions\n\n**Smell.** A total function is defined by `if eligible then real_value else\ndefault`, where the `default` (usually `0`, `default`, `⊥`, or\n`Classical.arbitrary`) is a sentinel for \"precondition not met.\" Downstream\ntheorems state properties that are only true on the eligible branch, but the\ntheorem's type signature does not carry the eligibility proof, so the\nobligation moves silently from the prover to whoever happens to call the\nfunction. See issue [#495], related to [#307].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\nThe signature lies about the domain of validity. A caller passing a\nnon-eligible input gets `0` back; any theorem proved about \"the output\" is\nproved for `0`, which is trivially true and carries no information. When a\nlater theorem composes the output with another lemma, the composition\ntype-checks but the conclusion is vacuous on inputs where the original\nprecondition failed.\n\nThe paper, by contrast, restricts the quantifier in the first place:\n\"Fix a tuple `(x₁, ..., x_k)` with Hamming weight `≥ d+1`.\" The Lean should\nmatch.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- `match ... with | some _ => real | none => 0` or `| _ => 0`.\n- `if hEligible : P then ... else default`.\n- Identifier names containing `fallback`, `placeholder`, `sentinel`,\n  `dummy`, `or0`, `orDefault`.\n- Recursive definitions whose base case unconditionally returns a sentinel.\n- Functions that return `Polynomial params` but can return the zero polynomial\n  on inputs that shouldn't be in the domain.\n\n### Concrete example (historical; resolved by PR #561)\n\nUntil PR #561, `MIPStarRE/LDT/Pasting/Defs/Interpolation.lean` contained:\n\n```lean\n/-- Extract the polynomial from a completed slice outcome; returns 0 on ⊥. -/\nnoncomputable def extractSliceOr0 {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]\n    (g : GHatOutcome params) : PolynomialModel params :=\n  match g with\n  | some p => p.poly\n  | none   => 0\n```\n\nThe consumer `interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport` ran Lagrange\ninterpolation on `extractSliceOr0`-extracted values. If the support contained\na `none`, the interpolant silently pretended that slice evaluated to zero.\nThe paper's Lagrange step is quantified over *eligible* slices only, so the\nLean API should carry `∀ i ∈ support, (g i).isSome` as a hypothesis; instead\nit carried nothing, and the theorem technically type-checked on inputs for\nwhich its conclusion was meaningless.\n\n**Current status:** resolved. The live API now removes `extractSliceOr0`,\nthreads the explicit hypothesis `hσsupport : σ ⊆ gHatTupleSupport gs` into\n`interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport`, and packages the chosen support subset\nas `InterpolationSupportWitness` so the arbitrary choice and its proof fields\nare visible at call sites.\n\n### Acceptable uses of this pattern\n\nNot every default branch is a castle. `Inhabited` / `Nonempty` instances\nthat provide a canonical inhabitant (e.g., the zero polynomial for\n`Nonempty (Polynomial params)`) are plumbing, not proof. The test is: **does\nany theorem mention the output?** If a theorem says \"the output satisfies\nP\", and P is not trivially satisfied by the sentinel, the fallback is\nsmuggling a precondition.\n\n### How to fix it\n\nPick one of:\n\n1. **Make the precondition explicit.** Add `(h : eligible input) :` to the\n   signature. Let Lean's type system enforce that non-eligible inputs cannot\n   be passed.\n2. **Return an `Option`.** The `none` result forces every caller to handle\n   the case, so theorems about \"the output\" now quantify only over the\n   `some` branch.\n3. **Restrict the domain.** Instead of `(x : X) → Y`, take `(x : {x : X //\n   P x}) → Y`. Common for finite-support Lagrange-style constructions where\n   the subtype is computable via `Finset.filter`.\n\n### Classical-logic dependencies\n\nA sibling smell in this pattern: `DecidablePred` / `DecidableEq` instances\nthat silently use `Classical.dec` to fill in decidability that should be\nconstructive. The historical `interpolationEligibleSandwichFamily`\nimplementation was exactly such a case: it used `open Classical in ...` to\ngate a predicate that is actually decidable by a finite-support check. PR\n#561 fixed that example by adding `interpolationEligible_decidablePred`.\nThose classical instances are acceptable only when the predicate is genuinely\nnon-constructive; if a constructive instance is plausible, write it, don't\nbottom out in `Classical.dec`.    243	We recall the Magic Square game of Mermin and Peres. It is a simple self-test for two EPR pairs, and it allows one to test that a pair of binary observables \emph{anticommutes}; both properties are used in the Pauli basis test. Here it is presented as a binary constraint satisfaction game. Throughout this section and the next, $\sigma^X$ and $\sigma^Z$ denote the single-qubit Pauli observables, with associated two-outcome projective measurements $\{\sigma^W_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ for $W \in \{X,Z\}$.
   244	
   245	\begin{definition}[The Magic Square game]\label{def:ms-game}
   246		\uses{def:game, def:graph-distribution}
   247		The Magic Square game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{MS}}$ is the following two-player game. There are $9$ variables $x_1,\ldots,x_9$ taking values in $\F_2$, arranged in a $3 \times 3$ grid: the cell in row $r$ and column $c$ contains the variable $x_{3(r-1)+c}$. There are $6$ linear equations over these variables: for each of the three rows and each of the first two columns, the sum of the three variables in it equals $0$; for the third column, the sum of the three variables in it equals $1$.
   248	
   249		The question types are
   250		\begin{align*}
   251			\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}} &= \{\mathsf{Constraint}_i : i = 1,2,\ldots,6\}\;,\\
   252			\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mv}} &= \{\mathsf{Variable}_j : j = 1,2,\ldots,9\}\;,\\
   253			\mathcal T^{\mathrm{ms}} &= \mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}} \cup \mathcal T^{\mathrm{mv}}\;,
   254		\end{align*}
   255		where $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ for $i \in \{1,2,3\}$ denotes the constraint of row $i$ (with variables $x_{3(i-1)+1}, x_{3(i-1)+2}, x_{3(i-1)+3}$), $\mathsf{Constraint}_4$ and $\mathsf{Constraint}_5$ denote the constraints of the first two columns, and $\mathsf{Constraint}_6$ denotes the constraint of the third column (with variables $x_{i-3}, x_{i}, x_{i+3}$ for $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$, $i \in \{4,5,6\}$).
   256	
   257		The question distribution is as follows: the verifier samples $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ uniformly from $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}}$, then samples $\mathsf{Variable}_j$ uniformly among the three variables appearing in the row or column of $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$; one player, chosen uniformly at random, receives $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ and the other receives $\mathsf{Variable}_j$. Equivalently, the verifier samples a uniformly random edge of the bipartite \emph{type graph} $G^{\mathrm{ms}}$ on vertex sets $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}}$ and $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mv}}$, whose edges are $\mathsf{Constraint}_i \,\text{---}\, \mathsf{Variable}_{3(i-1)+j}$ for $i,j \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $\mathsf{Constraint}_i \,\text{---}\, \mathsf{Variable}_{(i-3)+3(j-1)}$ for $i \in \{4,5,6\}$, $j \in \{1,2,3\}$ ($18$ edges in total, and no self-loops), and sends one endpoint to a uniformly random player and the other endpoint to the other player.
   258	
   259		The $\mathsf{Constraint}$ player answers with three bits $(\beta_{v_1}, \beta_{v_2}, \beta_{v_3}) \in \F_2^3$, where $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ are the indices of the three variables of $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$; the $\mathsf{Variable}$ player answers with a single bit $\gamma \in \F_2$. The players win if and only if the $\mathsf{Constraint}$ player's answer satisfies the equation associated with $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ and $\gamma = \beta_j$.
   260	\end{definition}
   261	
   262	The following theorem records the self-testing (rigidity) properties of the Magic Square game. It is used in the soundness analysis of the Pauli basis test to enforce anticommutation relations between certain pairs of observables.
   263	With zero-based labels, the paper's variables $1$ and $5$ have labels $0$ and
   264	$4$, respectively.
   265	
   266	\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the Magic Square game]\label{thm:ms-rigidity}
   267		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ms_rigidity}
   268		\leanok
   269		\uses{def:ms-game, def:tensor-product-value, def:EPR, def:povm-distance}
   270		Let $\mathcal S = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a strategy that succeeds in the Magic Square game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{MS}}$ with probability $1-\eps$, where $\ket{\psi} \in \hilb_{\mathrm A} \ot \hilb_{\mathrm B}$. Then there exist local isometries $\phi_{\mathrm A}\colon \hilb_{\mathrm A} \to \hilb_{\mathrm A'} \ot \hilb_{\mathrm A''}$ and $\phi_{\mathrm B}\colon \hilb_{\mathrm B} \to \hilb_{\mathrm B'} \ot \hilb_{\mathrm B''}$, where $\hilb_{\mathrm A'}, \hilb_{\mathrm B'} \cong (\C^2)^{\ot 2}$ and $\hilb_{\mathrm A''}, \hilb_{\mathrm B''}$ are finite dimensional, and a state $\ket{\mathrm{aux}} \in \hilb_{\mathrm A''} \ot \hilb_{\mathrm B''}$, such that:
   271		\begin{enumerate}
   272			\item $\bigl\| \phi_{\mathrm A} \ot \phi_{\mathrm B} \ket{\psi} - \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_2}^{\ot 2} \ot \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \bigr\| \le O(\sqrt\eps)$;
   273			\item letting $\tilde A^x_a = \phi_{\mathrm A} A^x_a \phi_{\mathrm A}^\dagger$ and $\tilde B^y_b = \phi_{\mathrm B} B^y_b \phi_{\mathrm B}^\dagger$,
   274			\begin{align*}
   275				\tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_1}_b \ot I_{\mathrm{B'B''}} &\approx_{\sqrt\eps} (\sigma^X_b)_{\mathrm A'} \ot I_{\mathrm{A''B'B''}}\;,\\
   276				\tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_5}_b \ot I_{\mathrm{B'B''}} &\approx_{\sqrt\eps} (\sigma^Z_b)_{\mathrm A'} \ot I_{\mathrm{A''B'B''}}\;,\\
   277				I_{\mathrm{A'A''}} \ot \tilde B^{\mathsf{Variable}_1}_b &\approx_{\sqrt\eps} I_{\mathrm{A'A''B''}} \ot (\sigma^X_b)_{\mathrm B'}\;,\\
   278				I_{\mathrm{A'A''}} \ot \tilde B^{\mathsf{Variable}_5}_b &\approx_{\sqrt\eps} I_{\mathrm{A'A''B''}} \ot (\sigma^Z_b)_{\mathrm B'}\;,
   279			\end{align*}
   280			where each $\approx_{\sqrt\eps}$ holds with respect to the state $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_2}^{\ot 2}_{\mathrm{A'B'}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{aux}}_{\mathrm{A''B''}}$ and the answer summation is over $b \in \{0,1\}$, and the approximation bounds carry implicit universal constants.
   281		\end{enumerate}
   282		As a consequence, letting $\tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_1} = \tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_1}_0 - \tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_1}_1$ and $\tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_5} = \tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_5}_0 - \tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_5}_1$ denote the associated observables, it holds that
   283		\begin{align*}
   284			\tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_1} \tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_5} \ot I_{\mathrm{B'B''}} &\approx_{\sqrt\eps} -\, \tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_5} \tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_1} \ot I_{\mathrm{B'B''}}\;,\\
   285			I_{\mathrm{A'A''}} \ot \tilde B^{\mathsf{Variable}_1} \tilde B^{\mathsf{Variable}_5} &\approx_{\sqrt\eps} -\, I_{\mathrm{A'A''}} \ot \tilde B^{\mathsf{Variable}_5} \tilde B^{\mathsf{Variable}_1}\;,
   286		\end{align*}
   287		where, for operators $M$, $N$ that are not POVM elements, the notation $M \approx_\delta N$ means $\bra{\psi} (M-N)^\dagger (M-N) \ket{\psi} \le O(\delta)$ with respect to the same state.
   288	\end{theorem}
   289	\begin{proof}
   290		This result is imported from Theorem~6.9 of~\cite{Coladangelo2017Robust}. There are two minor differences between their statement and the one given here. First, they state a robustness of $O(\eps)$, but measure the closeness of the actual and ideal states in trace norm; expressed as the Euclidean distance between $\phi_{\mathrm A} \ot \phi_{\mathrm B}\ket{\psi}$ and $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_2}^{\ot 2} \ot \ket{\mathrm{aux}}$, this becomes $O(\sqrt\eps)$. Second, their ideal observables for the $\mathsf{Variable}_1$ and $\mathsf{Variable}_5$ questions are $I \ot \sigma^Z$ and $\sigma^Z\sigma^X \ot \sigma^Z\sigma^X$; under a local change of basis these are equivalent to $\sigma^X \ot I$ and $\sigma^Z \ot I$, respectively.
   291	\end{proof}
   292	
   293	The converse construction shows that any pair of anticommuting binary observables yields a perfect strategy for the Magic Square game.

   296		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.obsOf, MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ms_perfect_strategy_of_anticommuting}
   297		\leanok

   304		\end{enumerate}
   305	\end{theorem}

results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-issues.json:274:  "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: pr150-terminal-sampling-support-followup -->\n## Context\n\nPR #150 proves the low-degree geometry and sampling identities from issue #106.\nIts terminal exact-head review found duplicated distribution and seed-fiber\ninfrastructure, incomplete blueprint dependency records, and mathematical\ndocumentation that still describes file organization. This cleanup is kept\noutside the reviewed proof packet.\n\n## Scope\n\n- Consolidate the general push-forward results in\n  `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/DistributionAux.lean` with the specialized API in\n  `DistributionMarginals.lean`, retaining one reusable proof path and deriving\n  compatibility wrappers where needed.\n- Move the exact `chiIndex` seed-fiber decomposition below both consumers and\n  reuse the existing `LdParams.seedFiber*` construction from\n  `Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/Correspondence.lean`.\n- Give the eight public distribution/push-forward declarations subordinate\n  blueprint entries and direct dependency edges, or make genuinely internal\n  helpers private.\n- Synchronize the Chapter 13 proof `\\uses` lists with the declarations the Lean\n  proofs actually invoke, including the sampling push-forwards, map\n  composition, marginals, and representative/prefix identities.\n- Replace implementation-oriented module and declaration prose with\n  mathematical descriptions; call recursive CL components levels or linear\n  contributions rather than stages.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- There is one authoritative distribution/marginal API and one authoritative\n  seed-fiber decomposition used by the relevant consumers.\n- Blueprint support nodes and `\\uses` edges match the public declarations and\n  their direct proof dependencies.\n- Changed docstrings and module preambles satisfy\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`.\n- Changed Lean files type-check; blueprint checks and the full local CI pass.\n\nProvenance: PR #150 at\n`789dfbcccc083fbd254f68375dfc38510c4a30fa`, terminal findings F3, F4,\nF9-F13.\n\n---\nAddresses #106",

results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-issues.json:573:  "body": "<!-- mipstarre-issue-key: pr151-round3-linearity-blueprint-followup -->\n## Context\n\nPR #151 proves the quantum linearity route, including the corrected bounds\n`2 * delta` for squared state-dependent operator distance and `delta` for the\nassociated binary-measurement distance. Its third exact-head review identified\nfive documentation and blueprint inconsistencies that must not expand that PR\nunder the owner's review-churn rule.\n\n## Required corrections\n\n- In `lem:qld-4-10` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`, change\n  the displayed squared operator-distance bound from `delta_{x,z}/2` to\n  `delta_{x,z}`. results/telemetry/github-snapshot/open-issues.json:854:  "body": "## Why\n\nThe #105 prover showed that `thm:ms-rigidity` / `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ms_rigidity` is false as stated: a role-symmetrized two-copy perfect strategy wins `msGame` with value 1 yet violates the conclusions at `\u03b5 = 0` (https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/105#issuecomment-5540390178). The paper (`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:620-649`) states the theorem for an arbitrary strategy and imports Coladangelo\u2013Stark Theorem 6.9, which concerns the one-way game; the paper's standing convention restricts attention to symmetric strategies (`06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:174`), and the only use (`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:339`) applies the theorem to a symmetric strategy `(\u03c8, M)`.\n\nOwner direction (2026-09-04): every gap in a source paper (wrong mathematics) is recorded as a paper-gap note and fixed in the blueprint, following `docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex` and `docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex`. This packet applies that to the Magic Square rigidity theorem. Decision taken: **restrict the statement to symmetric strategies** (option 1 on #26).\n\n## Deliverables\n\n1. **Gap note** `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ms-rigidity-symmetric-strategies.tex`, built from `docs/paper-gaps/template.tex` with the sections `policy.tex` requires, passing `python3 scripts/check_paper_gap_note_style.py`. Content: the source statement with paper lines; the counterexample (perfect strategy on two EPR copies, copy 1 when Alice holds the constraint, copy 2 when Bob does; Alice's and Bob's variable observables act on different copies, so their correlation is 0 while the ideal correlation is 1); why the CS one-way self-test does not constrain both players' variable observables in the role-symmetric game; the correction (hypothesis: the strategy is symmetric, which is the paper's convention and suffices for the paper's only use); blueprint and formalization status. Use the shared macros (`\\leanid`, `\\path`, `\\ghissue`) as the checker demands and cite #105 and this issue.\n2. **Blueprint** `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, `thm:ms-rigidity` (lines 228-250): restate for a symmetric strategy `S = (\u03c8, M)` of the symmetric Magic Square game (Definition `def:symmetric-game`, and the symmetric presentation `msGameSymm`), keep the `\\lean{}` link, cite the gap note at the statement the way other chapters cite gap notes (see how `qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility` is cited near line 432), and mention the correction in the proof paragraph. Keep statement-level `\\leanok` only if the Lean statement matches the corrected statement after step 3; never add proof-level `\\leanok`.\n3. **Lean** `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems.lean`: restate `exists_ms_rigidity` over `S : SymmetricStrategy msGameSymm` (`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/StrategyClasses.lean:60-81`, `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems/Basic.lean:43-54`), with the success hypothesis on `S.toStrategy` transported along `msGameSymm_toGame`, and the witness / distance definitions (`MsRigidityWitness`, `msOperatorDistanceA/B`, `msAnticommutatorDistanceA/B`) applied to that strategy. Keep the tracked `sorry` (the proof is #105's job). No other hypothesis may be added. Update the docstrings' blueprint and paper line citations, regenerate `lean_decls` if the hooks require it, and make `python3 scripts/blueprint_lean_sync.py` and `python3 scripts/check_blueprint_latex.py` pass.\n4. Note in `audits/2026-09-04_magic-square-rigidity-orientation-obstruction.md` (one paragraph at the end) that the statement was corrected by this packet, with the note's path.\n\n## Rules\n\n- Do not change `def:ms-game` / `msGame`; the correction is on the theorem's hypotheses only.\n- Everything under `docs/paper-gaps/` must compile with the shared preamble (`\\input{command}`, `references.bib`).\n- `lake build MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test` must succeed; `lake env lean` on every changed file.\n\n## Acceptance\n\n- The note exists, passes the style checker, and states the counterexample and the correction precisely.\n- The blueprint statement is the corrected theorem and cites the note; `blueprint_lean_sync.py` is green.\n- `exists_ms_rigidity` compiles with the symmetric-strategy hypothesis and nothing else new; `#print axioms` is not required (statement-only change).\n",
